An auditable process: First save your own task cards, source ledgers, and unassisted first drafts; Request only diagnosis, without first requesting full text rewrite; Ask AI to give the basis for modification, confidence level, and possible misjudgments; Rewrite item by item yourself and record the reasons for acceptance/rejection; Check facts, quotes, links, privacy, and register; Turn off AI and complete parallel tasks under new topics; Disclose the scope of use as required by the institution, school, client, or recruitment process. Models may misrepresent acceptable variations, create sources that do not exist, smooth out individual voices, or make an inauthentic experience appear highly believable. Don’t let it create fake projects, clients, responsibilities, data, and results; don’t let it complete exams, applications, or take-home tasks for you that prohibit the use of outside help. The average results from the automated writing evaluation study may support "Tools May Help Feedback," but do not prove that any one piece of model polish improves writer ability. Acceptance is still: after closing the tool, can you explain each change and complete it in a new task.
9. Asynchronous writing keeps work going: Remote collaboration is often not supplemented by instant meetings. A usable status update could be in this order:

Email subject lines should help divert traffic, such as [Decision by 15:00 UTC], [Blocked], [FYI], but must match the true urgency of the body. Attachments, links and permissions must be verified before sending. The handover document at least states the current status, verified facts, unfinished items, failure/rollback, environment/version, responsible person and next checkpoint. Writing is not a language exercise here, but rather reduces the dependence of collaboration on the online presence of the author himself.

10. Honest titles, quotes, and bylines: Titles can have tension and should not promise something that the text cannot deliver. Quoting allows readers to return to the original position, and rewriting cannot conceal the contributions of others. When it comes to co-writing, be clear in advance who will provide the material, who will draft it, who will check it, who will approve it, and who will be responsible for the final version. Signing means: I am willing to acknowledge who these words come from, what they are based on, who they affect, and what else cannot be determined. AI, editors, and companions can participate, but ultimately the publisher cannot leave the responsibility within the tool window. I hope that I can be an honest author: allow the article to be imperfect and allow for subsequent revisions, but do not deliberately mislead readers, nor use smoothness to cover up evidence gaps.

11. Fourteen-day writing experiment: · Days · Actions · Evidence left behind · · 1 · Choose a real audience and tasks, complete a time-limited first draft · Original text, conditions, intentions and unknown items · · 2 · Establish a ledger of facts and responsibilities · Claims, sources, authority and confidence · · 3 · Mark paragraph functions and document skeleton · Structural map and deleted items · · 4 · Compare native language intention, English first version and translation · Meaning changes and reasons for decision · · 5 · Revise tasks, facts and evidence · Second version and source verification · · 6 · Revise sentences, register and voice · Before and after revisions and classification · · 7 · Give it to real readers for retelling · Purpose, questions and next steps · · 8 · Record feedback acceptance and rejection · Feedback absorption form · · 9 · Complete delivery and boundary check · Links, attachments, permissions and responsible persons · · 10 · Rewrite the same message for a different audience · Register and structure migration · · 11 · Change the topic and write the same genre · Vocabulary and content migration · 12 · Let AI/companions raise counterexamples or omissions · Verification and rejection reasons · 13 · Complete asynchronous update/handover under time pressure · Real usage results · · 14 · Close the tool to complete the parallel tasks and decide on the next round · Keep, adjust or pivot the basis · Fourteen days is not a writing crash period. It answers: Without familiarity with the original manuscript and immediate polishing, if the audience or subject matter changes, can you still complete a text that is willing to be signed and can be used?

12. How to judge that writing is becoming a competency: Ability to leave one's first draft within a time limit, rather than just a finished tool; Readers can retell purpose, basis, limitations, and next steps; Ability to distinguish facts, sources, inferences, personal experiences, and suggestions; Each paragraph has work, and beautiful sentences can be deleted without losing the main line; Ability to explain what meaning has been changed by translation or AI modification; Ability to distinguish necessary corrections, ambiguities, registers, and styles, and explain decisions; Feedback goes into new text, not just polishing old ones; Asynchronous readers can continue, decide, or roll back without relying on additional meetings; Ability to deliver similar results despite changing audiences, topics, and genres; Willingness to take responsibility for titles, citations, privacy, facts, and attribution. Sometimes the improvement of writing is not that the sentences become more and more gorgeous, but that the readers guess less and less. You know when to present the facts, when to admit the unknown, and when to delete a line that only serves your self-image. The words begin to leave the author still working, and they also begin to leave themselves behind that can be rechecked after time has passed.

Source and Boundary: Kang & Han (2015), The Efficacy of Written Corrective Feedback in Improving L2 Written Accuracy: A meta-analytic synthesis of 21 studies showing that written error correction may improve L2 writing grammatical accuracy, while the effect is affected by variables such as proficiency, environment, and genre. Vuogan & Li (2022), Examining the Effectiveness of Peer Feedback in Second Language Writing: A meta-analysis summarizes 26 studies reporting overall positive effects of peer feedback; between-source comparisons and partial moderation conclusions are limited by the number of original studies. Zhai & Ma (2022), The Effectiveness of Automated Writing Evaluation on Writing Quality: A meta-analytic synthesis of 26 studies with 2468 participants, reporting the average effectiveness of automated writing evaluation and differences in educational stage, language background, and genre; does not mean that any tool output is reliable. Writing assignments, genres, audiences, institutional rules, copyright, and acceptable AI use vary. Important texts should be referenced to current facts, primary sources, authentic readers, and clear acceptance by those responsible. Related entrances: Grammar ｜ Reading ｜ Speaking ｜ Learning English with AI ｜ English for job hunting ｜ Writing evidence card ｜ Works

Conclusion: Write a version you are willing to sign: The world is noisy enough. Writing does not have to make more noise. It can reserve a quiet place for life to look back on, and it also allows a judgment to be questioned by facts, readers and time after leaving the current emotion. The first draft records what you were able to think of at the time, and the revisions record whether you are willing to let new evidence and other people's understanding change you. The words don’t have to be perfect the first time, but each time you prepare to deliver them, you should be more honest than the last about answering: whose words they are, what they are based on, who they will affect, and what else cannot be determined. If you don’t know where to start, write a real email, a description, or a 200-word essay. Give it to a real person and listen to him retell what you said; then change it to something you are willing to sign, be willing to take responsibility for, and be willing to reopen in the future.

items.title: Learn English with AI: from practice to real delivery
items.core: Use English baseline, real materials, guided exercises, four ability feedback and delayed retest learning instead of outsourcing English ability to an AI product.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: Write the real scenario and completion standards first, and then decide the steps that AI can intervene in; Keep the four abilities without AI baseline, feedback and delayed retest respectively; Let AI ask questions, prompt and generate parallel exercises, without completing key recall and expression for you; Write the results back to the AI ​​learning record and ninety-day action list. The product functions on this page were last verified on 2026-11-23. Learning mode, project space, voice and writing tools may vary depending on region, language, device, account and package; please reopen the official page to check before use.
First define “knowing English”: Don’t start with how many words you memorize every day, write a real task first:
The goal should at least include the scenario, audience, action, completion standards, deadline and evidence location. AI can help practice and check, but it can’t define “done” for you.

1. Test the baseline first, and then let AI intervene: Do not let AI translate, rewrite or prompt for the first time. Complete four 10–15 minute tasks under the same topic: Listening: Listen to a 2–4 ​​minute piece of real material, write the main idea, three details and an uncertain point; Reading: Read a page of material, write a five-sentence summary and a counterexample; Speaking: Speak continuously for two minutes, save the original recording; Writing: Write a 120–180-word work email, without word search or AI rewriting. Score 0–2 points each for task completion, understandability, accuracy and scope, organization and fluency, and revision and transfer. Write samples, reasons for scoring, and evidence of errors into the English proficiency diagnosis. Without a baseline, there’s no way to know whether AI is helping with capabilities or simply making the finished product beautiful.

Four abilities and evidence cards: · Abilities · AI can assist · Evidence retained after turning off AI · · Listening · Give a clue, mark time periods, generate parallel questioning · First listening, six-layer error map, scaffolding ladder, meaning reconstruction and delayed transfer in the listening evidence card · · Reading · Compare paragraph marks, question evidence location, ask parallel source questions · First reading, obstacle map, claim evidence, technical facts, and inferred boundaries in Reading Evidence Cards · · Speaking · Recording difficult passages, simulated questioning · Original recordings, audience retellings, and repairs in Speaking Evidence Cards · · Writing · Hierarchically pointing out fact, structure, language, and tone issues · First draft, four rounds of revisions, and reader feedback in Writing Evidence Cards · Cards are not extra homework, but turn an exercise into a reviewable sample. If you only leave the AI's annotations and do not have your own first version and migration tasks, you will not be able to judge whether the capabilities have really changed next time. Grammar is the structural layer shared by the four abilities. AI can juxtapose original sentences with parallel sentences, propose meaning differences, and generate variations, but the feedback must distinguish errors, ambiguities, register choices, and style preferences, and explain the degree of confidence; learners then use grammar evidence cards to save their decisions. Just because the model gives a more fluent sentence does not mean that the original sentence is necessarily wrong.

2. Use the same task card for each training: After the training, only select 1–2 errors that most affect communication, and do a new parallel task. Don't copy fifteen pieces of advice into your error library and then fail to use it again.

3. Vocabulary: From familiarity to use in real tasks: Choose 5-8 high-value word chunks from real materials every week, and do not pursue isolated words. First save the first encounter without looking up the word, and then record for each word chunk: the current meaning, pronunciation, part of speech, collocation, original sentence, own sentence, a similar expression and an active recall. For unknown items, decide first to let them go, infer, quick check, active learning or professional verification. AI can generate fill-in-the-blank, error correction, and substitution exercises, but definitions, collocations, and example sentences must be returned to the learner's dictionary or real corpus for verification. The four contacts can be arranged as follows: understand the original sentence and read it aloud on the day; recall and compose sentences with closed book the next day; actively use it in spoken language or emails within a week; transfer to new scenes after two weeks. Acceptance is not about "how many have been collected", but whether it can be used correctly without prompts and let the other party understand.

4. Listening: Break down “didn’t understand”: for the first time, just write the main idea and confirm the details, without reading the subtitles. Which category does the second marking question belong to: Unrecognized vocabulary; Recognized words but did not hear consecutive pronunciation, weak pronunciation or stress; No parsing of syntactic relationships; Insufficient background knowledge; Temporary failure caused by speaking speed, accent or concentration. Let the AI ​​point out a minimal clue first and then listen back for 10–20 seconds; don’t just translate the entire paragraph. Finally, close the subtitles, retell it in your own words, and record the parts you are still unsure about. Each pass requires different problems: save the first listening without subtitles first, and then locate the time period and obstacle layer; only turn on the necessary transcription, close the text and reconstruct the theme, relationship and next step; remove it and retest it with parallel materials after three to seven days. See the hearing evidence card for complete records. AI can provide candidate transcriptions, but cannot make the final decision on the original audio and reliable sources.

5. Speaking and pronunciation: Focus on communication results: a 12-minute training session: explain a real question for 2 minutes without reading the script; let AI only record areas that are unclear, logical breaks, and areas that need clarification; select a pronunciation or word chunk question that affects understanding, and repeat it slowly 5 times; answer an unprepared follow-up question; save the original and retest recordings. Speech recognition results are only clues and do not equal natural pronunciation. The most reliable acceptance is whether a credible listener can understand it once, whether it needs to be repeated, and whether you can continue to express it in new questions. Start by choosing a reference variant that is relevant to your real audience, then gradually add other English variants; don't let the model automatically rewrite "sounds different" as "wrong." Using spoken language evidence cards to preserve device, listener familiarity, recognition errors, listener retelling, and interactive repair, differentiating accent salience, actual misunderstanding, and comprehension costs.

6. Reading: Train evidence chains instead of collecting summaries: First independently mark the author's claims, evidence, definitions, examples, and unknown items, and then let AI compare your marks. It is required to give the location of the original text, and "the general idea of ​​the article" is not accepted. Answer after closing the material: What problem does the author solve? Which conclusion relies on which piece of evidence? Are there any counterexamples? If you change the scene to your own work, which parts still hold true? Only when you can answer these questions can you move from reading to judgment.

7. Writing: Keep the author’s hand: write the first version yourself. AI only does hierarchical feedback: facts and sources, task completion, structure and logic, language errors, tone, and privacy risks. Each time, only fix the three areas that most affect your purpose, and explain in your own words why you made the changes. Don’t just accept an entire paragraph rewrite. Keep the original draft, AI suggestions, final draft, and a new similar email to compare whether you really learned it. If the final draft is good but key changes cannot be explained, the ability is not yet stable. Further use writing evidence cards to record a ledger of facts and responsibilities, changes in meaning due to translation, reasons for acceptance/rejection of each piece of feedback, automated tool versions, scope of required disclosures and parallel tasks after closing the tool. Models can be editorial assistants, not invisible authors; fluency cannot replace source, authority, attribution, and final responsibility.

8. Choose tools, but do not confuse functions: · Tasks · Available capabilities · Must check by yourself · · Guided learning · Learning mode, layered Q&A, quizzes · Whether to let you answer first, explanation whether there is a source · · Long-term context · Project space, allowed uploaded materials · Permissions, retention, memory scope and export · · Material-based learning · File Q&A, NotebookLM, etc. · Original page, copyright, privacy and whether to exceed the material · · Online research · Search tool with citations · Open the original page and confirm that it really supports the conclusion · · Writing feedback · Language models, writing tools · Keep the first draft, understand and revise item by item · · Speaking practice · Voice dialogue · Recognition accuracy does not equal natural pronunciation, functionality will change · This is not a ranking of tools. First check whether the data is allowed to be uploaded, whether the output can be exported, whether errors can be reviewed, and whether the total cost is worth it. Platform memory is just a convenience layer. Please save the goals, samples, errors and next steps in the learning status or AI learning record.

A cross-modal exercise: from understanding to speaking clearly: being able to use pictures, sounds and text at the same time will increase the entrance to the practice; with more entrances, you need to know at which step you lose understanding. The following is a teaching design that takes about 20 minutes. The time can be adjusted according to your energy, and the effect needs to be verified by yourself. Explain yourself first: Choose an English-language diagram or instruction manual that you have permission to use and no private information. Without turning on the translation, speak in English for a minute: what is it saying, which numbers or steps are most important, and where is not sure. Save the original image and original recording. Check for two types of errors separately: ask the AI ​​to point out locations in the image that support or refute your interpretation, and then check the transcription against the recording. If the decimal point in the picture is incorrectly identified or the accent is transcribed incorrectly, it will first be recorded as a tool error; if the comparative relationship is indeed misunderstood or the meaning is misspoken, it will be recorded as a learning gap. Only take one key question: choose a sentence structure or relationship that affects understanding and re-explain it. Ask the AI ​​to ask a follow-up question, answer it yourself first, and then read the feedback. Don't replace your own recording with its polished version of the entire text. Change the material and remove the help: after three to seven days, find a picture with a similar structure but different numbers, and talk again without looking at the old draft. If necessary, ask the real listener to repeat what you meant; acceptance is whether the other party understands, whether you can clarify, and whether the key facts are correct. Record the original image page number or area, recording time period, model and date. Live conversations can be used to practice interruptions, clarifications, and turn-taking, but neither an AI’s thumbs-up, recognition success, nor simulated fluency are direct evidence of real-life communication skills. If there is no recording or transcription that can be reviewed, only the actual observed phenomena will be recorded, and the precise pronunciation conclusion will not be rewritten. When choosing between voice, vision, search, or local tools, use AI trends and learning paths to make a small comparison. The richer the function, the more important it is to retain the unmodified first version: it allows progress to have a real...

9. Feedback protocol and retest: Retest on the 30th day and 12th week with the same topic, similar duration and the same restrictions. Compare the original sample, not just the AI-modified finished product. Real progress includes relying less on prompts, repeating fewer mistakes, completing real-world tasks faster, and still being usable in new situations. After each retest, write at least one result and the next variable back to the ninety-day action list, and do not let the training stop in the chat window. If you want to compare the complete changes before and after AI intervention and after migration, use the evidence chain template to save four time points; the ninety-day action list is responsible for scheduling the cycle, and the evidence chain is responsible for interpreting the results. When preparing for job interviews, you can let AI simulate recruiters, technical colleagues or customers based on public job descriptions, ask unfamiliar questions and classify errors after you submit the first version. Don’t let them fabricate stories, write applications or take-home instructions that require a signature, or use hidden prompts to answer questions during a real interview without permission. For the complete process, see the English for Job Search and English for Job Search Evidence Cards.

Ten, 7 days, 30 days, 12 weeks: 7 days: Establish a closed loop Save at least one of the four baselines; Complete three trainings with task cards; Leave original output, feedback and a parallel task each time; Record an error that most affects communication. 30 days: Establish an error library. Complete at least four real tasks of the same type; classify by vocabulary, listening comprehension, syntax, organization, pronunciation and transfer; compare the first draft and retest, do not regard AI rewriting as an increase in ability; delete tool steps that cannot improve the results. 12 weeks: Complete real English delivery Complete a meeting, presentation, email, document or cross-cultural collaboration task; Save recordings, transcripts, feedback, revisions and retests; Let the real audience confirm whether they understand, whether they need to be repeated and whether the next step is clear; Write the results back to the English proficiency diagnosis.

Privacy, Copyright & Official Sources: Do not upload clients, colleagues, students, children, medical records, documents, or undisclosed contracts directly to unapproved tools. Even if the comment or page is public, consider authorization, minimum necessary scope, and deletion period. Copyrighted material will only be processed within the scope of the authorized use, and records of sources and permissions will be maintained. OpenAI: Introduction to learning mode; Projects in ChatGPT Google: Use learning tools in the Gemini app; create quizzes, flashcards, etc.; Gemini Live Anthropic: What are projects? (Free account can be created, up to five projects; enhanced knowledge retrieval requires paid plan) Google: NotebookLM Perplexity: Help Center DeepL: DeepL Write These pages are only re-verifiable product entrances, not a current feature list, nor do they constitute a tool ranking or performance guarantee. The last centralized verification date of the product entrance is 2026-11-23; please re-verify the functions, regions and packages before use.

Conclusion: After the tool leaves the scene: AI can quickly give fluent sentences, patient explanations and seemingly complete answers. But English skills don’t live in the chat window. It lives after the tool is closed, whether you can still understand the key meaning, whether you can explain it in your own words, and whether you can continue to think when others ask. Let AI help you see blind spots, generate exercises and provide feedback, then schedule it out. Every departure is like a small ebb: the part held by the tool will be exposed, and the part that really belongs to you will remain. If the meaning disappears along with the window, the exercise is not complete. The goal is not to train yourself to be more like a model, but to develop your own voice within a limited vocabulary, real hesitations, and necessary judgments. When the tool leaves, you still know what you want to say and are willing to take responsibility for what you say. AI is amplifying capabilities rather than occupying it for you.

items.title: 8. English for Job Search: Bringing Ability into Interviews and Remote Collaboration
items.core: Instead of replacing job analysis with a CEFR tag, break down overseas and remote job search into recruitment communication, project description, technical questioning, behavioral issues, asynchronous writing and misunderstanding repair, and use fourteen days of evidence to determine the next step.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: First break down job language tasks, and then judge the current CEFR direction, without replacing job evidence with an average grade; Distinguish recruitment screening, project descriptions, technical interviews, behavioral questions, asynchronous writing and remote collaboration; First save a baseline without drafts and without AI, and then train high-frequency stories, word chunks, clarifications and time management; Check communication with "Can the other party repeat and continue to ask" instead of just counting grammar and accent; AI You can simulate interviews, classify errors, and generate parallel questions, but you cannot fabricate experiences, ghostwrite submissions, or answer secretly when prohibited; fourteen days is enough to judge the next variable, but not enough to guarantee an offer or reach a certain permanent level.

1. "English required" is not a task: English required on the same job page may correspond to completely different language responsibilities: · Scenario · Actual task · Minimum completion evidence · · Written application · Resume, application form, short email and time zone/salary confirmation etc. · Recruiters can find matching experience, restrictions and next steps · · Recruitment screening · Explain motivation, available time, job matching and basic experience · Five to ten minutes Q&A does not rely on sentence-by-sentence manuscripts · · Project description · Explain the background, goals, your responsibilities, difficulties, decisions and results · The audience can retell the main line and point out your specific contribution · · Technical questioning · Understand the problem, expose assumptions, compare solutions, admit the unknown · Be able to clarify while thinking, without filling the silence with guessing · · Behavioral issues · Use specific events to illustrate conflict, failure, cooperation, feedback and change · Facts, your actions, impact and reflection are separated from each other · · Asynchronous collaboration · Write about progress, risks, blockers, decisions and handovers · Colleagues know what happened and who is responsible without the need for a meeting · Meeting fixes · Ask for repetition when you don’t understand, confirm terminology, summarize consensus · Misunderstandings are discovered, restated and confirmed · Start by flagging which tasks actually exist from job descriptions, hiring processes and team disclosure materials. In a position that mainly relies on asynchronous document collaboration, writing and handover may be more important than chatting; in a customer communication position, listening to needs, asking questions, and repairing misunderstandings may be more important than a prepared self-introduction. Don’t spend all your time imitating pronunciation just because of the word “spoken”.

2. CEFR is a coordinate, not an admission line: CEFR describes what can be accomplished in different complexities and situations. For many interview tasks in familiar areas, the B1 direction may support coherent explanations of experiences and reasons; the B2 direction is closer to explaining professional issues, participating in discussions, and defending opinions; more complex negotiations, management, and high-stakes communications may require a more flexible language range. This is not an admissions score, for at least four reasons: The reading, listening, speaking and writing of the same person may vary greatly; Familiar professional fields will provide knowledge scaffolding, and unfamiliar topics will magnify the gap; Interview performance is also affected by task understanding, pressure, cultural context, equipment and the recruiter's expression; Companies evaluate the overall evidence of job match, not just a language level. So instead of asking “Am I a B2?” complete the job baseline: Describe a real project in two minutes; Answer two unseen follow-up questions; Listen to a natural-paced question related to the position and repeat it; Write a recruiting follow-up email or an asynchronous project update in twenty minutes. Write the results in the job search English evidence card. Levels only help choose difficulty, samples help decide on the next workout.

3. Extract the language map from the job description: Don’t end it by translating the entire job description. Use three columns to build a language map: · Job facts · Language actions that need to be completed · Your existing evidence · · Work across product and engineering · Describe cross-team differences, trade-offs, and handovers · A collaborative case recording or project review · · Write clear technical proposals · Write background, options, risks, suggestions, and items to be confirmed · One page of English design instructions · · Communicate with customers · Listen to requirements, ask for constraints, and confirm next steps · Five rounds of role dialogue with audience retelling · · operate in an async remote team · Write progress, blocking, decisions, owners and time zone boundaries · An asynchronous status update · Mark each language action:

The purpose of the position language map is not to prepare you for all possible questions, but to find locations where "professional capabilities already exist, but English makes the evidence inaccessible".

4. Save the complete baseline first: Do not divide the baseline into fifty questions. Choose a real job description and complete it within forty-five minutes: Two-minute self-introduction: only talk about the present, evidence and direction related to the position; Five-minute project description: background, tasks, your actions, key trade-offs, results and unknowns; Three unfamiliar questions: asked by peers, teachers or AI after listening; An asynchronous update: limited to 120–180 words, describing progress, risks and next steps; One-time fix: Deliberately add a question that you didn’t hear clearly or won’t answer temporarily, and practice clarifying and delaying the answer. Recording conditions: preparation time, whether to read the manuscript, whether to use subtitles/dictionaries/AI, whether questions appear in advance, recording and text position. The most important thing about the baseline is not the total score, but the failure type: · Failure type · Performance · Next training · · Content gap · Contribution and results cannot be explained clearly in Chinese · Reconstruct the project evidence first, without practicing English sentences first · · Retrieval gap · Know the content, but cannot find the word chunks on the spot · High-frequency blocks, timed recall and variant questioning · · Listening gap · Key words are heard, but the relationship between the questions is not heard clearly · Question restatement, emphasis boundaries and clarification requests · · Organizational gaps · Lots of details, unclear main line and conclusion · Conclusion first, timeline and trade-off structure · · Interaction gaps · Silence or guessing when stuck · Requests for repetition, confirmation of assumptions, and buying time for thinking · · Accuracy gaps · Errors continue to change meaning · Only fix high-frequency errors that affect understanding · If content gaps dominate, brushing more oral materials will not directly solve the problem. First write down your real experience clearly.

5. Prepare stories, don’t memorize answers: Interview preparation requires a story bank, but the story bank is not a verbatim draft. Choose four to six real events, covering: a problem you actually solved; a failure, misjudgment, or rework; a collaboration with someone who disagreed; a decision made when there was insufficient information; a change of approach after receiving feedback; a work you chose to stop, demote, or hand over. Save only six lines for each story:

STAR (Situation, Task, Action, Result) can help organize, but it cannot suppress complex experiences into false victories. A bad outcome can still be a qualified story, as long as the facts, responsibility and learning are clear. As you practice, change one condition at a time: question wording, response time, audience, story entry, or follow-up question. If only fixed issues can trigger fixed manuscripts, it is not ready to be migrated yet.

6. Conclusion first, details later: remote interviews are often affected by delays, accents, equipment, and time constraints. The more complex the answer, the more important it is to give the other party a main line that they can grasp. Accent differences alone are not evidence of interview failure. Use spoken evidence cards to save equipment, listener retellings, locations that need to be relistened to, and interactive repairs; if the other party can grasp the conclusion, evidence, and next steps, don’t sacrifice preparation time to imitate a single accent. A practical sequence is: A conclusion: directly answering the question; Two or three pivots: context, action, or reason; A concrete example: keep only the details that support the judgment; A boundary: result, unknown, or still needs to be confirmed; Return to the conversation: confirm whether deeper technical details are needed. For example: The main reason we changed the design was reliability. The old path depended on one service and failed badly under partial outages. I proposed a fallback, added failure tests, and documented when to degrade. It reduced incident recovery time in our tests, although we still needed production data. I can go deeper into the trade-off if useful. The value of this paragraph is not in the advanced vocabulary, but in...

7. Interactive repair is an interview skill, not a point-losing move: when you have not heard clearly, need to think, or are not sure about the boundaries of the question, continuing to guess is often more dangerous than asking for clarification. Didn't hear clearly
Not sure about the scope of the question
Needs time to think
Don't know yet
Confirm understanding
Repair actions to keep the conversation real. It also shows teams how you can expose unknowns when collaborating remotely, rather than masking risks with a confident tone.

8. Remote positions are still testing writing: Remote collaboration doesn’t just happen in video conferencing. The hiring process and daily work often requires: Confirming interview times, time zones, and equipment; Filling in missing information after meetings; Writing project status, blockers, and decisions; Explaining scope, assumptions, tests, and unfinished items in take-home tasks; Handing off work to colleagues in another time zone to continue. A reliable asynchronous update can be used:

Write the first version in twenty minutes without letting AI write for you. Readers are asked to answer only: what happened, what needed to be decided, and who continued when. If the other person has to meet again to understand, the writing has not completed the asynchronous task. This type of text should retain its original draft, sources of facts, boundaries of AI use, and reasons for revisions. Use the writing evidence card to check the subject line, conclusion, evidence location, risks, responsible persons, non-response handling and rollback; a beautiful application or handover that relies on fictional experience, invisible ghostwriting or unexplained changes by the author will not be authoritative.

9. AI can simulate, but cannot gain integrity for you: AI is suitable for: Extracting language tasks and professional word chunks from job descriptions; Asking follow-up questions with different wordings after you submit the first version; Classifying content, organization, retrieval, listening and interactive questions based on the transcription of recordings; Generating parallel interviews that are similar but not repeated; Simulating different roles: recruiter, technical colleagues, products or customers. AI is not suitable for: Fictitious projects, responsibilities, data, clients or results; Hidden intervention after writing your final resume, application answers or take-home instructions; Answering for you through a second device or hidden prompts during a live interview, especially without permission; Uploading confidential recruiter materials, company code, customer information or third-party private data; Using a model score to declare you "suitable" or "unsuitable" for a career. After the exercise, turn off the AI ​​and redo it with a new problem. Evidence of ability comes from your ability to continue answering and fixing, not from the encouragement given by the simulator.

10. Fourteen-day job sprint: Fourteen days cannot rebuild all English, but it is enough to shift training from general learning to job-based evidence: · Number of days · Core actions · Evidence · 1 · Choose a real position and complete the complete baseline · Recording, asynchronous update, error map · 2–3 · Establish a job language map and four to six stories · Language action list and story cards · 4–5 · Training project description and conclusion first · Two versions of different lengths · · 6 · Practice unfamiliar questioning and repair sentences · Five rounds of Q&A recordings · · 7 · Complete delayed retesting without looking at old answers · Parallel question results · · 8–9 · Training technology or job-specific questions · Assumptions, trade-offs, unknowns and verification steps · · 10 · Write an asynchronous update and follow-up email · Readers retell the results · · 11 · Complete a 25–40-minute simulation · Full recording and stage scoring · · 12 · Only answer the three questions that most affect the results · Revision and reasons for rejection · · 13 · Change the interviewer or the order of questions · Migrate samples · · 14 · Close the tool to complete the final simulation · Decision to stay and the next variable · If it is closer to the real interview, compress the content and do not extend the late-night training. Prioritize sleep, equipment testing, job facts, and the most common language tasks.

11. Use stage thresholds to determine “whether it’s enough”: Don’t use “it feels smooth” to decide whether to deliver. Set the threshold for the current position: · Threshold · Observable conditions · · Content · Can explain at least three real projects or events, no fictitious contributions · · Tasks · Able to complete recruitment screening, project descriptions, unfamiliar questioning and an asynchronous writing · · Understand · Can retell most questions; will actively confirm when not heard clearly · · Expression · The main idea arrives first, errors do not continue to change the key meaning · · Interaction · Able to buy time to think, acknowledge the unknown, clarify and summarize · · Transfer · Ability to recall stories and structures despite changes in questioning method, audience, and order · · Boundaries · Know which materials cannot be uploaded, and which AI uses need to be disclosed or prohibited · The threshold does not need to be full marks. It helps you decide: submit immediately and continue practicing, fill a high-risk gap first, or whether the language and responsibilities of the position are temporarily beyond your current capabilities. The submission itself can generate feedback, but don't attribute a rejection entirely to English. Job fit, experience, hiring window, salary, region, visa, time zone and candidate pool all affect the results.
12. Close your account after the interview: After every real or simulated interview, before the memory changes, write:

If the recruiter provides feedback, keep the original words and do not over-interpret a polite refusal into a conclusion about ability. Without feedback, the review can only be based on recordings, notes and observable results.

Source and Boundary: Council of Europe: CEFR 3.3 Global Scale. This chapter only uses level as a language task coordinate and does not write it as a unified recruitment line for any company. Job process, AI use, recording, confidentiality, identity, region and job qualification rules vary by company and region and should be subject to current recruitment instructions, formal agreements and applicable requirements. Related entrances: CEFR Objectives and Self-Assessment ｜ Speaking Chapter ｜ Writing Chapter ｜ Writing Evidence Card ｜ Job Hunting English Evidence Card

Conclusion: Let your ability reach that real conversation: Interviews are stressful, not just because of the language. It compresses the past few years into dozens of minutes and requires you to quickly find facts, values ​​and directions in strangers' questions. It’s easy to pursue a performance without pauses, mistakes, or accents, as if we can’t be rejected if we’re fluent enough. But what a team really needs is usually not a perfect monologue, but someone who can understand the problem, explain the evidence, expose the unknown, repair misunderstandings, and hand over the work to others. English allows these abilities to be heard in another language, but it does not create non-existent experiences for you, nor does it eliminate all chance from recruitment results. You don’t have to wait until you feel like you’re “finally good enough” to leave your first sample. Choose a real position, talk about your project, let unfamiliar questions interrupt the prepared sequence, and then see which part still belongs to you. I hope that when you walk into your next interview, you will not only know the answers by heart, but also have the courage to stop and think. I hope your sentences don’t have to be gorgeous, but they can allow the other person to see what you have done, how you make judgments, and how you work with others to get things done. At that time, language is no longer a test that blocks opportunities, but a bridge that allows abilities to reach real relationships.

items.title: Part 1: Put yourself back into life
items.core: Put failure, body, relationship, career and choice back into the same period of life, and find a way to continue between facts, responsibilities, cherishing and sharing.
body: The question this department wants to answer: How to tell personal experiences without pouring back the results of what you learned later? How do you own your own mistakes without justifying transgressions, violence, or the choices of others? When a career, relationship, or body is out of order, what should be stopped first, what needs help, and what can continue in a small way? In the midst of uncertainty, how do you leave boundaries for decisions, dates for review, and ways back? How to turn care into willing care and sharing by both parties, and let care bring strength, instead of turning love into a liability or a reason to hold on? There is no unified answer to these questions. Different people have different physical, financial, responsibilities and security conditions. What this section provides is a method for reading the past, and it does not require everyone to reach the same conclusion.

Reading path: · Path · Chapter · Things to see · · Entering the scene · My story · Facts, costs, absentees and the unknown in an experience · · Re-understanding the body and emotions · I am still here · Depression, anxiety, risk of withdrawal, small actions in seeking help and recovery · · Catch yourself first · Recovery · Safety, basic care, support network and minimal order · · Reread the story · Narrative and evidence · Echo · The current version, retrospective interpretation and next testable action · · Re-selection · Choice · Reversibility, cost, impact and review conditions · · Let each other be heard · Communication · Relationship · Observation, feelings, needs, requests, boundaries and repair · · Cherish and share · Cherish · Specific care, care work, mutual capacity, rejection space and the load that can be relieved · · Facing your career · Entrepreneurship · Users, cash flow, technical debt, team responsibilities, and stopping thresholds · When reading personal stories, please allow yourself to pause. If the content triggers persistent insomnia, panic, despair or dangerous thoughts, leave the page first and contact a trusted person and local qualified professional support. A review isn't worth hurting yourself again.

What will you leave after reading: When this book ends, please don’t just leave a sentence of “I am relieved” or “I should work harder”. Leave a page of record that can be reviewed in the future: Three identifiable facts, and what remains unknown; One responsibility to take on, apologize for, stop, or repair; One boundary to protect your body, relationship, or money; One minimal action that doesn’t rely on a grand twist. When it comes to caregiving or shared burdens, it can also leave a concrete arrangement that both parties agree on: who will bear what, what will require additional support, and when it will be checked whether it is too much. Save it with the Life Advancement Worksheet. Records should be kept in a private location and unnecessary third-party identity, health, financial and relationship details removed.

Enter the text: We cannot go back in time and make new choices for ourselves at that time, but we can decide how to understand him today. Don’t rush to find lessons yet. Let the story fall with its original weight and hear the ambition, the silence, the pain, the desire that remains.

items.title: My Story: Failure, Recovery and Restart
items.core: A personal record about career ups and downs, entrepreneurial failure, physical and life disorder, and rediscovering the courage to act after returning home to recover.
body: Narrative boundary: This is a memory written from my personal position and is not the common version of all parties involved. Partners, associates and friends are described using pseudonyms or generalities; children and other third parties are kept only in detail necessary to understand the events. The dates, amounts, and physical experiences come from my memory and records, and there may still be errors; emotional judgments are not equivalent to factual judgments about others. Photos and stories involving others are only retained with the necessary consent and respect for deletion requests. If you want to use this memory as a study material, you can first read the chapter on narrative and evidence: Don’t write down your experience as fate, and then come back to see which are the facts, which are my interpretations, and which conclusions still need to be retained.

How do I face the costs after a company goes bankrupt: Hello friends, I am outrageous. Today I want to tell you an unseemly Internet entrepreneurial experience as honestly as possible. On April 1, 2017, I joined Nanjing xx Technology Co., Ltd. as a general front-end developer and began to develop a software for lawyers/law firms. At that time, the first version of the software was made by an outsourcing company. The code had no comments and no project management. It was a mess. To make matters worse, the company had no product manager at the time, and all ideas came from the boss. One month after joining the company, the timeline module I was responsible for had been modified for more than 20 versions. Such high frequency of modification requirements really made me nervous. Fortunately, a month later, the first version was tested, and the results were basically in line with the boss’s expectations. After that, I led the reconstruction of the front-end project using Vue as the technology stack. After more than half a year of hard work, it was finally released. Sales started at this time. We originally thought that at least there would be a little noise in the industry, but the result was hugely disappointing. There was no order at all for a long time. Company environment: Due to the company's unsatisfactory development, everyone's salary did not increase with the length of service, and many colleagues left one after another with disappointment. Seeing the people who used to talk and laugh leave one by one, I felt very uncomfortable. I was optimistic about this product from the beginning. Even though the membership changed from round to round and my salary did not increase in the past few years, I still chose to stay. In this way, I became the only person who stayed in the company. I also went from an ordinary employee to a department leader, then to the general manager of the company, and gradually moved towards the role of partner. The outrageous story begins here. Looking back on those days later, I found that the so-called "concentrating on career" was never a story about one person. Love and family were always present. Love Thank God for my...

I am still here, and I am still learning: Many people care about how I am now, I am still here, and I am fine. Supplementary note: The limited text in this article mainly records the conflicts between myself and my partner Mr. Gong (pseudonym) in the later stages of the company, which easily makes him look like a single opposite. That's just my perspective, not a complete judgment on him; he also has many qualities worthy of recognition. Open narratives should leave room for others to not be fully defined by my version of myself.

Back to the table: Later, as the chairman of China Ciyuan Cloud Computing Co., Ltd., I was invited by Hangzhou Alibaba to visit the Alibaba Cloud Hangzhou headquarters. Visiting Alibaba Cloud’s Hangzhou Headquarters This visit made me more willing to believe that AI should not just remain a concept, nor should it be just a tool in the hands of a few people. I want it to make its way into industry, land, and ordinary people’s lives when it’s empowered, accountable, and authentically proven. Understanding the Qianwen Big Model Next, I hope to continue to explore specific paths for AI to empower agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry, fishery and other real industries to support the development of the real economy. Especially in the direction of rural cooperatives, I also plan to provide free AI training so that more ordinary people can truly understand and use AI, use technology to improve production efficiency, and broaden business ideas. Seeking benefits for the people and doing practical things is not a slogan. After experiencing the trough, I increasingly believe that the most practical meaning of moving forward is to turn my ability to stand up again into something useful to others.

Conclusion: A restart is not a triumph: I don’t want to write 2026 as a victory over 2022. A visit, a title and a new direction cannot pay for the past, nor can they prove that the future has been fulfilled. They only mean that I have the strength to go to the table, face a question, and be willing to let reality answer it. The starting point is not to go back to the person who believes that he can solve everything. It is to continue living with another kind of memory: knowing that the company will fail, the body will keep accounts, relationships will be bruised by choices, and the silence of family members will not disappear automatically because of subsequent success. After knowing this, I am still willing to do things, but I no longer bet everyone’s future on my own beliefs. As of this writing of this story, there is no triumph, no complete reconciliation. I’m still learning how to take responsibility, how to repair, how to make new work without repeating old hurts. The so-called starting over may just mean seeing the cost earlier than in the past, being more willing to ask for help, and leaving a way back for yourself and others when you have to stop.

items.title: I'm Still Here: Coming Out of the Darkness of Depression and Anxiety
items.core: Han Xiankai's personal account of depression, anxiety, early forcible withdrawal from psychotropic drugs, and getting back to life with family, professional support, and many small actions.
body: Narrative Boundary: I wrote this chapter after my story because the previous chapter recorded how things happened, and this chapter records how things entered my body, emotions, and relationships. It's still just my perspective and not a complete judgment on anyone. The sections involving family, partners, children, and friends have been kept with only the details necessary to understand my experience. I am not a clinical professional and am not diagnosing myself or my readers based on a memory. This chapter does not provide drug names, dosages, tapering days, alternatives, or crisis diagnoses. The initiation, adjustment, reduction and discontinuation of any medication should be evaluated on an individual basis by the prescribing physician or other qualified professional. Personal experience can help us speak, but it cannot replace professional judgment.

Heiwu is not just a "want to be more enlightened": before the company went bankrupt, I believed that all problems could be solved by working longer hours. If there is a problem with the project, I will make a few more revisions; if there is a cash flow problem, I will find another way; if the team is about to break up, I will talk about the future again. In those years, I regarded persistence as a kind of morality and understood stopping as betrayal. In 2022, the company's sales dropped significantly, and problems with structure, products, and cash flow surfaced. Managing conflict turns the office into a room that is constantly tightening. Starting in June, I first had stomach problems, and later developed erosive gastritis, insomnia, blurred vision, loss of appetite, and wandering pain. My body kept sending signals, but I translated them into one sentence: I'm just not strong enough. One night, I said to Ruohan, "I may be dying," and then I started talking nonsense and explaining my funeral arrangements. She cried and the child woke up. There was no movie-like twist that night. There was only a family that was awakened by fear and waited for me to slowly calm down. In the next few months, I queued up at the hospital, took X-rays, had blood tests, waited for the results, and then asked the doctor about the results. Doctors told me again and again that there was no serious disease that could explain all my feelings, but my body didn't believe them. I searched for symptoms online, telling myself it was fine while continuing to look for answers that had yet to be checked out. Anxiety amplifies every small signal and translates every "nothing" into "it hasn't been found yet." Depression makes life lose its color. It’s not that I cry every day, but I have to go through a thick layer of air before eating, going out, or replying to messages. I gradually became reluctant to talk, see people, and open GitHub. In the end, even the work I was most familiar with felt like someone else’s life. It’s not that I don’t know what I should do, it’s that I can’t find the strength to turn “should” into action.

I used to think of going off medication as taking back control: early on, I experienced depression and anxiety, and was forced off psychotropic medication without adequate professional support. At that time, I understood stopping medication as taking back my dignity and control: as long as I relied on my will to push through it, I could prove that I was not knocked down and that I didn’t have to admit that I needed help. Looking back now, that was not bravery, but a dangerous decision made by a person whose judgment had been narrowed by fear and shame. Stopping the medication did not remove the problem from my life, it just deprived me of a support that could have been professionally assessed. The physical and mood swings became harder to discern after that, and I mistook "not continuing to take" for "the cause had been addressed." I don’t write about this experience as a template for withdrawal, nor do I write about medications as a one-size-fits-all answer. It only illustrates one very specific thing: when people are in darkness, it is easy to turn complex medical decisions into a moral test - whether I can endure it or not determines whether I am strong; whether I need treatment determines whether I have failed. Such binary choices continue to hurt people. If you are considering starting, adjusting, tapering, or discontinuing a psychotropic medication, please bring your questions, fears, and side effects to your prescribing physician or qualified professional for evaluation. Don't extrapolate your regimen from my experience, and don't stop suddenly without support. The name of the medication, dosage, and procedure are not included here because they should not be copied from a personal narrative.

There is no morning when I “figure it out” in the deepest part: In 2023, I transferred the last restaurant and returned to my hometown with my three-year-old son. Leaving the city where I have lived for more than ten years should have been a new beginning, but at that time I was just escaping from the days that I could no longer bear. After returning home, I became silent. My mother calls me to eat on WeChat every day; without this reminder, I might not even eat on time. As someone who is almost thirty years old, I still have to wait for my mother to remind me to eat. This makes me feel ashamed, and it also makes me unable to pretend for the first time that I am just temporarily tired. I really need help. I put my desktop back together and played games day and night. The game started out like a room you could hide in, but eventually even that room became boring. I lost my boundaries day and night, made no money, quarreled with my partner over the future, and broke up with my friends over money issues. I quit many groups, closed GitHub, blocked contacts, and deleted myself bit by bit from my original world. On her son's birthday, Ruohan asked if he wanted to go out for hot pot in the evening. I hesitated for a long time and said I could just buy a small cake and enjoy it at home. Later we went to Haidilao, but we didn’t order many dishes. When the waiter sang "Say Goodbye to All Troubles," I suddenly couldn't hold it any longer. Troubles are not easy to say goodbye to, and the grievances my family endured because of my choices will not disappear automatically just because I have worked hard. It wasn't a pretty awakening. It is more like a mirror, allowing me to see that I have compressed "living" into not letting others down, but I have not really taken care of myself, nor have I taken full responsibility for the impact I have on others.

Getting out is not a personal victory: I did not get out of the darkness with one decision. The first change that occurred was that I no longer viewed asking for help as a judgment on my character. I began to acknowledge that there were some issues that needed a doctor's evaluation, some nights that needed family nearby, some commitments that needed to be put on hold, and some relationships that needed to be apologized rather than explained. Nor does asking for help turn a person into my therapist or savior. I learned to say specific words: "Please remind me to eat" "Please accompany me to the hospital" "I am not in a good condition today and may be slow to reply" "I cannot agree to this now. I will give you a confirmed time after I review it." Specific requests let others know how to approach and allow me to retain choice in how I help. A more complete approach has been written in the recovery chapter: first confirm safety, then reduce the load, and finally use short-term, revocable tasks to gradually rebuild. For me, the most important thing is not to schedule every day to be full, but to stop overdrafting: eat and sleep first, suspend high-risk decisions, retain necessary contacts, and reduce "fix your life today" to "complete an action today that will not harm tomorrow." I also started splitting up responsibilities. The failure of the company is a fact, and the losses and the impact on colleagues are the responsibility; "My whole life is ruined" is a sentence made of shame. Physical disorders are real and require professional evaluation; "I just have to tolerate it a little longer and it will fix it" is an old fantasy. By separating facts, explanations and responsibilities, life regains manageable boundaries.

How I understand "coming out of the darkness" now: I no longer understand coming out as no longer depressed or anxious, nor do I regard a visit, a title, or a new job as a victory in the past. Those things only mean that I have some strength to return to the table and am willing to let reality answer the questions. For me, coming out is the quiet ability to: detect changes in sleep, appetite, body aches, and concentration earlier; stop using sudden withdrawals to prove my independence; talk to a trusted person before silence turns a problem into a crisis; be able to accept professional support and make it clear to friends and family what can and cannot be done; None of these changes were spectacular, but they gave me options again. The darkness did not give me a nobler personality. It only exposed that I once regarded patience as health, productivity as value, and concealment as strength. Recovery is about slowly separating these things and learning how to get along with yourself.

Written to those who are still in the dark: If you see yourself here, you don’t have to prove that the pain is severe enough to qualify for help. You can just say: "I can't function normally lately" "I'm afraid of my own thoughts" "I'm not good at being alone". If it's incomplete, send these few sentences to a trusted person and ask them to connect you with appropriate professional support. Please do not copy my early decision to forcibly stop medication, and do not use my experience to judge your treatment. Medications, psychotherapy, medical attention and crisis support all need to be attended by qualified professionals based on your situation. If you have definite plans to harm yourself or others, immediately stay away from objects that may cause harm, do not be alone, and contact people around you and local emergency or crisis services. The next step can be small: drink some water, eat a meal, open a window, send a message to a person, schedule an appointment for an assessment, or start by reducing the number of things that must be done today to just one. Small doesn't mean unimportant. Small means it has a chance of actually happening.

Source and Boundary: Recovery: Catch yourself first: a practical framework for safety, load reduction, specific help, and gradual resumption of work. Narrative and Evidence: Don’t write your experience into destiny: Separate the facts, explanations, responsibility, and what remains unknown. This chapter does not provide diagnoses, medication plans, withdrawal programs, or local crisis hotline numbers. Please contact qualified professionals and emergency services depending on your area.

Conclusion: I'm still here: I once thought that walking out of the darkness meant returning to the self that could solve everything. Now I am more willing to admit that I will not go back to the past, nor do I need to go back. I can continue to live with those failures, debts, physical memories, and evidence of the help I received. I didn’t come out of this in one moment. It was during many ordinary days that I learned not to leave myself to the darkness alone: ​​to ask for help when needed, to make clear what I could bear and what I could not bear; to take only one step today and leave tomorrow to tomorrow. My name is Han Xiankai. I’ve experienced depression, anxiety, insomnia, shame and powerlessness, and made decisions that put me at extra risk. I haven’t become a better person as a result, but I’m still learning how to take care of myself, repair relationships, work hard, and give life back to myself. I'm still here. Not a triumph, but a continuation.

items.title: Recovery: Catch yourself first
items.core: After failure, insomnia, relationship changes or long-term disorder, first distinguish between safety and capacity, restore the body, support, boundaries and mobility, and then use clear thresholds to gradually return to work.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: Confirm safety first, then discuss efficiency and the future; Choose safety mode, downshift mode or reconstruction mode based on safety, basic care and mobility, and do not decide the load based on shame; Treat the body as a part of life, not a tool to achieve goals; Split shame into facts, explanations and responsibilities, and avoid covering the entire reality with "I failed"; Ask for help in a specific way, support must have boundaries, and apologies should not be conditional on the forgiveness of the other party; The resumption of work must first pass safety, basic life, tasks, boundaries and review thresholds, and then gradually increase the load; use seven days to restore minimum order, and then use the ninety-day action chapter to establish a long-term rhythm.

1. Make sure it’s safe first: When a person suffers from long-term insomnia, despair, pain, or is weighed down by debt, his or her judgment will narrow. The most important thing at this time is not to prove that you are strong, but to temporarily remove irreversible risks. You can do four small things first: Tell a trusted person: "I am in an unsafe situation recently, and I need you to deal with it with me." Pause high-risk decisions: large loans, impulsive resignation, dangerous driving, complete disconnection or plans to harm yourself; Leave drugs, knives, ropes, weapons or other items that may cause harm to a trusted person for safekeeping; Contact local emergency services, hospitals, psychological crisis intervention or other qualified professional support. If you have definite plans to harm yourself or others, don't be alone and don't pin your hopes on the next chat. Please contact someone close to you and local emergency services immediately. Asking for help is not about losing control of your life, but about giving control to a more reliable support network when you need it most.

2. Choose today’s recovery mode first: Two misjudgments are most likely to occur during the recovery phase: as long as you can still reply to messages, you think you should resume all your work; as long as you do less today, you think you are regressing. A more reliable approach is to choose a model based on the reality of what you can afford today, rather than deciding the load based on shame. · Mode · Applicable signals · Today’s tasks · · Safety mode · There is a harm plan, basic safety cannot be guaranteed, serious disorder or real threats are expanding · Do not be alone, contact support and local emergency or professional services, and remove irreversible risks · · Downshift mode · There is no immediate danger, but sleep, eating, pain, panic, debt or care pressure significantly affect the function · Protect basic life, suspend high-risk decisions, retain only necessary communication and a minimum action · · Rebuild mode · Basic safety is relatively stable, capable of completing simple care and short tasks, and support and review are still in place · Use short-term, reversible tasks to test load, record the next day's cost, and do not immediately restore the full load · These three modes are not diagnostics, nor are they levels. A person can be in rebuilding mode in the morning and back to safe mode in the evening due to new risks; or they can switch back and forth over the course of weeks. Pattern changes are not failures, but new facts entering the plan. Answer only four questions at a time: Can you keep yourself and others basically safe today? Can you complete your meals, necessary medications or care, sleep preparations, and key communications today? Will a 10–20 minute task help restore order, or will it continue to widen the overdraft? If my condition worsens, who do I contact, what do I stop, and where do I go for support? If you can’t answer the first question affirmatively, stop evaluating productivity and enter safe mode. If persistent symptoms or functional changes prevent you from identifying patterns, see a qualified local doctor...

3. Recover your body first, don’t punish yourself with discipline: The body in depression often sends signals before words can: loss of appetite, fragmented sleep, blurred vision, rapid heartbeat, and wandering pain. Don't suppress these signals with "I'm overthinking", and don't draw your own conclusions based on similar symptoms online. A more reliable recovery sequence is: Seek medical treatment: Refer persistent or recurring symptoms to a qualified medical professional for evaluation; Sleep: Fix the time to get up first, reduce compensation for staying up late, and do not regard the quality of one night as a personality score; Diet: Start with acceptable simple foods, regularity is more important than perfection; Activity: Go out for a short walk every day, and the amount of activity will not be significantly worse the next day; Record: Write down the time, symptoms, triggers and methods that have been tried, and go to seek help with the record. Recovering your body does not mean developing a more rigorous self-discipline plan. You don't need to charge yourself interest when you're already overdrawn.

4. Restore shame to facts: After failure, it is easy for us to compress a series of facts into a sentence: I am useless, I am ruined, and I do not deserve to start again. This statement sounds like honesty, but doesn't actually offer anything to deal with. Try writing three columns: · Facts · My explanation · Responsibility I am willing to assume · · The project did not receive continuous orders · I mistook the number of features for user value · Next time, do the willingness to pay and delivery cost verification · · I have not slept well for several weeks · I am worried that I will lose everything if I stop · Make an appointment for a professional assessment and tell my family the true status · · A relationship has ended · I understand loss as never being loved · Respect each other's boundaries and sort out my own behavior patterns · Facts give the problem boundaries, explanations allow us to see deviations, and responsibilities make the next step concrete. All three are indispensable.

5. Relationships need apologies and boundaries: People in troughs often feel indebted and lonely at the same time. You may want to draw everyone back, explain every decision, and demand that they understand your difficulties. But the other party has the right not to accept the explanation, and also has the right to leave temporarily. A responsible apology includes at least four things: State clearly what happened, without using "if you feel hurt" to avoid the facts; Acknowledge the impact you have caused, and do not attribute all the stress to the environment; Explain how you are prepared to make amends, rather than just expressing pain; Do not regard the other person's forgiveness as a prerequisite for your recovery. An apology is not a long letter that forces the other person to reply. Many times, a brief, specific statement that allows the other person to keep their distance is more respectful of the relationship than repeated talk. At the same time, you also need boundaries: don’t accept humiliation, don’t argue endlessly late at night, and don’t take on all responsibilities that don’t belong to you just to prove that you are wrong. Recovery is not about surrendering yourself to whoever is the loudest judge.

6. Bring work back to an affordable level: For many people, work is not only income, but also dignity and order. But during the recovery phase, work should not continue to serve as a tool of punishment. Narrow the task down to a savable outcome: Organize a page of information instead of "re-planning your career"; Fix a test instead of "rewrite the entire system"; Write three sentences instead of "write a masterpiece"; Reply to an important email instead of "resolve all relationships"; Walk for ten minutes instead of "immediately return to the previous status quo". Every small result must leave evidence: documents, recordings, submission records, feedback or next steps. The evidence is not to show off to others, but to allow you to still see what you have done when your emotions sink again.

7. Returning to work is not an on-off switch, but a step-by-step test run: After regaining a little strength, it is easy for people to rush to prove "I am fine". So you accomplish a lot one day, lose functionality again the next day, and then interpret the repetition as weakness of will. The resumption of work is more like giving a bridge under repair a step-by-step test load: first let the low-risk, retractable weight pass, and then see whether the structure can bear it. Check at least five thresholds before resuming work: · Threshold · Observable facts · When not passed · · Safety · There is no imminent danger that is expanding, and you know who to contact and where to go when it worsens · Continue in safe mode and suspend new commitments · · Basic life · Basic diet, sleep preparation, necessary care and critical bills are not continuously lost due to trial work · Reduce tasks and repair the bottom line of life first · · Tasks · Able to complete a clear slice within a limited time and stop at the end · Continue to dismantle, do not extend until "finished" · · Boundaries · Relevant people know the current working hours, unaccountable items and emergency contact information · Complete communication first, do not rely on loss of contact to maintain work · · Review · There is a date, a record, someone can help see the deterioration, and it can be paused when necessary · Do not expand the load · Only one variable is added to a trial load: from 15 minutes to 30 minutes minutes, or go from an internal exercise to a real communication without adding time, complexity, responsibility and public pressure. After you finish, record what you accomplished that day, what you put in the next day, and whether you need any additional recovery. The load can be divided into three layers: Insulation: only save the contact, file status and next step, without pursuing output; Trial load: complete a short-term, low-risk task that can be reviewed by someone; Limited resumption of work: after several consecutive test loads, add a fixed period of work, but retain a clear upper limit and downshift channel. "Do it today...

8. Asking for help should be specific and retain subjectivity: "I feel very sad" is true, but it may not help others know how to approach you. You can write asking for help as an action: "Please accompany me to dinner tonight, there is no need to persuade me. "Please accompany me to the hospital and help me remember the doctor's advice." "Please take a look at this contract for me. I need professional advice." “Please remind me to go out for a walk twice this week. "I can't take on this project for the time being. Please help me clarify the delivery boundaries." " Specific requests give others the opportunity to really help, and also allow you to retain the right to choose how to help. Family support, friend support and professional support have their own boundaries and cannot be substituted for each other. Supporters also need an agreement with clear boundaries. You can agree on: You can: Accompany medical treatment, save emergency contacts, handle a bill together, send a necessary note on your behalf, and confirm safety at the agreed time; No replacement: Do not pretend to be the person signing the decision, do not disclose health and relationship information without authorization, do not turn companionship into surveillance, and do not take over all accounts and finances "I am doing it for you"; Conditions for upgrade: When contact is lost, dangerous plans are clarified, real threats expand, or professionals give suggestions that need to be upgraded, contact the agreed person or local emergency support; Return method: After the risk is reduced, gradually return the account, file, schedule and decision-making power to the person, and jointly review which support is still necessary. Privacy is not about keeping everything secret in a crisis, nor is it about telling everyone the minimum information necessary to complete the security task. Supporters can also be honest about boundaries and help connect other resources; a friend saying "I can't handle this alone" does not mean giving up.

9. This is not a challenge, nor is it a clock-in that must be completed every day. Evidence left behind · · Day 1 · Write safety contacts, symptoms and high-stakes decisions that require time-out · One-page safety checklist · · Day 2 · Eat a regular meal and book or confirm a professional support appointment · Appointment record · · Day 3 · Walk outside for 10–20 minutes and observe body reactions · Time and feelings · · Day 4 · Break down an debt into facts, implications and responsibilities · A draft apology · · Day 5 · Complete a 15-minute work slice in the current mode, or just save the resumption entry · Files, submission records, or next step prompts · · Day 6 · Agree with a trusted person about the support that can be provided, cannot be provided, and needs to be upgraded · A support boundary · · Day 7 · Look back at this week and decide whether to keep, stop, ask for help, and whether to trial load · Next week’s mode and review date · If you can't do it on a certain day, reduce the main tasks and don't stay up late to catch up. The goal of recovery is to regain the boundary, not to create another sense of failure. You can copy the recovery reset table in the life advanced worksheet and put the current mode, safety matters, support boundaries, today's minimum tasks and resumption threshold in a private page; use the weekly review to check whether adjustments are needed. After entering a stable daily life, use the life system chapter to design the complete day, compression day and recovery day.

10. When can't you just rely on willpower: If you suffer from insomnia, persistent depression, panic, pain, changes in appetite, inability to work, or recurring dangerous thoughts, you should seek early medical or psychological professional evaluation.
