Feedback should answer three questions: What is useful? Where did the misunderstanding occur? Which change is most worth making first? The fourth pass: Delivery version Revise based on feedback and write down the version, limitations, sources and known issues. Allow others to start using even a small movement without your verbal input.

5. The position of AI in the work: AI can be four kinds of assistants: Deconstructor: Break down the goal into minimum steps and acceptance conditions; Trainer: Generate parallel tasks for you to repeat in different scenarios; Reviewer: Ask questions based on audience, facts, structure, quality, and risk; Tester: Create boundary inputs, counterexamples, and possible paths to failure. But the following parts are best left to you: defining the problem, choosing your audience, writing the first version, confirming the facts, deciding what to leave out, and giving credit to the final result. A practical collaboration sequence is: write the briefing and first version yourself; let the AI ​​point out only the three issues that most affect the outcome; revise and save the differences yourself; let the AI ​​generate a parallel scenario or counterexample; turn off the AI ​​and complete a retest independently; write sources, feedback, costs, and open issues back to the work record. If AI delivers the final product directly, you may get a beautiful file but lose the most important training process.

6. Quality gates of works: Different works have different standards, but check at least five gates: Clear: the audience knows what problem it solves and what to do next; Accurate: facts, quotes, codes, and numbers can be returned to the source or tested; Usable: the main actions can be completed under real constraints, rather than just demonstration; Maintainable: others know the version, dependencies, limitations, and who to contact when problems arise; Responsible: sensitive data, privacy, copyright, and error consequences have been considered. Speed, word count, and feature count are just proxy metrics. A smaller piece of work that can be interpreted, reviewed, and revised is usually more valuable in the long term than a grand finished product that cannot be handed over.

7. Publishing is not a performance, but obtaining information: Public publishing does not mean giving privacy to everyone. You can choose the audience according to risk: Private record: keep the process and errors only for yourself; Small-scale trial: Give it to three to five relevant people and record whether they can complete the task; Public version: Remove unnecessary personal information, mark the source, restrictions and versions; Formal delivery: Write down the authorization, responsibility, support scope, cost and exit method. Before publishing, ask yourself: Do I have the necessary authorizations? Is third-party information desensitized? Will an unsubstantiated personal story be packaged as proof of results? Honest limitations do not reduce the value of the work, but rather make the feedback more reliable.

8. 7-day work start: Day 1: Choose a real problem from the topic you are studying; Day 2: Write a work brief and a baseline without AI; Day 3: Complete the first version of a micro or small work; Day 4: Let AI or peers point out the three highest value problems; Day 5: Revise by yourself, complete the sources, limitations and failure paths; Day 6: Give it to a real audience for trial or reading; Day 7 Day: Record feedback, determine scope for next version, and save all evidence. If you can only complete one page, a recording, or a minimum script that can run in seven days, you have completed a closed loop from learning to delivery.

9. 12-week work ladder: Weeks 1–2: Complete 4 small works, confirm the theme and scene; Weeks 3–5: Complete 2 small works, start collecting real feedback; Weeks 6–8: Expand a small work into a trialable prototype, record costs and failures; Weeks 9–12: Complete a public or formal delivery, and retest with blind reviews, user feedback, or parallel tasks. Leave originals, revisions, and feedback at each level. The number of works is not the goal. Being able to explain how you go from problem to result is a signal that your ability has begun to stabilize.

10. Stage standards for works: You don’t need to wait for a work to be perfect before calling it a work. A qualified stage product usually: has a clear audience and usage scenarios; has an observable completion standard; has an independently completed original version; has feedback from others, tests or sources; has versions, limitations and next steps; can explain key decisions without relying on chat transcripts. When the work is allowed to be seen, used and questioned by others, learning truly leaves the mind and enters the world.

Ask again after delivery: Delivery proves immediate performance under certain conditions, which does not mean that the ability has been maintained or can be transferred. After completing the work, open the evidence section: How changes are seen, and arrange a delayed retest to remove the prompts, and a transfer task to change the subject, audience, or constraints. Only by keeping the original version, delivery version and re-test version can you see how the work leaves a demonstration and enters real use.

Conclusion: Let the work remember it for you: knowledge will be forgotten, emotions will change, and chat records may disappear. Works are another kind of memory: they remind you what problems you have faced, what choices you have made, where you made mistakes, and how to change your mistakes to the next step. I no longer understand “finishing work” as proving to the world that I’m awesome. It's more like leaving a light to your future self: when you ever wonder again whether you can even start, there's at least one real thing to answer - you've already done it once.

items.title: Evidence: How to see changes
items.core: Establish an evidence chain from baseline, immediate performance, delayed maintenance to real transfer to determine whether learning, AI collaboration and life actions have really changed.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: Evidence must go back to specific tasks, conditions, and times, rather than out-of-scenario scores; Use baseline, immediate performance, delayed hold, and migration samples to form an evidence chain; Separate AI-assisted performance from independent performance, and who bears the judgment when recording handovers; Failures, rework, and inapplicable conditions are also evidence; Changes in life cannot all be quantified, but they can be recorded with more honest observations and boundaries; Only review one main question every seven days to avoid replacing real actions with more records.

1. The evidence is not the transcript: the transcript answers "how many points were scored under a certain set of rules." Evidence answers "under what conditions, what did I accomplish, can others review it, and can I redo it next time?" The two sometimes overlap, but are never the same thing. Collecting ten articles does not prove that you can explain one of the concepts; co-writing a piece of code with AI does not prove that you can maintain it when there is no chat history; getting up early for seven days in a row does not automatically prove that your life is more orderly. They are clues at best and must be put back into the task for examination. A useful piece of evidence must answer at least four questions: · Question · What needs to be written clearly · What will happen if it is missing · · Can it be traced back? · Where are the samples, sources, editions and dates · Results can only be retold from memory · · Are there conditions? · What are the subject, audience, time, tools and constraints · Different conditions are mistaken for the same level · · Can they be compared? · Are similar tasks retained between the two times? · Changes cannot be attributed or reviewed · · Can they be migrated? · Can you still complete it after changing the subject, object or scene? · Proficiency only stops at practicing the original questions · Evidence is not to queue people up, but to make the next choice less blind.

2. Save four points in time: For the same task, it is best to save four states. They do not need to be long each time, but they must clearly distinguish "who provided what help at what time." · Time point · Purpose · Example · · Baseline · Before intensive training or tool intervention, know what you can really do · Explain a familiar workflow without checking the manuscript · · Immediate performance · Just after the exercise or feedback, observe whether it can be completed · Re-record after watching the demonstration and revising it · · Delayed maintenance · Do it again after a period of time without the prompt · Repeat the same task seven days later with a different piece of material · · Transfer sample · Change the topic, audience, medium or constraints, and check whether the ability deviates from the original topic · Change the internal description to a brief description to the customer · If you only save the immediate performance, it is easiest to overestimate yourself; if you only save the final product, you will forget how you never got to the meeting. Putting the four time points together, we are closer to an interpretable change trajectory.

3. Don’t confuse the three types of results: there are three common types of results in learning: you can do it, you can remember it after a few days, and you can still use it in another place. They are related to each other but require different checks. Performance: Can you complete the task today? See clearly the errors, time and external help; Sustain: Can it still be completed after a period of time? Remove the prompt just now and keep the difficulty level; Migration: Can the task still be completed after changing the shell? Change the subject, object, sequence, or stress conditions. For example, if you write an English email with the help of AI, it indicates that the immediate performance may be good; only by writing a similar email independently the next day without reading the original manuscript can you observe and maintain it; only when you can actually clarify the problem with a customer with a different tone can you start to approach migration. Don't use the first result to stamp the second and third results.

4. When AI intervenes, record artificial doors: AI will change the speed and the nature of the task. When using a tool, don't just record "what model was used", but also record which judgments are still made by humans: · Conditions · What needs to be done by humans · Evidence focus · · Standalone version · Complete your own first version without looking at the AI · Baseline, errors and stuck locations · · Assisted version · Allow AI to ask, explain, compare or give feedback · Tips, sources, reasons for modifications and rework · · Handover version · Explain, maintain or continue completion to others after closing the chat · Key decisions, permissions, testing and responsible persons · If the AI directly produces the final answer, you should do an additional "retest after removing the tool". Correct answers that cannot be explained cannot be counted as abilities already possessed; automation that cannot be handed over cannot be counted as a system that can be run with confidence. This is why this book repeatedly requires saving AI mission briefs, work briefs and delivery cards, and learning statuses: they are not paperwork, but keep artificial gates and responsibility boundaries in the record.

5. Document failures and rework as evidence: Showing only successful versions can make the method look simpler than it is. Failure provides at least three kinds of information: which condition did not hold true, which assumption was disproven, and which risk should be reduced next time. When recording a failure, don’t just write “didn’t do it well.” It can be written as:

The number of reworks itself is not an indicator of capability. A timely rework may protect users and relationships; repeatedly fixing a task that isn't worth doing may be avoiding more important decisions. The value of evidence lies not in making the record look pretty, but in allowing the price to be involved in the next choice.

6. Don’t make life a dashboard: Some changes are suitable for counting: how many deliveries have been completed, the accuracy rate of delayed retests, whether a test passed or not. Some changes are not suitable for being reduced to a single score: whether you are more willing to ask for help, whether you are less harmful to others, whether you are finally able to stop when you are tired. Regarding the latter, a closer observation can be recorded: In what scenarios do I notice myself being overloaded earlier than before? Do I explain boundaries to those affected, rather than disappearing suddenly? What repairs did I make after a conflict, and what was the outcome? Did I make one less high-risk decision by saving a break? Which changes are only known to you, and which changes have been observed by others? There is no universal answer to these questions, nor does it require turning relationships and bodies into KPIs. They simply help us break down “I seem to have changed” into narratives that respect privacy and acknowledge uncertainty.

7. Use evidence to decide the next step, rather than deciding your own value: Evidence can show whether a method is effective under certain conditions, but it cannot show whether a person is worthy of love or qualified to start over. One failed recording session, one failed test, or one week of failure to complete the plan is not a character judgment. During your weekly review, ask in this order: What are the facts? Write only what you can see, hear, and lead back to the document or source; Which explanation is most useful? Also keep at least one possible counterexample; which variable should be changed next time? Don’t change materials, tools, time, and goals all at the same time; what supports or boundaries are needed? Includes peers, professionals, authorization and suspension conditions; When will the test be retested? Let dates, scenarios, and completion criteria take precedence over emotions. If the evidence is insufficient, don't rush to rate yourself. Narrowing the problem and preserving a better baseline is often more honest than producing an accurate but false conclusion.
8. One-page evidence chain: A study or life action can be compressed into the following page:

This page can be linked to the weekly review template and the ninety-day action list. When the cycle is over, put it side by side with the original sample; don't just keep the summary sentence, but also keep the version that got it wrong.

9. Seven-day evidence audit: For the next seven days, only check one thing every day: Day 1: Save a baseline without the help of AI; Day 2: Write down the task conditions and completion standards; Day 3: Complete an auxiliary exercise and record the specific role of AI; Day 4: Close the tool and independently redo a small part of the same task; Day 5: Find a real person, test or source to propose a counterexample; Day 6: Change a topic or audience and make a migration attempt; 7 days: Compare four time points and determine only one variable to change in the next period. After seven days, you may find that you haven’t made “a lot of progress,” but you will have a clearer sense of where progress has occurred and where it hasn’t. This clarity is an ability in itself because it frees the next step from having to rely on excitement or shame. Evidence is not the end, but the gateway to the next responsibility. When you are ready to bring methods into technology and enterprise delivery, enter the AI ​​development and resource layer entrepreneurship, and let the results be tested by users, costs, failures and handovers; when you are ready to hand over a capability to the complete cycle, enter the action chapter: ninety days, return life to yourself; if a certain concept is still vague, go back to the terminology and method index first, and do not continue to add more information with unclear definitions.

Conclusion: Let the changes be seen honestly: There are many important changes in life without applause: a hurtful message that was not sent, a timely request for help, an apology that was finally completed, and a delivery that still retained boundaries despite exhaustion. They may not fit into a chart, but they are worth remembering. I hope that what the evidence ultimately brings is not monitoring of myself, but a kind of gentle credibility: I know where I have been, I know what I have accomplished today, and I also know which conclusions cannot be written down in a hurry. With this credibility, we don’t need to exaggerate accidental success into talent, nor do we need to exaggerate a failure into destiny. Change does not happen because it is recorded. Recording only gives us the opportunity to recognize changes after they occur and carry them into the next phase of our lives.

items.title: AI learning, project development and resource-level entrepreneurship
items.core: Records Han Xiankai’s engineering, delivery, operation and business verification path from AI learning, AI-assisted development to AI resource-level entrepreneurship, distinguishing between facts, practices and unknown results.
body: Let’s separate the facts, practices and results first: What has happened: I assume the responsibility of chairman of China Ciyuan Cloud Computing Co., Ltd.; the official website currently describes token.love as a unified AI intelligent gateway for enterprise and government-enterprise scenarios, and lists model access, routing disaster recovery, usage metering, audit traces and privatization/offline deployment capabilities. In practice: I use AI to learn new knowledge, disassemble requirements, develop projects, write tests, organize documents and complete delivery. I am also putting these experiences back into team and enterprise scenarios for verification. It remains to be verified whether customers continue to pay, whether services can be scaled up, whether unit economics can be established, whether changes in suppliers are controllable, and whether revenue is sufficient to cover risks. If facts, judgments and wishes are mixed together, entrepreneurial articles will become advertisements; only by separating them can they become reviews. When preparing to dismantle a public experience, you can use the AI ​​Experience Case Review Template to first write down the sources and facts clearly, and then negotiate for negotiation and migration.

How failure in 2022 changes access control today: The problem back then was not not writing code, but not first proving core capabilities, data sets, performance, security, and user value. UI, multi-terminal adaptation and preset results make the product look complete, but they cannot answer "where does the data come from", "how to verify the results" and "who is responsible for failure". Therefore, every AI project today asks five questions first: Does the capability really exist: is it a model, retrieval, rule or manual process, and marketing words cannot be used instead of description; Is the data allowed to be used: are the source, authorization, sensitivity level, retention and deletion clear; How are the results accepted: what are the test samples, boundary conditions, manual review and real user standards; Can the cost be covered: whether the model, network, engineering, support, rework, compliance and failure costs are entered into the ledger; How to exit in case of failure: Who can pause, downgrade, switch, notify, rollback and resume play. If there are no answers to the five questions, the minimum action is not to continue adding features, but to narrow the problem and conduct an experiment that can disprove the hypothesis.

1. From learner to builder: I once understood English learning as "remembering more". Later I learned that the end point of learning is not to collect answers, but to be able to complete tasks independently. The same is true for AI learning: the truly valuable result is not how long the answer the model gives, but whether I can explain key decisions, run the program, face errors, and deliver the work after closing the conversation. I now use a work closed loop: Ask real problems: write down who encounters what problems, and what results are considered complete; Leave an AI-free baseline: do it independently first to expose knowledge gaps, constraints, and blind spots in judgment; Prepare credible materials: provide official documents, data, existing code, organizational policies, and risk boundaries; Let AI help me dismantle: compare plans, generate small-step experiments, explain hypotheses, and do not outsource final judgment; Active development and verification: use AI to assist prototyping, coding, refactoring, testing, documentation, and debugging; Accept feedback from multiple sources: tests, real users, domain experts, source materials, and security reviews for joint judgment; Save status and evidence: record completion, errors, costs, decisions, and next minimum tasks. This closed loop is connected to using AI to learn everything, but project development has an additional hard requirement: every key decision must be able to be tested, explained, or rolled back.

2. Use AI to develop projects: after speed, there must still be quality: AI can generate seemingly complete code in a few minutes, and can also spread errors to the entire project in a few minutes. The way I work is not to let AI replace developers, but to make it a high-frequency, interrogable, and must-acceptance collaborator. 2.1 Project Brief For each project, first create a page of task-brief.md:

"Good experience", "Advanced architecture" and "High degree of intelligence" are not acceptance criteria. Write the criteria as observable actions, such as "Users can complete an import within 10 minutes and see error reports." 2.2 Reviewable development chain · Stages · AI can assist · People must confirm · · Requirements · Organize users, scenarios, constraints and problems · Whether the problem is real and whether the completion standard is observable · · Solution · Propose architecture, interfaces and minimal experiments · Data boundaries, dependencies, failure modes and long-term costs · · Prototype · Generate pages, interfaces, scripts and sample data · Whether the core tasks are solved, rather than just showing the effects · · Implementation · Complete code, explain changes, generate tests · Key logic, permissions, exception handling and maintainability · · Verification · Run tests, static checks, performance and security checks · Whether tests cover real risks and whether results can be reproduced · · Delivery · Organize documents, deployment steps, change records and rollback plans · Whether users can use it, whether the team can take over, and whether problems can be traced · Only push one logical slice at a time, and don't mix requirements, refactoring, formatting, and dependency upgrades. Keeping an AI-free baseline, a real working piece, and a bug/revision log is the difference between speed and power. 2.3 Code and release access control

Before release, save at least: version number, change summary, migration steps, monitoring indicators, rollback trigger conditions, responsible person and user notifications. Code reviews check for requirement deviations, data loss, permission bypasses, injections, race conditions, exception handling, performance, maintainability, and test gaps by severity. Fill in the AI ​​project scorecard after each pilot or release, while retaining the AI-free baseline, AI-assisted version, and delayed independent retest; without these three samples, it is impossible to judge whether the tool brings capabilities, agency work, or rework.

3. What is the AI ​​resource layer: The model is the capability layer, and the application is the result seen by the user; there is also a layer of infrastructure between the two that makes capabilities accessible, controllable, measurable, and sustainable. I call this layer the AI ​​resource layer. It is not just "selling a model interface", but organizing scattered models, accounts, computing power, data boundaries and organizational processes into services that the team can understand, use and manage. As tool invocation and agent orchestration become common, the resource layer also handles interoperability and authorization boundaries. The MCP specification (2026-07-28) defines resources, prompts, and tools as composable connection capabilities and supports optional long-term task numbers; but it does not complete the security review for the system. Data scopes, write permissions, user consent, call records, and recall paths still need to be listed before connecting to any external server. What the agreement reduces is the cost of repeated access, not the cost of liability. In practice, the authorization gate of the AI ​​workflow and the process/result records of the AI ​​evaluation can be used for small-scale verification first. 3.1 Capability map · Resource layer capabilities · Problems encountered by customers · Minimum verifiable evidence · · Multi-model access and routing · Business bets on a single supplier, high switching costs · Routing rules and comparison records of two models on the same task · · Identity, permissions and quotas · Who can use, how much can be used, problems cannot be traced · Role matrix, quota policy, audit log sample · · Measurement, cost and settlement · It can be used but I don’t know how much the team and project spent · Cost report and reconciliation process by team/project/call · · Deployment and operation · Services cannot enter the network and environment approved by the organization · Deployment list, environment differences, rollback drill records · Observation and fault location...

4. Chinese Ci Yuan Cloud and token.love: A business path in practice: China Ci Yuan Cloud Computing Co., Ltd. is the company where I currently hold the responsibility of chairman. The official website currently describes token.love as a unified AI intelligent gateway for enterprise and government-enterprise scenarios, and lists model access, routing disaster recovery, usage metering, audit traces, and privatization/offline deployment capabilities. This is the product positioning on the homepage of the official website. It does not represent endorsement by any third-party organization, nor does it replace formal documents, compliance approvals, contracts, and the customer's own security review. From the resource layer, this business path can be broken down into: Model and computing resources → Unified access and routing → Permissions, measurement and governance → Enterprise system integration → Operation, maintenance and continuous service. The real product should let customers know: where the capabilities come from, how the cost is generated, where the data passes, who will handle the failure, and whether there is still an option for the next migration. Specific capabilities, available regions, packages, compliance scope and service commitments shall be subject to token.love’s formal description and written agreement.

5. Enterprise pilot: First solve an acceptable problem: 5.1 Discovery stage Don’t demonstrate the model first in the first communication. Ask first: What is the current process, which step is the slowest or most error-prone; Who bears the cost, how often does it happen, and what is the impact of errors; Which data can be used, and which data must never leave the organizational boundaries; What are the accounts, contracts, networks, permissions and security requirements of the customer; If the pilot is successful, who will continue to use, approve and pay; What results will make the customer clearly say "continue", and what results will make both parties stop. Output a one-page problem brief, not a one-page general AI value statement. 5.2 Pilot Phase A qualified pilot should have: scope, sample, non-targets, data boundaries, person in charge, time, acceptance criteria, failure exit conditions and cost limit. Keep a baseline of the old process before piloting: labor hours, error rates, wait times, number of reworks, existing costs, and user satisfaction. New processes were simultaneously recorded during the pilot: model invocation, routing, delays, failures, manual takeovers, support hours, data anomalies, rework, and user feedback. Merely recording “how much content was generated” does not demonstrate business improvement. Use the AI ​​project scorecard to register test conditions, costs, independent performance, and online access control by version to avoid being left with just one demonstration after the pilot is over. 5.3 Acceptance and handover Before delivery, the acceptance is divided into four levels: Function: whether the process can be completed and whether errors are visible; Quality: whether the output meets business standards and whether exceptions can be manually taken over; Security: whether permissions, logs, data retention, deletion and audit are passed; Operation: who is responsible for upgrades, failures, costs, supplier switching and user support. The handover package should include architecture diagram, data flow diagram, permission matrix, environment variable description, deployment steps, monitoring panel, duty and upgrade path...

6. The logic of making money: Undertake priceable work for customers: Making money is not to change the name of the model and add a new price, but to take on a part of the work that is originally expensive, scattered or difficult to manage for customers. Possible value exchanges include: Resource management services: Manage model access, quotas and costs by call, team, project or service level; Integration and delivery services: Connect to the customer's existing system, complete deployment, permissions, logs and acceptance; Continuous operation services: Handle upgrades, failures, quality fluctuations, supplier switching and daily support; Governance and security services: Establish data boundaries, approvals, audits, traces and risk treatment processes; Customized projects and training: Complete solutions, prototypes, go-live and team handover around real business problems. These are not revenue promises, but fee interfaces that can be verified on a case-by-case basis. Each item must be answered: why the customer is willing to pay, how to accept the results, and whether the service cost can be covered in the long term. 6.1 Charging methods and applicable scenarios · Charging interface · Suitable for solution · Main risks · Must be recorded · · One-time diagnosis/solution fee · Help customers clarify processes, boundaries and pilots · No subsequent value after solution delivery · Deliverables, working hours, subsequent conversion signals · · Project implementation fee · Integration, deployment, permissions and acceptance · Each customer is re-customized and cannot be copied · Scope, changes, rework and gross profit margin · · Usage or resource management fees · Ongoing management by call, project or team · Vendor price and usage fluctuations · Call volumes, routing, costs, reconciliations and caps · · Subscription/service level fees · Ongoing operations, support and governance · Service commitments that exceed team capabilities · · Response times, availability, support hours and exceptions · · Training and consulting fees · · Helping teams build usage and governance capabilities...

Record one-time and ongoing costs separately for each project. One-time projects look at delivery efficiency, while continuous services look at retention, support intensity, unit cost and renewal signals. If each new customer only adds new calling fees, labor and risks, the larger the scale, the faster the losses may be.

7. Operation and maintenance: There is no enterprise service without a runbook: 7.1 Minimum monitoring panel Request volume, success rate, failure type and number of retries; Latency distribution, rather than just looking at averages; Cost by model, team, project and task; Exceeding quotas, abnormal data, permission denial and manual takeover; Supplier status, routing changes and version changes; User feedback, support hours and recurring issues. These are recommended operating indicators and do not mean that token.love currently provides all capabilities. Indicators, responsible persons, alarm thresholds and storage periods should be written into the project contract or internal operation manual before going online. 7.2 Fault grading and handling

Severe faults are recorded at least: time of discovery, affected items, recent changes, data risks, temporary measures, supplier status, recovery time, customer communication, root cause assumptions and permanent repair evidence. AI can help organize the timeline, but it cannot replace the person responsible for the incident. 7.3 Supplier switching drill Each key supplier should prepare at least: alternate routes, degradation models, throttling strategies, caching or manual processes, data migration plans, contract contacts and rollback tests. Rehearse every quarter with a low-risk sample to verify "can switch" rather than documenting it.

8. Data, security and compliance boundaries: · Data level · Examples · Default practices · · Public · Published documents, public code and data · Available, check sources and licenses · · Internal · Unpublished plans, processes, non-sensitive logs · Only use organization-approved tools, limited members and retention periods · · Confidential · Customer information, contracts, business strategies, undisclosed vulnerabilities · No uploading without explicit approval, prioritizing local processing or desensitization · · Restricted · Keys, identity/medical data, children's data, third-party privacy · Do not enter the common model, processed according to organizational policies and applicable laws · Resource layer services must be able to answer: Where does the data enter, which vendors go through, which logs will be saved, who can view it, how often it is deleted, and how to prove the deletion. Deleting a file does not mean deleting all history, caches, exports and backups.

Nine and twelve weeks verification route: · Time · Key issues · Action · Evidence that must be left behind · · Weeks 1–2 · Which type of organization has the most urgent and specific problems? · Interviews, looking at old processes, drawing data flows · Interview transcripts, baselines, boundaries, stopping conditions · · Weeks 3–5 · Can a minimal product reduce integration or management costs? · Set up a sandbox, plug in a task, run control tests · Runnable prototype, tests, failure records, costs · · Weeks 6–8 · Are customers willing to continue using it in real processes? · Small pilots, manual takeover, weekly reviews · Usage traces, failures, support hours, safety records · · Weeks 9–10 · Can the delivery be replicated by another person? · Handover, deployment, and rollback drills · Runbooks, permission sheets, handover acceptance · Week 11–12 · Are cost, quality, and charges aligned? · Review, quotation experiment, renewal discussion · Cost ledger, quotation, renewal signal, next decision · When the evidence does not support continuation, narrow the problem, change customers, or stop the plan; when the evidence supports continuation, safety, contracts, permissions, monitoring and handover must be completed first, and then expansion can be discussed.

10. Two practical slices of public account articles: from "abstract" to "frame by frame": There are two articles related to me in the WeChat public account, respectively writing about AI from the perspective of character observation and Internet controversy. They are not technical audits, customer stories, or proof of revenue; I treat them as public narratives that complement this practice path with action and problem awareness. 10.1 Reject the first “most likely answer” On August 11, 2026, TokenMany released “Han Xiankai: The Most “Abstract” Human in the AI ​​Circle”. The article explains "abstraction" as not eager to accept ready-made answers, but willing to let technology, business, human nature and daily life reflect each other. This is a literary observation of the author's image, not an independent measure of ability. I translated the transferable parts into development actions: Write the default hypothesis first, and then list at least one counterexplanation; Condens cross-domain associations into a small experiment that can be verified within 1–2 hours; Record which observations come from facts, and which are just analogies, intuitions, or hypotheses to be verified; Allow experiments to overturn your own beautiful ideas, and keep failure samples in the project record. In this way, the "brain hole" will not stop at the expression style, but will go through problem definition, minimum prototype, testing and review, and become evidence that can be checked by others. 10.2 Restore the noise into respondable questions On August 21, 2026, Wanli Center of Guanxue Holdings released "Han Xiankai and AI: Split the noise into frame-by-frame emotions". The article is written in a narrative style: Submit comments one by one to AI classification, record "opinions, evidence, emotional intensity, expression, and degree of response" next to them, and treat "cursing words" as "emotion samples" first. This text cannot prove that a public opinion product has been delivered, nor...

11. The most likely place to lose control: Treat model output as fact, and the demonstration effect as product quality; Mistake one-time project revenue as sustainable business; Only calculate API costs, not support, rework, compliance, sales and management time; Upload customer data, company secrets or third-party privacy to unapproved tools; Be locked in a single model or supplier, but there is no migration, downgrade and failure plan; Promising response times, availability or compliance capabilities that the team cannot reliably provide; writing related products as independent reviews, or hiding business relationships behind recommendations; using more prompt words to cover up problems without real users, real costs and real experimental results. Therefore, this project will adhere to a few simple principles: sources can be traced, interests are clearly stated, results can be retested, risks are not beautified, and unknowns are labeled unknown.

12. What do I hope to leave behind: If this road does not become a big enough business in the end, it should still leave behind three types of things: A set of methods that allow me and the team to learn and develop faster and more steadily; A group of works that real users can use, test and criticize; A business record that does not delete failures, so that future generations know which judgments were valid and which were just wishes at the time. I still want to make money, because income is evidence that value exchange can continue; but income is not the only value, nor is it an ending that can be announced in advance. The more honest goal right now is to connect AI capabilities to real people, real organizations, and real responsibilities, and then see if it’s worth continuing.

Source and boundary: Personal experience: Timeline of software company failure in 2022, recovery in 2023, and re-entering AI in 2026, see my story and entrepreneurship. Project correlation: Chinese Ci Yuan Cloud, token.love, ku0.com and public account articles can be found in the author's project and real practice. There is author correlation and it is not an independent evaluation. Business Conclusion: Charge methodology, cost ledger and 12-week route are methodologies to be validated and are not proof of revenue, customer numbers, profits or return on investment. Official page verification: 2026-10-16. The homepage positioning of token.love and ku0.com and the external article links in this chapter can be accessed; specific product capabilities, service scope, regions, policies and contractual commitments should still be reconfirmed in actual projects.

Bring the method back to daily life: This chapter should not leave readers stuck between product names, architecture diagrams and charging interfaces. What it really wants to leave behind is a slower and more honest working attitude: clarify the problem, write down the boundaries, and put a run, a cost and a failure back into a position where they can be inspected. Whether the project can continue or not ultimately depends on the user, team, contract, time and responsibility. Readers can first go to the author's project and real practice to check the correlation, status and evidence boundaries; or they can go directly to the fourth part: Practice and Recovery, and bring the judgments here back to their own small tasks, weekly rhythms and an action that can be restarted. Technology is paving the road faster, but that doesn’t mean people have already reached it. What can really carry you through the next period of time is not a beautiful demonstration, but your ability to continue learning, continuing to deliver, and continuing to modify under real conditions.

items.title: Part 4: Practice and Recovery
items.core: Let learning and change enter the real schedule, and through the first week of practice, capacity design and returnable rhythm, actions can withstand busyness, interruptions and troughs.
body: The question this department wants to answer: How to leave baseline, feedback, delayed retest and a migration in the first week instead of just leaving continuous punch-ins? How do you prepare for different weights for full days, compression days, and recovery days? How do time, energy, relationships, and bodies fit into a budget together? Which things will truly compound interest, and which repetitions will just accumulate fatigue? After an interruption, how to restore the rhythm with a small enough movement without compensating overdraft? When learners are underage, how do children, parents, teachers and AI divide their labor to provide protection without taking away subjectivity? “Recovery” here does not require you to return to productivity as soon as possible. Safety, eating, sleeping, getting help and basic care can themselves be the most important tasks of the day.

Reading path: · Path · Chapter · Things to leave behind · · Live the week first · Practice chapter: finish the first week first · Starting point, seven-day evidence chain and weekend decision · · Family learning together (on demand) · Family learning chapter: Return growth to children · A task defined by children's participation, role boundaries and fourteen-day common agreement · · Settling down for a day · Life system chapter · Three capacity versions, environmental portals and relationship boundaries · · Give time · Rhythm chapter · Repeatable actions, regression protocols and review dates · Don’t rebuild sleep, study, exercise, work and all relationships at the same time in the first week. Choose only one main question. A system that requires five simultaneous reforms is not ready for real life.

What to leave behind after reading: When you finish this part, please leave behind: A page of rhythm ledger recording capacity, minimum movement and resistance; If you are supporting underage learners, a joint home learning agreement; A record of return after a real interruption; A design to decide to continue, and a clear request to delete; A period of time to protect, a boundary to be spoken, and a person to contact when needed. Rising numbers aren't the only result. If you see fatigue earlier, stay up late less to repay interruptions, be more willing to ask for help, and know better when it's not worth continuing, these are also evidence that the system has become reliable.

Enter the text: Don’t plan an ideal year yet. Narrow the future down to seven days and run an issue through a real schedule, varying capacities and a weekend review. One week is not enough to define you, but it is enough to tell you whether the next week should be lighter or clearer.

items.title: Practice: Complete the first week first
items.core: Before the grand plan, use a real question, a starting point sample, seven days of minimum actions and a weekend retest, and let life rather than passion determine the next step.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: Enter the first week with only one real problem and do not transform your entire life at the same time; Save an unassisted starting point sample before using AI, courses or templates; Use seven days to complete input, output, feedback, delayed retesting and a migration; Prepare actions of different weights for full day, compression day and recovery day; Keep only one valid condition, delete one invalid requirement at the weekend, and decide whether to enter the next week.

1. The first week is not a reduced version of ninety days: many seven-day plans just compress the ninety-day ambition into a smaller grid: study every day, exercise every day, read every day, get up early every day, and record emotions and reflections. It seems complete, but actually turns "observing life" into "taking five exams at the same time." There are only three things you really need to leave from the first week: a starting point sample: what the results will look like when done independently now; a few real-life attempts: whether you can start again, in different capacities and environments; and a weekend decision: what to keep, what to stop, and what to change next week. This is a week not for estimating your potential, but for discovering system conditions. You may find that mornings are not suitable for deep learning, but you are willing to listen to materials while commuting; you may also find that you are not short of time, but you don’t know the first step every time you open a task; you may also find that fatigue has continued to affect your life, and you need to deal with your health and responsibilities first, instead of continuing to increase training. Being able to see these facts earlier is not a failure. It prevents you from using a longer plan to cover up a problem that could have been adjusted earlier.

2. Go into the week with just one question: A good question must meet three criteria: be relevant to real life, be observable within seven days, and the answer may change the next step. · Scenario · Overly broad goals · Questions that can be answered in the first week · · English · Improve speaking · Can I explain a real difficulty in English and respond to a follow-up question? · · Work · Improve programming skills · Can I independently fix a real problem and write tests and change notes? · · Writing · Start continuous output · Can I complete a short article that allows a stranger reader to retell the main idea? · · Life · Become self-disciplined · Can I leave a clear entrance to tomorrow in all three capacities? · · Relationships · Learn to communicate · Can I state a boundary and also make it clear when I will respond back? · Don’t choose a question whose answer is necessarily “keep trying.” A real question should allow for three outcomes: continue, shrink, or stop. You might start by writing:

If the problem involves persistent insomnia, pain, depression, loss of control, or dangerous thoughts, your goals for the first week should first be to document the facts, stay safe, and seek local qualified professional support. This chapter is not a substitute for medical or psychological care.

3. Save the unpolished starting point on day one: do it alone before asking the AI ​​to rewrite, watch a tutorial, or apply a template. Keep it to 10–25 minutes, don’t search for the perfect answer, and don’t re-record it just to make it look better. A starting point could be a 90-second recording, a one-page essay, a code change, a real email, a reading reframing, or a draft of a boundary communication. It does not need to be public, but it must be able to be compared again on the sixth or seventh day. Attach a five-line description to the sample:

It’s normal to have an ugly starting point. Its task is not to maintain self-esteem, but to prevent you in the future from recalling "it seemed worse before" just based on your feelings. Without a starting point, progress is easily exaggerated by excitement, and regression is easily exaggerated by the mood of the day. After saving, decide whether to use AI, companions, or classes. Tools can help you analyze errors, generate parallel tasks, and provide feedback, but they cannot rewrite this baseline for you.

4. Don’t ask for full marks in seven days, just ask to be able to come back: The following is not a course schedule that must be checked in one by one, but a minimum chain of evidence. If one day is interrupted, you can combine actions; if the capacity drops, reduce the output and don't stay up late to compensate. · Number of days · Do one thing · Leave evidence · · Day 1 · Complete the unassisted starting sample · First version and three difficulties · · Day 2 · Find a high-quality input and deal with only one difficulty · Sources, themes and a reusable structure · · Day 3 · Complete the second version after closing the material · · Output and differences from the first version · · Day 4 · Get one concrete feedback · Original words, verifiable questions, and suggestions not to be adopted · · Day 5 · Change only one variable and complete version 3 · Before and after revisions · · Day 6 · Do a delayed retest without looking at notes · Keep and forget sections · · Day 7 · Change topics, audiences, or constraints, test migration · Results under new conditions and decisions for the next week · Don’t fake continuity if you only complete four out of seven days. Write the absence as fact: what happened, which conditions were changed, how much it would cost to come back. The more important evidence than "seven days in a row" is whether you still know where to continue after the interruption.

5. A real example: Talking about fatigue in English: Suppose the question this week is: Can I explain in English why I am tired, what support I need, and respond to a follow-up question without translating sentence by sentence? Exhaustion can come from sleep, illness, stress, caring responsibilities, work schedules, or many other reasons. What is practiced here is expression, not diagnosis. Sleep or physical problems that continue to interfere with your life should be evaluated by a qualified professional. Start by retaining five structures that can be transferred to everyday communication: · English structure · The role it plays · Your sentences · · I have been feeling ... · Describe a recent state, do not write the feeling into a permanent identity · · · What makes it harder is ... · Point out an observable condition · · · I am not sure whether ... · Retain uncertainty, do not pretend to diagnose · · · What I need this week is... · Propose specific, limited support · · · If this continues, I will... · Describe the next call for help or check-up action · · Record a 90-second audio clip on the first day. On the third day, re-record after reading a reliable material or getting language feedback; on the sixth day, repeat without reading the manuscript; on the seventh day, change the audience from "friends" to "colleagues" or "professionals" and observe whether the wording and boundaries change. Don’t just count grammatical errors when grading. Check to see if the other person can answer three things: what happened, what you can't confirm, and what you want to do next. It allows real communication to continue and is closer to usable fluency than imitating a certain accent.

6. Works made in the trough are not responsible for saving lives: During a period of disorder in my life, programming gave me a small entrance to action. In the past, the company's products required a high-performance rich text editor. I couldn't find an open source project that met the needs, so I started making Editable and published it to GitHub. This project includes issues such as the editor core, plug-in system, complex tabular data structure, and rendering engine. I spent a long time working my way through it, and also submitted work to Slate.js. You can view Editable items. I don’t want to write about this experience anymore as “programming cured me” or “I just need to find love to get out of the slump.” Programs do not solve all problems and are not a substitute for care. What it really provided at the time was an hour with clear boundaries: problems could be broken down, code could be tested, and the little piece of work done today wouldn't disappear because of a change in mood. When choosing your work in the first week, you don’t have to look for big projects that will prove your worth in life. Choose something that can be closed within seven days: Fix a reproducible problem and add testing; Write a page with clear instructions for readers; Record an expression that can be followed up; Improve the steps that a real user goes through every day; Submit a contribution with a clear scope that can be rejected. The function of works is not to save you, but to allow judgment to enter reality. It will tell you: whether the problem is real, where the capability gaps are, whether others can use it, and whether it is worth continuing next time.

7. Prepare three gears for capacity: The first week is the easiest to fail, not because there are too few actions, but because the plan only admits one ideal state. Write three stalls in advance: · Stalls · Available capacity · Actions for the day · · Full day · 30–45 minutes of full attention · Input, output, and one-sentence recording · · Compressed day · 10–20 minutes or interrupted multiple times · Only minimal output done, mark next bug · · Recovery day · Illness, insomnia, sadness, or surge in responsibilities · Protect safety and basic care, only prepare for next entrance · Production of the work is not required on the recovery date. Putting materials on the table, writing down the first step for tomorrow, and explaining the delay to relevant people can all be regression actions. If you can only run the recovery file for several days in a row, go back to the recovery section first: catch yourself first and check your health, safety and support network. If you are supporting underage learners, the next chapter will go to the family learning chapter to clarify the role boundaries of children, parents, schools and AI; other readers can continue to the life system chapter to deal with energy budget, environmental design, relationship boundaries and interruption regression. The first week only needs to prove one thing: you are willing to change tasks based on capacity, rather than punishing yourself based on tasks.

8. Answer only four questions at the weekend: Don’t ask “Am I working hard enough” first on the seventh day? Put the first version, feedback, delayed retest and migration results side by side into the evidence chain template, and then answer four questions: Completion: Did I complete the target action under real constraints? Quality: In which observable dimension does the output change? Preservation: After leaving the material behind, what remains? Migration: Will capabilities still be available after changing topics, audiences, or environments? Then write two sentences of decision:

Don’t immediately double your tasks just because the week went well; and don’t declare yourself unsuitable just because the week was chaotic. Use the weekly review template to separate facts, explanations, and next experiment. The sample in the first week is too small to change direction, not enough to define a person.

Conclusion: The first week does not prove who you are: At the end of the first week, you may only have three broken recordings, one problem that has not been fully fixed, a page of text that has been messed up, or several days of intermittent recording. They may not seem life-changing, but they are closer to the future than a grand plan that never enters your life. The real beginning is not how exciting you are on the first day, but how after life is interrupted, you can still find the file, see the next step, acknowledge today's capacity, and then complete an action that does not require performance. Let’s finish the first week first. Let facts filter the direction for passion, let works leave traces for wishes, and let one weekend decision lighten the weight of the next week. You don't have to prove who you are in seven days. You just need to leave a path for the eighth day that you are willing to walk in again.

items.title: Family Learning: Return Growth to Children
items.core: Establish a common learning method for learners, parents and teachers who are roughly in the junior middle school stage, using children's goal expressions, short tasks, work evidence, family boundaries and safe AI to replace monitoring and acting.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: First confirm whose problem it is, whose goal it is, and what requirements the school has that cannot be ignored; Use a short, non-agent sample to establish a starting point, and do not define the child by overall ranking; Parents are responsible for the environment, safety, resources, and communication, and are not responsible for proxy answers, continuous monitoring, or public display; Only promote one real task every week, so that input, output, feedback, delayed retesting, and migration enter the same evidence chain; AI use obeys platform age rules, school requirements, and family agreements, and children's data does not enter the general model by default; When sleep, safety, ongoing pain, school trauma, or family conflict become major concerns, pause the learning experiment and seek appropriate support.

1. First ask: Who wants this change: "Learn English well", "Improve your grades" and "Don't be addicted to mobile phones" are often proposed by adults. They may be motivated by genuine concerns, but they are not yet a matter of the child being able to implement them. There is no rush to make plans during the first conversation. Please let the three parties answer respectively: · Role · Questions that need to be clarified · · Learner · Which real-life scenario have I been stuck in recently? What do I wish was easier? What helps make me uncomfortable? · · Parents/Guardians · What am I really worried about: grades, safety, sleep, habits, the future, or loss of control? Which worries are factual and which are just imagination? · · Teacher/School · What are the clear requirements for current courses, assignments, exams and classes? What abilities can be observed through works or performance? · The answers from the three parties do not have to be exactly the same. What the family needs is not a quick unification of opinions, but a reframing of conflicts from personality judgments to conditions that can be discussed. For example: Adult goal: "Vocabulary must be improved." Learner question: "I stop when I encounter new words when reading in English, and in the end I don't know what the article is about." School requirement: "You need to complete two readings of similar difficulty and a classroom retelling this month." Common question: "Can I finish reading a short article without looking up the dictionary word by word, write the main idea, and do it again with another article seven days later?" Common questions retain school reality while also leaving actions for children to understand and answer. It does not require children to first agree with all adults’ judgments about the future.

2. Do not use the total score as a starting point: the score can explain what happened in a certain assessment, but it cannot alone explain whether the problem comes from vocabulary, comprehension, expression, time, anxiety, sleep, absence from class or unclear tasks. A home learning experiment requires a smaller baseline. First choose a 10–20 minute task that will not publicly humiliate the child: Read a short article that matches the difficulty level of the current curriculum and retell it in three sentences; Listen to a one-to-two-minute piece of material and write down the main idea and two details; Complete three questions of the same type without looking at the answers, and explain why you do so; Introduce an interest in English, allowing pauses, but answer a real follow-up question; Write a piece of code, give a scientific explanation, or divide the wrong questions of the day into three categories according to the reasons. Save the original version and don't correct ten issues in a row on the spot. Ask four things first:

The baseline belongs to the learner and should not be posted to family groups, social platforms, or used to compare with classmates. The need for adults to know enough information to provide support does not equate to the right to disclose all aspects of a child's performance.

3. Four roles, not substitutes for each other: A reliable home learning system requires clarity on who is responsible for what: · Role · Primary responsibility · Role that should not be assumed · · Learner · Submit your own first version; explain difficulties, capacity and needs; participate in choosing next tasks · Provide ongoing justification for adult anxiety · · Parents/Guardians · Protect time, sleep, safety, equipment and necessary resources; Help with communication; Enforce privacy boundaries · Ghostwriting answers, monitoring throughout the day, maintaining the plan with shame · · Teacher/school · Explain course requirements; provide subject-related feedback and support paths · Replaced by AI or family guessing · · AI/Tools · Explain, ask questions, generate parallel exercises and organize errors within the scope allowed · Act as guardian, decide the child's value, do submissions on behalf of the child or preserve the child's privacy · The child has the right to participate, which does not mean that he alone bears all the responsibilities. Just because adults have the responsibility to protect does not mean they have every answer. Once the roles are clear, help doesn't have to happen through takeover.

4. The job of parents is to set up the environment rather than stand behind it: Continuous supervision will create a superficial efficiency: children act when they are seen, and as soon as the adult leaves, the system loses momentum. More secure family support encompasses four categories of work. Protect an available time box. Instead of requiring a fixed two hours a day, confirm with your child a time that is realistically available and can be ended. An initial experiment can be 20–35 minutes long: know the task before you start, save a version when you finish, and don’t drag it out late into the night unfinished. Reduce startup friction. Prepare materials, accounts, headphones, dictionaries, pens and paper or documents in advance. Adults can help find school-specific resources, troubleshoot equipment, and organize spaces without having to sit around and watch every move. Only ask questions that can change the next step. More useful than "Are you serious today?" is: Which step can you complete independently? Which step needs tips? Does this prompt help you understand, or does it give you a direct answer? What will be the first step after opening the file tomorrow? End of Conservation At the end of study time, help the child save the evidence, write down the next entry, and then allow the task to leave the dining room table and bedroom. Learning without end boundaries will turn the entire family into a classroom that never ends.

5. Complete only one real task per week: Here is a seven-day path for family experimentation, with no requirement to complete each day: · Number of days · Learner actions · Adult support · Evidence left behind · · Day 1 · Complete the unacted starting sample · Explain time and privacy boundaries · Original version with one difficulty · · Day 2 · Work on a problem that most affects the outcome · Provide designated materials or contact the teacher · Source and understanding in one sentence · · Day 3 · Close the material and complete the second version · No continuous correction in the process · Second version · · Day 4 · Accept up to three specific feedbacks · Help distinguish observations, comments and suggestions · Feedback original words and choices · · Day 5 · Change only one variable · Protect the time box, no additional tasks · Revised version · · Day 6 · Delayed retest without looking at old answers · No reminder of original answers · Delayed sample · · Day 7 · Do a transfer with a change of topic, audience, or question type · Review together, allowing for narrowing or stopping · New condition results and decisions for next week · If there are already enough school assignments, home experiments should be embedded in existing tasks rather than adding another set of lessons. Transforming the same assignment into comparable samples is often more reliable than purchasing additional materials.

6. A synthetic example: Introduce your interests in English: The following is a method demonstration, not a real student case, nor can it represent all junior high school students. The common question is: Can learners introduce an interest in English for two minutes without memorizing it sentence by sentence, and answer a follow-up question from a classmate? The baseline on the first day may leave these facts: · Conditions · Results · · 10 minutes of preparation, without AI · Can speak for 45 seconds; repeat I like; stop when asked · Only three structures remain this week:

The AI or teacher can point out up to three issues affecting understanding after the learner submits the first version, and generate a parallel exercise on a different topic of interest. The final class content, facts and expressions are confirmed by the learners. On the sixth day, re-record without reading the original manuscript, and on the seventh day, change the audience to family members or classmates. If you can still only recite the original sentence, do not add a longer word list next week, but continue to practice the structure of "reasons-examples-still learning". This exercise does not promise to improve exam rankings. It just puts vocabulary, organization, audience feedback, and delayed retest into the same real task.

7. Before AI enters the home, it must pass through five doors: UNESCO’s generative AI education guidance emphasizes the humanistic perspective and the development of human capabilities. For underage learners, "humanism" cannot be just a beautiful slogan, it must become at least five checks. Age and Account Gate Check the platform’s current age, account, guardianship and district rules first, and then check the school requirements. Do not lie about your age, use an unknown account, or circumvent school policies in order to use a feature. Rules will change and families should refer to current terms and school announcements. Data Gate does not upload names, schools, classes, IDs, precise locations, faces, voiceprints, health, family relationships, transcripts, private information of teachers or classmates by default. Practice using composite names, paraphrased material, and minimal unrecognizable fragments. First Version Gate As long as the task allows, children submit their own version first, and then let the AI ​​ask questions, explain or give feedback. If AI gives a complete composition, code or answer from the first step, families will get the finished product, not the starting point evidence. Judgment Gate AI doesn’t decide whether a child is smart, suited for a certain direction, whether a friend is trustworthy, whether someone is sick, or who “just has something wrong” in a family conflict. Return to trusted adult, school and local qualified professional support when it comes to safety, health, school injuries and ongoing pain. Exit Door Save the work at the end of the study, close the session, and allow the child to retell it in their own words. AI shouldn’t be the only person you can talk to, the all-time companion, or the home monitoring tool. The ability to continue thinking after the tool is withdrawn is evidence that the ability remains in the person.

8. Three capacities, no need to stay up late to repay study: Families can write three versions together: · Gear · Situation of the day · Learning action · Adult action · · Complete day · Homework and physical condition are relatively stable · 20–35 minutes for input, output and recording · Protect time, no temporary additions · · Compressed day · More homework, activities or commuting · 10-minute minimum output · Help determine the first step and end point · · Recovery day · Illness, obvious lack of sleep, injury, conflict or very low capacity · Pause training and only reserve the next entrance · Prioritize care, safety, communication and necessary help · Missed training does not need to be made up in one session on the weekend, nor can it be repaid with lost sleep. If a family puts "the integrity of the plan" before the body and relationships, the plan itself will lose its educational significance.

9. Feedback does not mean judging the child: Feedback should be directed at the work and conditions, not personality: · Insufficient statement · More actionable feedback · · You are just not serious · There are no steps for the third question this time, I don’t know where you start guessing · · Your English foundation is too poor · The main idea of this paragraph can be repeated, but the two causal connections are not clearly explained · · AI has already explained it, why can’t you still know it · I can complete the original question after reading the explanation, but the parallel questions still need prompting after seven days · · Others can persist · Two of the three tasks this week started too late in the evening, and we need to change the time · Parents can keep at most one main question and three pieces of feedback each time. Children can also reject a review and explain the reasons. Learning together is not about removing adult judgment, but about allowing judgment to be heard, checked and revised.

10. When should you suspend learning experiments: Do not upgrade clocking, punishment or AI supervision first when the following situations occur: Sleeping, eating, or physical discomfort continues to affect daily functions; Strong fear, despair, loss of control, or thoughts of harm occur repeatedly before and after learning; There is school violence, bullying, threats, extortion, sexual harassment, or other safety risks; Family conflicts can no longer be safely discussed, and the study plan becomes a tool of attack or control; The child refuses to enter school or tasks for a long time, and the reasons cannot be explained by just one communication. Stay safe first, contact a trusted adult, school personnel, and seek local qualified medical, psychological, social services, or emergency support as appropriate. This chapter does not diagnose the cause, nor is it a substitute for professional treatment. Suspending learning and experimentation does not mean giving up growth. A person needs to have a ground to stand on before the method can take place.

11. Use fourteen days to decide whether to continue, adjust, or stop: Families do not need to initially commit to a semester. First complete the fourteen-day experiment using the family learning joint agreement, and answer the following questions at the end:

Do not hold a "review meeting" in front of the children where only adults speak. The learner speaks first, and the adult adds later; when facts conflict, keep two records and confirm with the teacher when necessary.
12. A minimum agreement for the family: If you can only start four lines today, you can write:
These four lines are not a legal contract, and they do not guarantee that conflicts will disappear. It just rewords “it’s all for your own good” into responsibilities that both parties can review.

Source and Boundary: UNESCO: Guidance for generative AI in education and research, verified on 2026-09-02; This chapter only adopts its humanistic and capability development direction, and does not replace international guidance with local school rules, platform terms or professional opinions. Specific platform age, account, guardianship and data rules may change. Please check the current official terms, school policies and local applicable requirements before use. Related entrances: Practice: Finish the first week first ｜ Life System ｜ Shared Agreement on Family Learning

Conclusion: Don’t walk that road for your children: Parents see more risks than their children, and often see the weight of time earlier. Because of this, love can easily become a substitute: choosing goals for him, explaining failures for him, keeping every minute for him, and proving for him that all this is necessary. But the most precious part of learning cannot be done by others. A child needs to meet the master himself, make a first version that is not good enough, hear the feedback for himself, and discover for himself what is left after seven days. Adults can guard the lights, the door, and the way home, but they cannot grow judgment for him. I hope that learning at home will no longer be a competition where who is more anxious has the right to speak. I hope that children can say "This is what I want to accomplish" and "I can't do it today"; I hope that after adults hear these two sentences, they will still know how to help and not rush to take away the direction. Growth is not about sending children to a destination pre-drawn by adults. It accompanies him to gradually take his own steps in the increasingly larger world.

items.title: Life System: Put changes into daily life
items.core: Use the minimum feasible day, energy budget, environmental design and interruption regression to put learning and change into real life.
body: Quick overview of this chapter: Use "minimum viable day" instead of a schedule that must be full marks; budget time, energy and responsibilities together, without using willpower to pay all costs; reduce startup friction through environment and default options, and reduce unconscious input; clarify boundaries for relationships and work in advance, so that concentration does not cost the cost of losing contact; only restart the next step when the plan is interrupted, and leave evidence for review; use seven days of practice to change this system into a version that suits you.

1. Design the minimum feasible day first: "Study two hours a day" sounds clear, but it does not answer a more practical question: Can I still do it when there are only twenty minutes left today? Write a three-level schedule first. They are not success, failure, and abandonment, but three stalls of the same system at different capacities: · Gear · Applicable moment · What must remain · · Full day · Relatively stable time and energy · One input, one output, one record · · Compressed day · Work gets longer, attention is shredded · 10–25 minutes of minimum output · · Recovery day · Illness, insomnia, sadness, or a sudden increase in responsibilities · Safety, Diet, Rest, and a Tip to Get Back in Your System · A full day is not the standard answer, nor is a recovery day a moral failure. You could write your own version as:

If you can't even complete the minimum output, check your sleep, body, safety and responsibility first instead of continuing to add more. The judgment here is for life planning, not medical diagnosis; conditions that continue to affect function should be referred to a qualified local professional for evaluation.

2. Budget your time, energy, and responsibilities: There are 24 hours in a day, but the number of hours available for deep work is not the same. Energy is consumed by commuting, pain, caregiving, meetings, emotions, and switching. Putting this into your plan is not about making excuses for yourself, but about letting your plan begin to describe real people. Start by answering four questions each week: What time is already occupied by fixed responsibilities? What are the easiest times to retain your full attention for 25–45 minutes? What things that night will consume the next day's capacity? If you could only accomplish one important thing this week, which one would be most worthy of protection? You can use the following table to make a rough budget: · Resources · Facts of the week · Lower limit to protect · Adjustments when exceeded · · Time · Available fixed slots · A mainline time box · Narrow tasks without squeezing breaks · · Energy · High, low and unpredictable periods · Complete a minimum output · Switch to a low-friction version · · Attention · Notifications, switches and information portals · An uninterrupted window · Closing a portal · · Relationships · People and responsibilities to respond to · An honest communication · State delays and boundaries in advance · · Body · Sleep, pain, mobility and recovery · Basic care and safety · Pause on high-stakes decisions and ask for support · Don’t think of “I can squeeze in a little more” as a budget. The budget should first leave a bottom line that cannot be overdrawn, and then arrange for variable ambitions.

3. Let the environment reduce friction for you: Many delays are not a matter of values, but that the first step is too far: files are hidden in the wrong directory, practice materials have to be searched again, and the phone opens ten entrances as soon as it lights up. Instead of asking yourself to be stronger every time, keep the next step handy. Start friction. Open only one file the day before and write the next step at the top of the file; divide the practice materials into three places according to "today, backup, and archive", and do not let favorites determine the task; prepare a fixed entrance for the 25-minute task: the same card, the same pen or the same terminal command; write your own judgment before using AI to avoid mistaking "opening the chat window" as having started learning. Exit Friction Systems also need ways to end. Set a clear closing action: save the version, write down a bug, close the tab, and record your first step for tomorrow. Tasks that are not finished will continue to occupy space in the mind, making it more difficult to start next time. Environmental design is not about turning life into a military camp. It just makes it easier to start important things, and makes unimportant inputs require one more step of confirmation.

4. Embed learning into your existing life: The easiest way to fail with a new habit is that it requires you to have a blank period of time that never exists. A safer approach is to hang the action on something that has already happened: · Existing anchor · Embeddable action · Evidence · · Turn on the computer · Write a sentence about today's question first · One-line update of learning status · · After lunch · Listen to a short material and note the gist · A record of the listening audit · · Before the meeting · Retell a risk in English · 60 seconds of recording · · Close the work · Save today's version and next step · Work or code submission · · Fixed weekend period · Review the first version and feedback · Weekly review · Anchor points are not a hard and fast rule. If a scene is interrupted frequently, switch to a more reliable scene. The goal is not to have output every minute, but so that important moves don’t have to be renegotiated every time.

5. Let the relationship know your boundaries: Focusing is not disappearing.
