Recent official information separates "can run longer" and "can be left to run": long-term tasks require checkpoints, recovery points, and manual takeover; browser pages, screenshots, and tool return values ​​should all be treated as untrusted materials. First do an experiment without side effects: give the task a unique running number, limit the network exit and write range, save the state and evidence after each stage is completed; recover from the latest checkpoint after interruption, and check whether it has been written before retrying. Experiment with at least...

What is needed for a small team handover: When handing over a process to a colleague, attach at least: a working input, a qualified output, a failure example, how to run it, what actions are allowed, who is responsible for acceptance, and where to recover if something goes wrong. Documents and prompts must have versions; re-run representative cases after changing models, prompts, retrieval materials or tools. The “AI lead” on the team can’t just be responsible for tool subscriptions. Someone also needs to maintain the samples, receive errors, confirm sources, remove expired materials, and decide when to return to manual processes. Factor maintenance time into task costs first and then evaluate expansion scope.

Exercise you can do today: Pick a task you really want to do this week and write down the input, deliverables, and three checkpoints. Complete the manual version and the AI ​​collaboration version once each, and record the total time taken and a failure case; if MCP or other external tools are connected, additionally record the tool scope, authorizer, and withdrawal method. Then use AI evaluation and reliability methods to determine whether it is worth doing another round. If this process is to become a paid service, continue reading from the problem to the first users; if someone is willing to use the tool, it can only show that the task may be valuable, but cannot directly prove the scale of demand or continued payment.

items.title: AI Measurement and Reliability: Know When It's Deliverable
items.core: Compare AI workflows with real tasks, small test sets, failure classification, and full costs to identify the difference between right first time and stable availability.
body: Define qualifications starting with the task: Don’t just ask “Was the answer good or bad?” Write out the next actions that the user will complete, as well as unacceptable failures. For example, when organizing public event information, the qualified results must allow people to find the original text, distinguish the known from the unknown, and do not write the expiration date as the current arrangement. Divide the inspection into two levels: All conditions must be passed: authentic sources, correct key figures, no leakage of restricted information, and no unauthorized operations. Failure cannot be offset by style scores. Comparable qualities: clear organization, readability, number of revisions, and total time taken. Compare these differences after satisfying the previous level. Standards should be written before test results. Temporarily relaxing standards after seeing a candidate version fail will only allow reviews to defend the solution.

Build a small and differentiated test set: sample from real tasks you are preparing to serve, obtain permission to use materials and remove unnecessary information. For the first time, you can select ten cases: four common inputs, two missing items, two conflicting or expired inputs, a tool failure, and a case with operating instructions entrained in the material. This is just a starting point, the important thing is to cover failures with different consequences. · Type of case · What you want to observe · Examples of qualified behavior · · Common tasks · Whether basic abilities are sufficient · The results meet the format and fact requirements · · Missing information · Will you make up the facts · Mark the missing items and explain what else is needed · · Source conflicts · Will you choose without authorization · Keep conflicts, indicate the date and caliber · · Tool timeout or empty results · Will you lie about completion · Report the failure status and save the recoverable progress · · Malicious instructions in the material · Will it exceed the authority · Use the instructions as materials and maintain the original task boundaries · · Repeat submission · Will there be repeated side effects · Check the existing status before deciding whether to write · Save the input, expected behavior and judgment basis for each case. Don't write the answers to all cases into the prompts and then treat the scores as generalization ability. A group of cases that have not participated in the modification is left and will be used when deciding to adopt the version; if you refer to it to continue adjusting prompts, it is no longer a reserved set and new cases need to be added.

Only change one major factor when comparing: fix the same inputs, data, tool permissions and budget for the current version and the candidate version, record the model identification, prompt version, data version and run time. If you change the model, hints and knowledge base at the same time, it will be difficult to know where the improvement comes from. The same case can be run several times to observe fluctuations, paying special attention to tasks that generate external actions. Duplicate results cannot be treated as more independent users, nor can the best result at one time represent the entire version. Keep failure, timeout and manual takeover records and do not delete them from the denominator. Anthropic's review article in January 2026 split an evaluation into several objects that cannot be mixed: a task is a fixed input and success condition, an attempt is a run of the task, the process record contains tool calls and intermediate interactions, the result is the final actual state of the environment, and the evaluation or agent harness is responsible for stringing together the run, record and score. Multi-round systems should save these objects separately; "model says done" is not a substitute for checking databases, files, or user-visible results. Assessment concepts are referenced here; the following examples, rubrics, and worksheets are the guide's own exercise designs. See Demystifying evals for AI agents.

Long-term tasks and isolation environments should be evaluated separately: If the task can run asynchronously, wait for the tool to return, or receive input midway, split "whether it is completed" into four questions: whether the state can be restored, whether it is safe to retry, whether the network and write range are still within authorization, and whether humans can take over before irreversible actions. The MCP 2026-07-28 specification introduces Tasks as an optional long-duration task extension; it provides interoperability semantics and does not decide timeouts, permissions, or security boundaries for you. For each run, a unique number, checkpoint, wall clock duration, tool invocation count, network domain name, authorization record, and final environment state are saved. Start each experiment with a clean environment to avoid files, tokens, or caches left over from the previous run that make the results look better. If you use a browser or computer to operate, treat page text, screenshots and links as untrustworthy materials; do not expand the network export or upload scope just because the page requires it. Add another case of "evaluation environment failure": the network should be closed but unexpectedly opened, the test machine reaches the real system, or the write is retried and repeated. Anthropic's review of network security evaluation incidents shows that environment configuration and scope description can themselves be the cause of failure; therefore, passing conditions should include network egress verification, credential isolation, real-time logs, and recoverable manual fallback. See Investigating three incidents in our cybersecurity evaluations and MCP Security Best Practices. Minimal case of a long task · Case · Extra records · Hard door · · Resume after pause · Checkpoints, resume numbers, completed writes · No repeated side effects, final state can be verified...

Full example: A faster but not yet adoptable version: Suppose a team tests the comparison table workflow with ten public information, each running only once, and gets the following fictitious results: · Metrics · Current version A · Candidate version B · · First delivery qualified · 8/10 · 9/10 · · Key factual errors · 0 · 1: Write the ungiven price as free · · Qualified after manual modification · 10/10 · 10/10 · · Preparation, operation, verification and rework · 120 minutes · 100 minutes · · Tool cost · 6 yuan · 8 yuan · If the working hours are estimated internally at 60 yuan per hour in the example, the total cost of this batch of tasks for A is 120 ÷ 60 × 60 + 6 = 126 yuan, and for B is 100 ÷ 60 × 60 + 8 = 108 yuan. This is just an example of process costs, excluding customer acquisition, taxes and other operating items; the costs of each qualified result after rework are included are 12.6 yuan and 10.8 yuan respectively. B is faster and has more qualified products for the first time, but it violates the condition that "key facts cannot be fabricated". Therefore, the decision in this round is not to expand use, but to repair and retest first. This doesn't mean A has been proven reliable; ten inputs, one run each still has limited evidence. Here "passed for the first time" and "passed after manual modification" must be separated. If all the results of human repairs are counted as the correct answers of the model, the quality will be exaggerated and the maintenance cost will be underestimated.

Who will score, and how to handle differences: Fields, calculations, file status, etc. should be judged with clear rules as much as possible. Semantics, usage, and expression were checked by someone knowledgeable about the task. If you use model-assisted scoring, first compare it with a batch of manually annotated cases to check whether it favors longer, more confident answers. Look at the source material item by item for high-impact errors, not just the average score. When the two reviewers disagree, record the points of dispute, add scoring instructions, and re-evaluate; do not just rely on voting to cover up ambiguity in the standards. Different expressions of the answers are allowed, and "insufficient material to judge" is allowed to be the correct result.

Convert failure to the next regression check: · Failure · Troubleshoot first · Next step of verification · · The source does not support the conclusion · Material version, extraction, reference location · Change to a material with similar expressions but different conclusions · · No information found · Search scope, filter conditions, tool return · Add a case where the information does not exist · · Output format drift · Field convention, structure verification · Missing fields and extra fields can be found · · Repeated or unauthorized operations · Permissions, status checks, retry logic · Use a side-effect-free test environment to drill interruption retries · · Verification time is too long · Task scope, source granularity, acceptance method · Compare whether the total working hours have really dropped · After repair, run both the case that triggered the problem and the previously qualified cases to avoid solving one part and damaging the other. If the result relies on external services, retain the data and environment version and explain which conditions cannot be completely reproduced.

From evaluation to small-scale use: After the model is changed, the old results cannot be automatically used. A pass describes the performance under a certain set of inputs, models, materials, memory settings and tool permissions. This guide recommends recording these conditions together; if the service does not provide a fixed version, also record the displayed model name, run date and uncontrollable parts truthfully, without pretending to be completely reproducible. Create two sets of samples with different purposes: the regression set contains errors that have been exposed to prevent recurrence; the retention set is used to check situations that are not involved in tuning. After repeatedly looking at the retention set modification process, you should transfer it to the development or regression set and add new cases. When changing models or tools, updating the knowledge base, opening memories, or discovering anomalies, first run relevant cases in the test environment and check the final files or system status. For retrieval tasks, check "whether the required materials have been found" and "whether the conclusion is supported by the materials" respectively; for multi-modal tasks, check "whether the identification is correct" and "whether the explanation is valid". Only in this way can you know which level to repair. Document adoption date, responsible person, and last qualified version. If a hard condition fails, the verified scope will be retracted; if the old version cannot be restored, the manual process will be retained as a fallback. Maintenance work is also included in the cost, and a release is not a substitute for follow-up care. Let every selection have an exit method. Before selecting a version, write down the tasks allowed to be processed, unsupported input, manual acceptance conditions, cost caps and withdrawal methods. During small-scale use, continue to collect real failures and update samples regularly; rerun relevant tests after changing models, prompts, retrieval or tools. Record a complete comparison in the AI ​​evaluation record template. If you don’t have a real task yet, go back to customer verification first: no matter how detailed the evaluation is, it cannot prove that a result that no one needs is worth producing.

items.title: Resource Layer and Enterprise Services: A Practical Note
items.core: Appendix Case: The author’s practical path from learner to builder to AI resource layer, explaining why companies pay, how to accept delivery, data and permission boundaries, and twelve-week verification and stopping conditions.
body: What does this page answer: How does an ordinary person go from "being able to use AI to learn", to "being able to use AI to deliver", and then to "managing AI capabilities for others"? During this process, why customers are willing to pay, what counts as delivery completion, who is responsible for failures, and when should it stop. This page only discusses business logic and engineering boundaries. The method part - learning loop, task briefing, code access control and evidence card - is left in the third part of the text and the practical pages such as AI workflow and AI evaluation.

From learner to builder to resource layer: The author’s experience can be divided into three segments, each with a different type of evidence: Learner: Learn to complete tasks in English, programming and AI. Evidence is work, error records, and retest results. Builder: Use AI to assist requirements, prototyping, coding, testing, documentation and delivery. The evidence is a working system, acceptance records, and rollback plans. Resource layer: Organize scattered models, accounts, computing power, data boundaries and organizational processes into services that teams can access, control, measure and govern. The evidence is customer trials, cost ledgers, operating records and renewal decisions. There is no automatic upgrade between the three stages. Being able to learn does not mean being able to deliver, and being able to deliver does not mean being able to operate a service. With every step forward, the scope of responsibility expands: from being responsible for your own results to being responsible for your customers' data, costs, and failures.

Why enterprises pay: Enterprises pay, usually not for "one more model name", but to take on a part of the work that is originally expensive, scattered or difficult to manage: The business is bet on a single supplier, and switching costs are high; Who can use it, how much can be used, and problems cannot be traced; It can be used, but it is not known how much the team and the project have spent; The service cannot enter the network and environment approved by the organization; Delays, failures and quality fluctuations cannot be explained; The flow, retention and approval of sensitive data are unclear; Ability cannot enter the business process, and if there is a problem, no one can be found. The value of the resource layer is to make these problems less repetitive and integrated, less out of control costs, and more responsible interfaces that can be understood and managed by the organization. Charging interface and applicable scenarios · Charging interface · Suitable for solution · Main risks · Must be recorded · · One-time diagnosis or solution fee · Help customers clarify processes, boundaries and pilots · No subsequent value after solution delivery · Deliverables, working hours, follow-up signals · · Project implementation fee · Integration, deployment, permissions and acceptance · Re-customized by each customer and cannot be copied · Scope, change, rework and gross profit margin · · Usage or resource management fee · Ongoing management by call, project or team · Supplier price and usage fluctuations · Call volume, routing, costs, reconciliation and caps · Subscription or service level fees · Ongoing operations, support and governance · Service commitments exceed team capabilities · Response time, availability, support hours and exceptions · · Training and consulting fees · Help the team build usage and governance capabilities · It is difficult to attribute the effect if you don’t use it after learning · Course objectives, assignments, migration and retesting · These are chargeable interfaces that can be verified on an item-by-item basis, not revenue forecasts. Each item must answer three questions: Why would the customer want to...

One-time costs and ongoing costs should be recorded separately. One-time projects look at delivery efficiency; continuous services look at retention, support intensity, unit cost and renewal signals. If each new customer only adds new call fees, labor and risks, the larger the scale, the faster the losses may be.

How an AI development delivery is accepted: The acceptance is divided into four layers. If there is no evidence at any layer, it cannot be considered complete: Function: whether the process can be completed, whether errors are visible, and whether exceptions can be manually taken over. Quality: Whether the output meets business standards, which cases have regressed after revision, and whether manual review is still within the budget. Security: permissions, logs, data retention, deletion and whether audits pass. Operations: Who is responsible for upgrades, outages, costs, vendor switching and user support. The handover package contains at least: architecture diagram, data flow diagram, permission matrix, environment variable description, deployment steps, monitoring panel, duty and upgrade path, rollback method, known issues and next review date. Without a runbook, there is no enterprise service. Save before release: version number, change summary, migration steps, monitoring indicators, rollback trigger conditions, responsible person and user notifications. After release, use the AI ​​project scorecard to register test conditions, costs, independent performance, and online access control by version to avoid leaving only one demonstration after the pilot.

Data, permissions and security boundaries: The resource layer handles other people's data, and boundaries must precede functions: Minimum permissions: Roles, quotas, visible scopes and call records are designed separately; denied by default and authorized item by item. Data tiering: Public, internal, confidential and restricted materials are handled separately; restricted data does not enter unapproved paths. Traceability: each call records the time, subject, task, model, routing and result status; the retention period and deletion method are clearly written. Opt-out: Customers can export, migrate, delete data, and know how long the migration will take. The protocol is not a guarantee: The MCP specification (2026-07-28) reduces the cost of repeated access, but it does not complete the security review for the system; external servers, tool descriptions, and web page content are all treated as untrusted input. Manual takeover: High-risk actions must be able to be suspended, downgraded, switched and rolled back; who has the right to stop is written in the operation manual. These boundaries apply to personal practice as well. The recording habits you develop during the learning stage will directly determine whether you can clearly explain "where the data passes, who is responsible, and what to do if there is a problem" when entering the enterprise scenario.

Twelve-week verification and stopping conditions: A rollback resource layer pilot that can be advanced in twelve weeks. Each stage leaves evidence and can be stopped at any stage. Weeks 1–4: Define the problem and baseline. Walk through the customer's existing process and record labor time, errors, waiting, rework, and existing costs. Outputs a one-page problem brief, data boundaries, and acceptance criteria; no demonstration, no commitment to results. Weeks 5–8: Bounded pilot. Select an acceptable slice and write down the scope, sample, non-targets, person in charge, cost limit and exit conditions. Also record the invocation, routing, delays, failures, manual takeover and support hours of the new process. Weeks 9–12: Acceptance and Decision. According to the four-level acceptance of function, quality, safety and operation, the handover package is completed and a review is conducted: continue, reduce the scope, change the problem, or stop. Stopping is not failing, but using the evidence to inform your next decision. Stop conditions (pause and review if any one of them appears): Key data cannot be confirmed for authorization or cannot be deleted; Error rate, delay or support cost exceeds the pre-specified upper limit; Acceptance criteria are repeatedly moved during the pilot process; Customers cannot tell who uses, who pays, and who is responsible; the team is unable to fulfill the promised service level.

Limitations and next steps: The limitations of this page need to be written clearly: It records the author's personal practice and judgment, not a third-party audit, nor an industry benchmark; The company's product capabilities, regions, packages, and compliance scope are subject to formal descriptions and written agreements, and will change; Whether customers continue to pay, whether unit economics can be established, and whether costs are controllable after scale expansion, we are still waiting for real results; The book does not provide prices, profits, customer numbers, or revenue figures, and readers should not regard any public narrative as investment advice. The next step can be small: choose a real problem, use AI mission briefing to write down the boundaries, use AI to go through the case review and recording process, and then decide whether it is worth entering the pilot. The resource layer is not a more advanced path, it just makes the matter of "taking on part of the work for others" more specific. Methods and lessons learned from failures return to the third part of the text; the smallest experiments on the entrepreneurial side are from problems to the first users and sustainable small businesses.

items.title: Should we help the elderly?
items.core: A personal article in 2016 that recorded the experience of helping the elderly twice. The conclusion is limited to doing what one can do rather than universal probability.
body: Chestnut 1: Go to the hospital: The last time I went back to my hometown, I took my mother to buy groceries in the morning. At the door of a live fish shop, I met an old man with a sudden nose bleeding. I didn't know what was going on at first, until the old man stumbled up to me and asked me how to get to the hospital. I saw that the paper he was covering his nose was bleeding. My first reaction was to point him in the direction of the hospital, which was not far away, about 600 meters away. When he took his first step he almost fell to the ground and I knew immediately that this wasn't going to work. There are all fish sellers around here, and the road is very slippery, making it easy to fall. In addition, the old man has a bleeding nose and needs to hold his head high, so the chance of an accident is greater. I hurriedly caught up with him and helped him up. When I was crossing the intersection, a large truck passed by. The old man walked forward in a daze, and almost hit the truck with me. At this time, the old man was very excited and shouted for me to save him. He went directly to rescue him and said that he would save himself first. Seeing the old man trembling and falling in my arms, I began to get nervous. I silently said in my heart that it is important to save people, it is important to save people. My mother also followed and held the old man's handbag. I hugged my grandfather and walked quickly to the hospital. Go straight to the emergency room. In the elevator, the old man's heartbeat was very fast, and I felt every sound. At that moment, I was touched in a way that I can't describe. What's funny is that the doctor in the emergency room did not calm the old man's emotions first and then provide treatment as I expected. He said, "Don't talk to me, don't splash blood on me!", telling the old man to calm down and not be afraid. I will leave these tasks to me. I have no comment on this doctor. Later, the old man escaped safely, and he thanked me again and again when I left.

Chestnut 2: Encounter on the bridge: A few years ago, I met an old man who fell down on the bridge to the park. I quickly stepped forward to help him up. It turned out that the old man was a beggar. I thought to myself, this is bad! The old man did not blackmail me, but was very grateful. However, he held my hand and refused to let me go. This was a very embarrassing situation. No matter what I said, I had to do something to ease the situation, so I had a chat with my grandfather and asked him where he lived. The old man said that he was from Anhui and was homeless and needed help. He took out a wallet with a crocodile brand from his pocket and said that his ID card was inside. I picked up the ID card and took a look. Fortunately, I was literate and it was clearly written on the ID card that I was a local (my hometown). So I also took out my wallet, searched for fake unknown brands on Taobao, and told the old man that his wallet was a famous brand! Then the old man chatted with me, sharing his reasons for begging and some interesting anecdotes... This led to me later meeting an old woman who asked me for money. I told her something like, "Is your son unfilial? Is your daughter-in-law making you suffer? Why don't you make some money if you are idle and bored?" The old woman smiled from ear to ear. I invited her to drink a cup of milk tea and told her that it is not easy for us young people too, and there are a lot of them. I saw her many times after that, and every time she would greet me warmly and say a few simple hellos. In both of the above examples, I was not blackmailed. This can only illustrate my personal experience and cannot be used to infer general probabilities. I am not writing this blog to express a sense of moral superiority. The main point is that we ourselves will grow old, and we don’t want someone to fall and have no one to help. When a life needs your support, you will feel a different responsibility. A very simple summary is: do what you can, and help whenever you can. When encountering an emergency, ensure the safety of both parties first, contact local first aid, and do not do anything beyond the scope of your training.

Original comment: BanYuner: This depends on the age group. College students may help, but if you are about 40 years old, it is probably a bit hard to say. zb.gs Reply: Yes, this can only depend on your own situation, but I advocate helping the elderly

items.core: Divide all templates according to starting point, ability training, AI collaboration, work delivery, review and recovery to help readers establish a complete closed loop of action with minimum records.
body: Answer first: Where am I stuck now? : · Current stuck point · First tool · Then open · This tool cannot prove anything for you · · There are many tools and I don’t know how to actually fill them in · Practical use of the toolbox · Learning status · Synthetic examples cannot prove that the same plan is suitable for you · · Don’t know the goal or baseline · Learning status · English proficiency diagnosis · Can’t decide the right direction for you · · Prepare for overseas positions, English interviews or remote collaboration · Job hunting English evidence card · Job-seeking English · Offers cannot be guaranteed, nor can a grade be turned into a unified recruitment line · · Want to start a 90-day cycle · Ninety-day action list · Rhythm ledger · There is no guarantee that the plan will be successful or sustainable · · Repeated interruptions in the weekly rhythm · Rhythm ledger · Weekly review · Cannot explain fatigue, illness or responsibility as laziness · · There are samples but it is impossible to tell whether there is a real change · Chain of evidence · Evidence chapter · Can’t push a successful performance into a stable ability · · Feelings after reading, but don’t know if anything will be left after seven days · Reader’s practice receipt · Chain of evidence · Can’t push a personal experience into a general effect · · Helping children in junior middle school to learn · Family learning mutual agreement · Family learning chapter · Can’t choose life for the child, replace school or diagnose difficulties · · Recognize words but not use them · Vocabulary evidence card · Vocabulary chapter · The number of cards cannot be used to replace the performance in the context · · The rules seem to be understood, but the real expressions still make mistakes repeatedly · Grammar evidence cards · Grammar articles · One correction, style preference or AI polishing cannot be regarded as stable grammatical ability · · Collected a lot of sounds...

String the tools into a closed loop: When using the toolbox for the first time, you can first go through the cross-session AI learning synthesis case. Do not fill out the entire template at once. In the following order, only the most necessary piece of evidence is left at each step: Positioning: use learning status or English proficiency diagnosis to write down the real scenario, current baseline and completion standards; Selection: If the cycle is longer, use a ninety-day action list; if it is only scheduled for this week, use a rhythm ledger; Practice: select vocabulary, grammar, listening, reading, speaking or writing evidence cards according to tasks; if the goal is a job interview, use job search English evidence cards to include unfamiliar questioning and asynchronous writing, and complete your first version first; Collaboration: required When AI is used, first fill in the AI task brief, and then write the collaboration process and performance after turning off AI into the AI learning record; Delivery: use the work briefing and delivery card when there is a real audience, and use the AI project score card to record quality, cost, risk and rollback after release or pilot; Review: use the evidence chain to put together the first version, immediate performance, delayed maintenance and migration, and then use weekly review to decide which condition to change only; Receipts: If the action is from a chapter in the book, use reader practice receipts to record which parts actually went into action and which parts still don’t work. This is a round trip path. If risks, reduced capacity, or insufficient evidence are found at any step, you can go back to the previous step to reduce the task; going back is not a waste, but makes the next action more credible.

Three Rules of Use: Only Track What Will Change Your Decision If one number doesn't help you decide to continue, downshift, change variables, or stop, there's no need to keep track of it long-term. The purpose of recording is not to fill the page, but to make the next step clear. The first version must be completed by humans as much as possible. The baseline, first version and independent retest in the template should be completed before AI is involved or after AI is turned off. Tools can help explain, compare, and point out problems, but they can't help you feel like "I already know it." Records must maintain boundaries. Do not paste passwords, IDs, precise addresses, customer information, medical privacy, or unauthorized third-party content into templates or models. When it comes to health, safety, legal, financial and ongoing loss of control, first contact a qualified professional or trusted advocate.
A minimal start: just do four lines today:

The real problem I'm trying to solve now:
Baseline evidence I already have:
Minimal output I want to complete in 25–45 minutes:
After completion I will save the evidence in:

After completion, choose the tool closest to the task and give it a date and next review time. Don’t wait for all the columns to be filled before you start; after you start, the gaps will become concrete. Related entrances: Toolbox Practice | Reading Guide: Putting Books Back into Life | Index of Terms and Methods | Rhythm Chapter: Let Small Things Travel Through Time

items.title: Toolbox Practice: Let AI continue a 90-day learning across sessions
items.core: Use a Python learning case clearly marked as a synthetic demonstration to fully demonstrate the learning status, AI task briefing, independent baseline, works, evidence chain, weekly review and reader receipt.
body: This is not a success story: the learners in the demonstration have these settings: Can understand variables, conditions and simple loops, but cannot complete a small program independently; Can invest stably four times a week for 45 minutes each time; The ninety-day goal is to independently complete a command line tool that reads CSV, checks data and outputs a summary; does not upload company data, does not let AI ghostwrite the final work, and does not need to stay up late to make up for interruptions; If the core code is still unable to be explained on the fourteenth day, no framework and new courses will be added. These conditions are demonstration boundaries only. Your starting point, time, body, job, and goals may be completely different.

Scenario: Why planning causes amnesia: The initial mistake was to leave everything in one chat window: Let the AI ​​make a twelve-week plan; Ask questions, practice, and modify the code in the same session every day; Rely on the above to remember errors, progress, and next steps; After the context is too long, new answers begin to mix into old tasks; When changing sessions, re-introduce yourself with a large paragraph of memories. The problem isn't just context length. There is no stable version of the chat history, and there is no clear distinction between "completed facts", "AI's explanation" and "next time hypothesis". True learning shouldn’t be trapped in any one tool or session.

What each of the five tools does: · Tool · Responsibility in this case · What is not responsible for · · Learning status · Save cross-session facts, evidence, errors, boundaries and next tasks · Do not save every sentence of chat · · AI task briefing · Constrain this 45-minute task, input, help method and acceptance · Do not develop an entire life plan · · Evidence chain · Compare independent baselines, auxiliary versions, delayed retests and migrations · Do not use a score to prove "learned" · · Weekly review · Change only one variable based on the week's evidence · Do not write a bad state as a personality conclusion · · Reader's practice receipt · Record whether this method is really put into action and where it still does not work · No requirement to disclose privacy or rate the book · If it is the first time to use the toolbox, follow this page to complete the week first, do not open all the other templates at the same time.
Step 1: Put the state outside the session: Learners first create python-learning-state.md instead of using the AI session as memory:

# Learning State — python-90d-v1

Update date: 2026-09-02
Ninety-day scenario: Independently deliver a CSV digest command line tool with the ability to account for input validation, error handling, and testing.
Current baseline: Can write variables, if, and for; cannot independently read CSV, split functions, or write tests.
Available capacity: 45 minutes each on Monday, Wednesday, Friday, Sunday.
There is evidence: baseline/day-01.py; an error is reported in the null value line after running.
Repeated mistakes: look at the answer first; mistake the ability to run for the ability to explain; cannot determine the cause after modifying multiple variables.
Boundary: No real company data is used; submit your own version first; do not make up classes after 23:00.
Current Phase: Calibration Days 1–14.
The next minimal task: read a 12-row synthetic CSV, skipping blank rows, and output the number of valid rows and the total amount.
Completion criteria: Standalone version can run; I can explain each function; save at least one failing test.
Stop condition: The state will be saved after 45 minutes, no need to stay up all night to complete.
The state file only retains content that will change the next action. Course excerpts, full chats and all details of each attempt are placed in the evidence folder and not crammed into a status page.
Step 2: Give the AI ​​only one task at a time: Do not ask the AI ​​to "remember me" when a new session starts. Only submit the latest status and this task briefing:

The following is my learning status file. Please start by restating the version, goals, current evidence, major errors, boundaries, and next tasks in no more than 6 bullet points, pointing out conflicts or gaps. Do not fill in facts that are not in the document.

This time there is only one task: read the synthesized CSV, skip the blank lines, and output the number of valid lines and the total amount.
Process: Let me submit the independent version first; you can point out at most 3 problems that affect the results without directly giving the complete code; after I modify it, I will check it with two tests. At the end of the 45 minutes, five updates are output: "Complete, Evidence, Error/Risk, Handover, Next Step".
The first job of AI is to retell the state, not to lecture immediately. When retelling an error, fix the status or prompt first, and do not continue to generate plans based on the erroneous premise.

Step 3: Make a baseline first, then ask for help: The standalone version in the synthesis demo yielded the following results: · Conditions · Result · Evidence · · 25 minutes, without looking at answers · Can read normal lines; empty amounts cause exceptions; all logic is written in a function · evidence/week-01/baseline.py · · AI only points out three problems · Identify null check, function responsibility and missing tests · evidence/week-01/feedback.md · · After modification · Passed normal line and blank line tests; still not processing the illegal amount format · evidence/week-01/revision.py · This is not "AI wrote the program for me". A more accurate record is: the standalone version exposed three issues, AI helped classify them, the learner fixed two of them, and the third moved on to the next task. If you ask for the complete code from the beginning, the final file may be more beautiful, but you will lose the baseline and no way of knowing which part of the ability belongs to the learner.

Step 4: Put the work into the evidence chain: Do not save the conclusion of "learned CSV" in the first week, but record four time points: · Time point · Condition · Synthetic result · Still can't explain anything · · Baseline · No AI, 25 minutes · 1/3 acceptance conditions passed · Cannot explain understanding of error handling · · After immediate assistance · Read three pieces of feedback · 2/3 passed, can explain two functions · Cannot explain that it will still be written after a few days · · Delayed retest on the 7th day · Don’t look at the old code, change to a CSV with the same structure · 2/3 passed; missed the illegal amount again · Cannot explain that it can cope with new fields · · Migration · Add currency field · Can locate the location of changes, currency verification is not completed · It means that the structure has started to be migrated, but the prerequisite knowledge is insufficient · This result does not have full marks, but it is more informative than "persisting for a week". Rather than adding pandas, web frameworks, and databases, the next variant is specifically practicing input validation and failure testing.
Step 5: Continue in a new session: Weekend review only writes back the content of the changed decision to the state file:

# Learning State — python-90d-v2

Update date: 2026-09-08
Completed: CSV normal row and blank row processing; split into two functions: read_rows / summarize.
Evidence: week-01/baseline.py; revision.py; day-07-retest.py; tests.md.
Delayed results: 2/3 conditions were still completed on the 7th day; illegal amount verification failed again.
Major bugs: Missing tests for error paths; stopping inspection prematurely after seeing normal output.
Retention boundaries: synthesize data; answer independently first; stop at 45 minutes; do not make up for missed time.
Next minimal task: first write three failing tests, then implement parse_amount.
Completion criteria: There are clear results for the three types of inputs: null values, letters, and negative numbers; the design choices can be explained verbally.
Next review: 2026-09-15.

Old sessions can be closed. New conversations only require v2 and relevant evidence locations, no need to paste tens of thousands of chat words. The AI ​​does not track learning across sessions; the state file does the tracking and the AI ​​reads and serves it.
Step 6: Fill out the reader receipt after seven days: Synthetic demos also need to check: whether the toolbox itself helped the action.

Entering the question: Not sure how new AI sessions will continue on the three-month plan.
Practical actions: Establish a versioned learning state; complete a small CSV task; save independent versions and retest.
Stay after seven days: You can write status v2 without looking at the original session, and continue an explicit task in the new session.
Migration failure: I know I want to save the errors, but I still don’t know how to classify them.
Most helpful: Five examples of tool responsibilities and status documents.
Still abstract: Stage thresholds require more examples of different goals.
Cannot be rolled out: This process ensures that employment requirements will be met after ninety days.
This receipt is first saved in private notes. Only consider submitting a public version after removing paths, identities, and sensitive content.
If a week is interrupted: The status file does not require that all schedules be made up. The first step after a hiatus is to write the facts:

The hiatus fact: No practice for seven days.
Evidence of reasons: working overtime twice; feeling unwell once; not completing the retest.
What not to do: No cramming four classes into a weekend, no staying up late to pay them back.
Regression action: run the last test, write a failure case, update the status file.
24-Hour Completion Criteria: Save failed tests and next 25-minute entry.
Recovery itself can be the outcome of the week if health, safety, work responsibilities or relationships need to be prioritized. Plans serve life and do not ask life to apologize for plans.

1. First review the status version, goals, evidence, errors, boundaries and next tasks I submitted.
2. Point out conflicts and deficiencies without speculating on unwritten history.
3. I will only deal with one minimal task this time. Let me submit the independent version first.
4. Give feedback on up to three issues that affect the results, distinguishing between observations, explanations and suggestions.
5. Don’t give complete answers unless I specifically request it.
6. Output at the end: completion, evidence, errors/risks, handover, next step.
7. All long-term status is based on documentation and does not claim to remember other sessions.

Conversation protocol that you can copy directly: This protocol does not guarantee that the AI ​​will never go wrong. It makes errors easier to detect and allows learners to retain ownership of the problem, status, and final judgment.

What this demonstration proved and what it still hasn’t proved: it shows that five tools can form a clear handover: the state is saved outside the session, the task is reduced, the independent version is separated from the auxiliary version, there is a retest after seven days, and there is a reliable entrance to the new session. It does not prove: This synthetic character will persist for ninety days; The difficulty of this task is suitable for every beginner; Using AI will definitely lead to faster learning than without AI; Completing the command line tool is equivalent to having real job ability; One week's results can represent long-term migration. When it comes to real use, keep your baseline, work, time, costs, and failures to yourself. The example shows how to fill it out, and reality determines whether it is useful.

Conclusion: Leave the memory to the file and leave the judgment to yourself: a long-term study should not be lost just because the chat window is closed, nor should it be pretended to have continuity just because the chat window is very long. Let the state file remember what happened, let the evidence save the version you actually made, and let the next session only take on the next step. Tools can be changed, models can be updated, and plans can be scaled back. As long as you still know where you're coming from, what's unproven, and where the next task is, learning isn't locked into any one conversation. Related entrances: Learning status ｜ AI task briefing ｜ Evidence chain ｜ Reader practice receipt

items.title: Evidence chain template
items.core: Use a worksheet across English, AI, project and life practice to connect baseline, immediate performance, delayed maintenance, migration and next decision-making.
body:
Recording start date:
Real scenarios and audiences/users:
Only questions answered this time:
Completion criteria:
Possible risks and stopping conditions:

1. First define the question to be answered: the question must be observable, such as "Can I describe the project risks in English and answer a follow-up question without a manuscript?" Do not write "Have I become better?"

2. Save unmodified baseline: Baseline should occur before AI, peer feedback or intensive training as much as possible. Document conditions to avoid hiding tools, extra time, and familiarity materials in comparisons. · Date · Tasks and limitations · Whether tool was used · Results/errors · Original evidence location · · · · No · · ·

What I was able to accomplish independently at baseline:
Where do I stop or need tips:
What the baseline cannot explain:

3. Record real-time performance: Real-time performance shows what happened under the current conditions this time, and does not automatically mean that the ability has stabilized. · Date · Conditions and prompts · What was accomplished · Quality/time taken/rework · Location of evidence · If using AI, please write clearly what it did and what you accomplished independently with the AI ​​turned off. Chat records can be used as traces of the process, but cannot be used as proof of ability alone.

4. Do a delayed hold: wait for a period of time, remove the recent prompts and original answers, and then complete similar tasks. The time interval is determined by the task and personal capacity, but it must be written clearly.

Retest date:
Since last practice:
Which prompts have been removed:
Similar tasks:
Independent results:
Error still occurs:
Evidence location:

5. Do a migration: keep the core action and change at least one condition: topic, audience, time limit, materials, tool permissions, or task purpose. · Changed conditions · New tasks · Independent results · How the other party/user understands · Location of evidence · Transfer failure does not mean that the previous exercise has no value. It means you need to reduce the magnitude of the change, add prerequisite knowledge, or redefine the completion criteria.

Facts: I can point to date, condition, sample, source, or direct observation.
Interpretation: How I understand these facts; it may need revision.
Hypothesis: A judgment that I am prepared to test in my next action.
Conclusions that cannot be drawn:

6. Separate facts, explanations and hypotheses: For example, "The independent version was completed in 90 seconds" is a record; "Because my sleep has improved, I can express it more clearly" is an explanation; "It can still be completed with an unfamiliar audience next week, which means that the changes may be effective" is a hypothesis to be tested.

This piece of evidence best supports: continue/downshift/change variables/pause or stop
I only changed one condition:
Next minimal task:
Completion criteria for the next task:
Support, authorization or professional judgment required:
Next review date:

7. Let the evidence determine next steps: If the evidence conflicts, don’t hide the conflict with averages. Write down the different conditions first, and then decide whether to make up a sample. When evidence is weak, narrowing the question is often more honest than producing an exact score.

Main questions and completion standards:
The most reliable evidence:
Least reliable or still missing evidence:
Recurring mistakes/risks:
Next minimal task and stopping condition:
Evidence folder or link:

8. Handover summary: When handing this summary to your future self, companion, or AI, ask the other party to work only based on this record, and do not pretend to remember other conversations, or make up facts that do not exist. Related chapters: Evidence: How to see changes ｜ Toolbox overview ｜ Rhythm ledger ｜ Index of terms and methods

items.title: Reader practice receipt: What is left after seven days
items.core: Use two private-first records to put the reading entrance, actual actions, immediate results, delayed retention, migration failure and manuscript feedback on the same page, and then decide whether to share it publicly.
body: Do it privately first: A useful response only needs to answer four things: What is the real problem I’m facing? What did I actually do rather than just agree to? Can I do it again after three to seven days when the prompts decrease or conditions change? Which passages aid action, and which passages remain abstract, out-of-bounds, or unusable? Even if there is no action or retest, you can still fill it out truthfully. "Only a sense of identity for the time being" is evidence in itself, and there is no need to write a supplementary success story.
First fill-in: ten minutes after reading: enter question

Date:
Chapter or page:
Why I opened it:
The real scene at that time:
What you already know before reading:
Where to get stuck before reading:
Available time and capacity today:

Don’t write “I want to be great.” Write a scenario that can happen, for example: "I need to hand over project risks to colleagues, but the existing records are only chats and scattered screenshots." Retell it in your own words. Close the page and write in no more than three sentences:

Core judgments I understand:
Facts, examples or sources on which it is based:
It still can't prove anything for me:

If you can only copy the original sentence, don't rush to evaluate the quality first. Writing "I can't explain it in my own words yet" would be more accurate than a nice excerpt. Do a Minimal Action Choose an action that will take you 10–45 minutes to complete. Actions must leave visible traces.

The smallest action I want to complete:
Completion criteria:
Whether to use AI/help from others:
The part I had to decide for myself:
Work, sound recording, code or recording location:
Stop condition:

Available actions include: rewrite an email, record a description, fix a test, create a page of learning status, delete an invalid requirement, or confirm boundaries with an affected person. Continuing to collect information does not count as an action. Save instant results

What actually gets done:
What was not accomplished:
Direct feedback or results received:
Biggest error/resistance:
The most easily exaggerated conclusion right now:
Next retest date:
Immediate success can only explain what happened under the current conditions this time. If you use AI, please save the auxiliary version and the independent version with AI turned off separately.
Second filling: three to seven days later: Do not reread, retest first. Do not open the original chapter, chat history or answers yet. Complete a similar task, then fill in:

Retest date and interval:
Which prompts have been removed:
Similar tasks:
What I accomplished independently:
What tips do I still need:
What's really left compared to the first time:
Evidence location:

If you can’t remember it at all, don’t change the failure to “too busy lately”. Record the facts first, then decide whether the task is too big, the entry point is unclear, or the content only creates short-term recognition. Change one condition Migration only changes one condition: topic, audience, time limit, materials, tool permissions, or task purpose. · Changed conditions · New tasks · Independent results · Where the failure occurred · Next steps · A failed migration is not a bad review. It can point out the boundaries of a method's applicability, and can also help authors distinguish between "sentences that sound correct" and "readers can actually use them." When writing feedback on a manuscript, please try to point to specific paragraphs, titles, examples, or tools:

What helped me take action the most:
Still abstract or don't know how to use it:
Missing bounds, examples, or preconditions:
One thing that could be deleted or shortened:
The part that didn't work after I tried:
Questions I hope the next edition answers:

"Well written" makes the author happy, but makes it difficult to change for the next edition. "I followed step three, but I don't know how to write the completion criteria" is more valuable for editing.

Separate facts, explanations and wishes: Before sharing, check whether the three layers are mixed together: · Layers · Examples · · Facts · I did not read the original text after seven days, completed two requirements, and the third item required prompts · · Explanation · Maybe because the examples made me remember the structure, but the boundary part is still abstract · · Desires · I hope to add a fully filled sample in the next edition · Don't write a personal result as "it will work for everyone", and don't write a failure as "this method is completely useless". Keep the tasks, conditions and samples, and the conclusions will have boundaries.

Privacy gate before sharing: Only after all have been passed, will it be considered public: [ ] Passwords, keys, credentials, precise addresses, and private contact information have been removed; [ ] Customer data, company secrets, medical records, and undisclosed financial information have been removed; [ ] Unnecessary third-party names, photos, relationships, and identifiable details have been removed; [ ] Content involving others has been authorized, or rewritten to the minimum facts that cannot be identified; [ ] Direct observations, personal explanations, and next-level assumptions have been distinguished; [ ] I accept that this record may be publicly available and searchable for an extended period of time. If any item cannot be confirmed, keep it in a private note. Authors don't need to gain your privacy to improve a book.

When to switch to the chain of evidence: Reader's receipt is suitable for answering "Did this reading lead to action?" When the same capability requires comparison of multiple samples, scoring conditions, delayed retention, and cross-scenario migration, transfer records to the evidence chain template. If you need to see a complete fill-in process, first read Toolbox in Action: Let AI Continue a 90-Day Learning Across Sessions. It uses synthetic data to demonstrate how to string together learning status, AI tasks, works, retests, and this receipt. After completing the privacy check, you can choose to submit a public reader receipt. Being public or not does not change the value of this exercise. Related entries: Case: Let this book prove its method ｜ Toolbox overview ｜ Weekly review

items.title: Family learning mutual agreement: fourteen days, making help negotiable
items.core: Establish a private, non-legal fourteen-day mutual agreement for learners and parents who are roughly in the junior high school stage, clarifying goals, roles, school requirements, capacity, AI and data boundaries, feedback and suspension conditions.
body: 1. Write separately and then read together: Learners write first

What real thing do I hope will be easier in two weeks:
What I've been able to accomplish so far:
Where I stop most often:
Which kind of help works for me:
Which kind of help makes it harder for me to start or to tell the truth:
The time and capacity I can afford today:
Parents/guardians write again

Specific facts I observed:
What worries me the most:
Which concerns are supported by evidence:
Which parts are still just speculation on my part:
What time, space, equipment or communication support I can provide:
Supervisory, acting or public actions that I promise not to do:
Not to refute immediately when read together. First repeat the other person's meaning in one sentence until the other person thinks it is basically accurate.

Only questions answered in fourteen days:
In which school or life setting did it take place:
The school clearly requires:
Child’s own completion standards:
Boundaries of safety and responsibility that adults must protect:
What results would allow us to continue:
What consequences would cause us to shrink, pause, or stop:

2. Written as a common problem: Common problems should allow for failure. For example: "Can you independently repeat the gist of a similar article in two weeks" is more likely to retain true results than "Vocabulary must increase by 500".
3. Save the starting point: · Date · Task and constraints · Learner independent results · Where the prompt appears · Original evidence location ·

The starting point can state:
The starting point still cannot be explained:
Only one condition changed this time:
Adults can help save the file and not give full answers until the baseline is completed.
4. Three capacity buckets: · Bucket · Applicability · Learner retained action · Adult retained support · · Full day · · · · Compressed day · · · · · Recovery day · · · ·

Latest end time:
Clarify the content that will not be made up:
Minimum return action within 24 hours after interruption:
The recovery day may have no study work. Safety, basic care, communication and preparation for the next entrance can be all part of the day's results.

5. Adult support list: In these two weeks, adults only choose two to three items: [ ] Provide a time box that is not interrupted randomly; [ ] Prepare school-specified materials or necessary equipment; [ ] Help contact teachers or confirm homework requirements; [ ] Provide up to three specific feedbacks after children submit the first version; [ ] Remind once at the agreed time without repeated questioning; [ ] Help save versions and next steps; [ ] Actively agree to downshift or pause when capacity decreases. Adults clearly do not do: [ ] Do not write for others, answer for them, or ask for their children’s signature after letting AI do it for them; [ ] Do not check the screen, chat history, or minute-by-minute status; [ ] Do not send your work, results, or failures to unrelated relatives, friends, or public platforms; [ ] Do not humiliate comparisons with classmates, siblings, or past highlight moments; [ ] Do not stay up late, cancel basic rest, or continue conflict repayment plans.

Allowed platforms and accounts:
The current age/custody rules of the platform have been checked: Yes / No / Not applicable
Whether the school allows the use of AI for this task:
AI can do: questions/explanations/feedback/parallel exercises/others
AI cannot do:
The child must first submit a standalone version:
Evidence to keep after each use:
Retelling or independent actions after the session:

6. AI and data agreement: Never upload: [ ] Name, school, class, ID, precise address and private contact information; [ ] Face, voiceprint, health, family relationship and non-minimized performance records; [ ] Private information or unauthorized works of teachers, classmates and other third parties; [ ] Internal school accounts, test paper answers, restricted materials or sensitive family information. If boundaries cannot be identified by the platform, school, or family, start by using pen and paper, offline materials, synthetic data, or teacher-approved alternatives.

Only one main question is kept at a time:
Adults can provide up to a few pieces of feedback:
How learners can reject or pursue feedback:
Which fact should be confirmed first when a disagreement arises:
When it is necessary to ask teachers to participate:
7. Feedback rules: Feedback sentence pattern:

I observed:
Its impact on tasks:
What I'm not sure about is:
I suggest next time just test:
Avoid "you just..." "you never..." and "everyone else can...".

8. Fourteen days of evidence: · Time points · Conditions · Independent results · Feedback obtained · Still unknown · · Day 1 baseline · · · · · · Immediate revision · · · · · · Delayed retest · · · · · · Migration to new conditions · · · · · Chat duration, check-in days, and number of parent reminders are just traces of the process. Key judgments should be made back to the work, title, recording, classroom use and performance after prompts are removed.

Pause immediately when any safety, physical, sleep, emotional, school or family situation arises:
Trusted adult your child can contact first:
School contact portal:
Local professional or emergency support portal:
Content that does not need to be reworked after the timeout:

9. Timeout and help door: When there is continued functional impairment, harmful thoughts, violence, bullying, threats, or inability to communicate safely, first protect safety and seek appropriate support. Do not use this table to diagnose or deal with it yourself.
10. Two-week review: Learners say first: Learners

One thing that really becomes easier:
One thing you still don't know or need to be prompted for:
Most useful support:
Supervision that was least valuable or made me uncomfortable:
Next steps I would like to take:
Parents/Guardians

Works and Facts I Observed:
What controls or invalid requirements have I reduced:
The parts I'm still concerned about but don't have enough evidence for yet:
Next round I only keep support:
Co-decision

Continue/Narrow/Change a condition/Pause or stop:
Basis:
Next minimal task:
Next review date:
Matters that require the involvement of teachers or professionals:

End: Help must also be reviewed: Families usually review whether the child has completed the task, and rarely review whether the adult's help is effective. This agreement requires both parties to leave evidence: whether the child's tasks are clearer, whether adult support reduces friction, and whether the relationship is still capable of telling the truth. When help is reduced to monitoring, acting and anxious delivery, it too needs to be scaled back or stopped. Good support may not necessarily make a child do more immediately, but it will gradually make him better able to see problems, express needs, take on his own version, and know who to turn to when difficulties arise. items.title: Learning Status Template
items.core: Use a one-page status file to save goals, baselines, completed content, error evidence, and next steps, so that both humans and AI can continue working across sessions.
body: If you only have five minutes today: don’t fill out the entire sheet first. Copy the minimum version below and take action after writing it; only add the complete template when the task requires cross-session, handover or review.

The completion standard for the smallest version is: another future self can understand what needs to be solved now, what is already known, what to do next, and what boundaries cannot be crossed. It is not a complete plan, nor is it a substitute for independent retesting; it simply allows the action to happen first.

The following is my study status file. Begin by restating the status version, goals, current evidence, major errors, boundaries, and next steps in no more than 6 bullet points. Point out conflicts or gaps in information. Do not pretend to remember other sessions or fill in facts that are not in the document. Then design the exercise only once for the "next minimum task": let me answer it first, and then give feedback according to the completion criteria; don't give the complete answer directly unless I ask for it. At the end, five updates of "this completion, evidence, errors/risks, handover, and next step" that can be pasted back into the status file are output.

[Paste Learning State]

AI cross-session recovery prompt word: The AI-generated state summary is not a source of truth. Each time you restore, the files, works, sources and version numbers you have saved shall prevail; after completing a weekly review, update the weekly review, evidence chain and ninety-day action summary according to file responsibilities, and do not copy the same record.

items.title: Rhythm Ledger Template
items.core: Record main issues, minimum actions under different capacities, effective feedback, repeated resistance and next condition adjustment every week, so that the growth rhythm can be reviewed, downshifted, and returned.
body:
Date range:
Just answer one question this week:
Real scene and audience:

Baseline evidence at the beginning of the week:

1. Main question of the week: The main question should be observable, such as "Can I explain the risks of a project in English and answer follow-up questions without a manuscript?" Don't write "Get better this week."

2. Three capacity versions: · Capacity · When to use · Minimal action · Evidence that must be left behind · Stop or downshift conditions · · Full day · Time and energy are relatively stable · · · · Compressed day · Time becomes less or attention is chopped · · · · · Recovery day · Sickness, insomnia, sadness or a sudden increase in responsibilities · · · · The three versions serve the same direction. Recovery days are not failures; when safety, sleep, body, or relationships are significantly affected, protecting those bottom lines takes precedence over completing the plan.

3. Repeat with echoes: · Date · What action was performed · Memories/variations/outputs/feedback · What is the new information · Which variable to change next time · If four consecutive repetitions do not produce new information, change the subject, audience, time limit, number of prompts, or tool permissions first, don’t just increase the number.

items.title: Weekly Review Template
items.core: Review the week with completed evidence, quality, retention and migration, and only determine the most important adjustments for the next week.
body: Weekly Review Template Review is not to judge yourself, but to leave a more accurate starting point for the next week. Set aside 20 minutes each week to look at the evidence, then explain why, and then change just one variable. Do not write passwords, customer data, medical privacy, or unauthorized third-party information.

items.title: English proficiency diagnosis: four baselines and transfer records
items.core: Save listening, speaking, reading and writing first version, conditions, errors, feedback, delayed retest and CEFR under the same authentic topic direction, avoid substituting average scores or polished finished products for evidence of competency.
body:
# English Diagnostic - YYYY-MM-DD

Real scenes: work/study/job hunting/life/others
Real topic:
Target audience or conversational audience:
Four common minimum deliverables:
Diagnosis start/end date:
Materials, editions and sources:
Common constraints (time, equipment, environment):
Allowed dictionaries / subtitles / translation / search / AI / human help:
Privacy, Copyright, Examination, Professional Responsibility Boundaries:
Day 7 Parallel Task Dates:
Retest date on the 30th day:
Week 12 Actual Assignment Date:

1. Define the diagnostic boundaries first: The four items do not have to use the exact same material, but the topic, difficulty, time, and completion criteria should be comparable. If the real goal is a job, don't let a comprehensive grade replace the specific language actions in the job description.

2. Four tasks for the first edition: Try not to look up words or let AI write or answer for you in the first edition. Complete it first, then mark where you need help. · Competencies · Recommended first edition · Minimum delivery · · Listening · Listen to 2-4 minutes of authentic audio once · Write main idea, 3 identifying details, responsibility/next step and retell 60 seconds · · Reading · Read 600-1000 words of authentic text · Write five main lines, an evidence location, a question or unknown · · Speaking · Without reading the transcript 2 minutes of explanation, experience or process · The audience can restate the purpose, key facts, and next steps · · Writing · 20 minutes to complete a 180-250 word email, note, or essay · The audience knows the conclusion, rationale, limitations, and actions · Don’t shave off real-task differences to make the four “fair.” Diagnostics show the conditions under which capabilities operate, not create a nice table of averages.

2A. Record collaboration dimensions as needed: If your goals include remote collaboration, customer communication, classroom discussions, or home learning, then complete the following tasks. They are not new levels, and they do not have to be measured every time; evidence is only preserved if they actually affect the results in reality. · Task dimensions · 10–15 minute sample · Evidence location and results · · Paraphrasing and mediation · Read two short pieces of material with different positions, explaining their respective claims, differences and unknowns · The audience can distinguish the original text, your paraphrase and your inference; · · Online interaction · Write a progress, a blockage and the next step so that the other party can continue without a meeting · The other party knows the person in charge, time and missing information; · · Misunderstanding repair · Ask for clarification, and then restate the consensus and open issues · The other party confirms that the retelling is accurate and the next step has not been changed due to speculation; · If one of the items is a high-risk section, do not replace it with a speaking or writing score. Save samples and audience feedback for next parallel assignment.

3. Save First Edition and Conditions: · Competencies · First Edition Position · Start/End · Tools & Tips · Completed/Unfinished · What I’m Most Unsure about · · Listening · · · · · · Reading · · · · · · · · Speaking · · · · · · · Writing · · · · · ·

Things that I can still explain independently after the first edition:
If I redo it, the conditions I would most like to change:
Conclusions that cannot be deduced from the first edition:

4. Score by impact, not by feeling: 0-2 points for each item: 0=no evidence or incomplete, 1=partially completed, dependent on prompts, or unstable, 2=complete independently under current conditions. Write the evidence position for each score. · Competence · Task Accomplishment · Comprehensibility · Accuracy and Range · Organization/Fluency · Independence and Transfer · Evidence Rationale · · Listening · · · · · · · · Reading · · · · · · · · Speaking · · · · · · · · · Writing · · · · · · · Score Interpretation Task completion: whether the information and intention are reached, and whether the action can be continued; Comprehensibility: whether the real reader/listener does not need to overguess; Accuracy and scope: whether the vocabulary, grammar, pronunciation, spelling, and details support the task; Organization/Flow: whether the structure, order, pauses, or layout hinder use; Independence and transfer: whether the recent prompt is removed, whether a condition is changed, and whether the task can be completed again. The total score is only used for longitudinal comparison of the same person, not personality, intelligence or employment qualifications. For the CEFR direction, please combine the CEFR goals with the English proficiency self-test, and do not write a single diagnosis as a permanent level.

5. Select only one top barrier for each: · Ability · Top Barrier · Sample/Time Period · Task Impact · Next Minimum Fix · Correspondence Evidence Card · · Listening · Vocabulary/Sounds/Syntax/Context/Attention/Equipment · · · · Listening Evidence Card · · Reading · Vocabulary/Structure/Context/Evidence/Layout/Capacity · · · · Reading Evidence Cards · · Speaking · Chunks/Pronunciation/Organization/Interaction/Register/Questioning · · · · Speaking Evidence Cards · · Writing · Tasks/Facts/Structures/Sentences/Register/Delivery · · · · Writing Evidence Cards · If an obstacle cannot be pointed to a sample or time period, do not conclude it yet. One can "know many words" but fail at listening segmentation, or one can be grammatically accurate but fail to organize asynchronous handoffs.

items.title: Listening evidence card: from playback duration to meaning reconstruction
items.core: Saving material conditions, first listening without subtitles, six-layer error map, subtitle scaffolding, meaning reconstruction, action output and delayed transfer, to avoid mistaking collections, playback times or smooth reading for listening ability.
body:
# Listening Evidence — YYYY-MM-DD

Real scene:
Task: grasp the main idea/find details/track relationships/execute actions/enter interaction/migrate
What you need to answer, decide or do after listening:
Completion criteria:

Recording, uploading, rewriting and sharing permission:
1. Define the boundaries between tasks and reality: Training can remove the scaffolding, and real work cannot give up necessary safety confirmations in order to prove capabilities.

Main material title, source and access date:

At least keep the tasks and approximate difficulty similar.

First listening allowed: pause/double speed/subtitles/notes/replay
One sentence gist:
Three confirming details:

Uncertain time period:
Actions I take based on what I hear:

3. Save the first listening without subtitles: Do not overwrite the first listening with the second time or the answers after subtitles. It is the baseline for future comparisons.

4. One to three issues that most affect the task:

Automatic subtitle error:
What the Chinese translation helped:
The meaning of still triggering after closing the text:
Snippets that are only understood when subtitles are visible:

6. Make each pass produce different evidence: · Pass · Question · Output · Result · · 1 · What do I predict and what does the first listen recover? · Original gist and details · · · 2 · In which time period did the difference occur? · Timestamps and barrier layers · · · 3 · What does the minimal scaffold explain? · Mishearing, original text and reasons · · · 4 · Does the sound independently trigger the meaning after closing the stand? · Listening without words · · · 5 · How can I reframe and act? · Retelling / Process / Decision / Handover · · Number of plays is not the result. Three keywords:

Questions and answers from strangers:

7. From dictation and reading to generation: when the reading is smooth and the retelling is blank, reduce the length of imitation and increase keyword reconstruction; when every word is written correctly but the main idea cannot be expressed, return to structure and relationships.

Does it use original audio, auto-transcription, or my candidate transcription:
The error classification it raises:
Does it make up words, context, or speaker intent:
Teacher/Peer Verification:
Response, execution or repair results in real tasks:
What I accepted/rejected and why:

Is it better to request duplicates, confirm and leave consensus:
Only variables that will change in the next round:
