items.title: Reading Evidence Card: From Reading the Summary to Real Delivery
items.core: Save reading tasks, versions, first readings, obstacle maps, claim evidence, technical facts, multi-source comparisons, independent output and delayed transfer to avoid treating page numbers or summaries as comprehension.
body:
# Reading Evidence - YYYY-MM-DD

Real scene:
Tasks: Locate information/Understand arguments/Read technical documentation/Build endurance/Synthesize sources/Support decisions
Who needs to know, decide, implement or hand over something after reading:
Completion criteria:
Limited time:
Allowed dictionary/translation/search/notes/AI:
Copyright, privacy and preservation boundaries:
1. Define tasks, readers and boundaries: Write the completion criteria as results, such as "can run the minimum example in the current version", don't just write "finished".

2. Record the source and version: · Project · Main material · Parallel material · Whether it is comparable · · Author/maintainer, title, link · · · · Version, publication date or chapter · · · · Access date and text length · · · · · Author/institutional position or interest relationship · · · · Citations, images, codes and copyright boundaries · · · · · Theme, genre and difficulty · · · · The webpage will be revised, paid for or removed from the shelves. Save necessary citation information and do not copy the entire article without permission.

First reading conditions:
First reading time:
Whether to search word by word:
One sentence gist:
How to advance articles/documents:
Three confirming details:
What the author/maintainer wants me to believe or accomplish:
A place that remains uncertain:
What actions will I take based on my current understanding:
3. Save the unedited first reading: Complete the first reading first, then look up the words or read the explanation. Don't overwrite it with a prettier translated summary.

4. Create a six-layer obstacle map: · Paragraph/page number · Where am I stuck · Obstacle layer · Task impact · Current action · · · · Vocabulary and grammar / Structure and direction / Background and schema / Argument and evidence / Layout and technology / Attention and capacity · Change of meaning / Task blocking / High frequency repetition / Comprehension effort / Low impact · ·

One to three obstacles that most affect the task:
Low-impact words and phrases to skip first:
Parts that may come from equipment, version, fatigue or environment:
If almost every sentence blocks the main idea, first change to easier parallel material or fill-in-the-field word blocks. Lowering the entrance does not mean lowering the target.
5. Draw claims, evidence and limitations: · Paragraph/page number · Paragraph function · Author’s claim · Original evidence/examples · Limitations, counterexamples or unknowns ·

Facts directly stated in the original text:
Inference supported by the original text:
My own judgment or association:
Evidence still missing:
What new evidence would change my judgment:
Separate “what the author said” from “whether I agree or not.” For technical, health, legal or financial content, go back to reliable primary sources or qualified professional advice.
6. Technical documentation fact card: If the material is an API, SDK, migration guide, command line help, error documentation, or README, add this page:

Target and applicable versions:
Prerequisites, permissions and environment:
Minimum input:
Expected output:
Actual output:
Default value, range, order, or side effect:
Failure conditions and error messages:
Limitations clearly stated in the documentation:
The part I'm still speculating on:
The next minimum test:

After reading the technical documentation but not running, hand-calculating, reproducing or confirming a minimal fact, it can only mean that you have read the page, but it does not mean that you have mastered it.

7. New words, word families and translation records: · word/expression · role in this task · found definition/word family/collocation · original text position · whether it can be interpreted after closing the tool · · · core / repetition / technology / low impact · · · ·

Translation helped me add background:
English structures, moods or limitations that may be obscured by translation:
Words I decided not to look up for now:

The number of unknown words is used to diagnose the difficulty of the material and does not directly determine the level. Word families help with guesswork and coverage, but derived words do not automatically equal available words.

Common questions:
Source A Definition, Date and Evidence:
Source B Definition, Date and Evidence:
Respective omission or interest relationship:
Which differences are facts and which are value judgments:

8. Multi-source comparison vs. real output: · Output · Audience · What I delivered · How the other party responded · Is the basis traceable · · Confirmation email / Minimal test / Verbal explanation / Decision memo / Handover · · · · · · After you have finished reading, prioritize testing your understanding with a reader, code, decision, or next task.

Tools/Feedbackers/Version and Date:
It sees the original text, my first reading, or my summary:
Missing locations it points out:
Does it confuse fact, inference, and style:
Teacher/peer/primary source verification:
What I accepted/rejected and why:

9. Documentation tools and feedback: AI can extract candidate terms, question structures, and generate parallel tasks, but may fabricate summaries, quotes, context, and authorial intent. Keep your first reading first, and then request to locate the original text.

10. Do delayed retention and migration: · Date · What to remove · Changed conditions · Output · Results · · Day 1 · No full translation or AI summary · Main material · First reading and five-sentence reconstruction · · · Days 3-7 · Remove old notes and dictionaries · Parallel materials · Purpose, evidence, inference · · · Day 14 · Remove recent feedback · New topic or genre · Explanation, test, or decision memo · · · Day 30 · Close all prompts · Real document, report, or handover · Complete delivery · · ·

Ways to keep it after seven days:
Obstacles that reappeared after changing materials:
Whether to translate less word-for-word or rely on summaries:
Which post-read action is still unstable:
Only variables that will change in the next round:

11. Scoring and retention: 0-2 for each item: 0=not completed, 1=depending on prompts or unstable, 2=completed under current conditions. · Project · Day 1 · Day 7 · Day 14 · Reasoning for evidence · · Keep main line on first reading · · · · · · Able to distinguish claims, evidence, and inferences · · · · · · Able to locate obstacles and select actions · · · · · · Able to verify technical facts or source locations · · · · · · Able to reconstruct after closing tools · · · · · · Able to change materials, topics or genres and still deliver · · · · ·

items.title: Spoken Evidence Card: From Accent Anxiety to Verifiable Interaction

body:
# Speaking Evidence — YYYY-MM-DD

Real scene:
Tasks: Description / Q&A / Fix / Collaborate / Migrate
Audiences and relationships:
What the other party needs to know or do after it’s over:
Time limit:
Allow outlines/re-recordings/subtitles/dictionaries/AI:
Recording and Uploading License:
Content that must remain private:
1. Define the task, audience, and boundaries: Completion criteria should be written as audience outcomes, such as "can retell risks and next steps," rather than just "speak fluently."

Current reference variant or audio source:
Reason for selection:
Differences that simply need to be recognized, not forced to imitate:
Other English variants added this round:

Equipment/Microphone:
Network/Room Noise:
Recording or call platform:
Are listeners familiar with the subject matter and my accent:
2. Record reference variations and technical conditions: When equipment, network, and audience familiarity change, do not interpret all differences in scores as changes in ability.

3. Save three types of unscripted baselines: · Sample · Conditions · Recording location · First breakpoint · Task completed or not · 90-120 second monologue · Unscripted account of real experience/problem · · · · · Five rounds of Q&A · At least one unfamiliar follow-up · · · · · One interactive fix · Request for repetition, confirmation of scope, restatement or summary · · · ·

The gist of a sentence I want to convey:

Key Figures/Time/Responsibilities/Conditions:
What I’m most worried about being misunderstood:
Don’t cut out pauses, reduce noise, or let AI generate the manuscript first. The first version should show what can be accomplished when the scaffolding is removed.

4. Save what the listener actually heard: Ask the listener to listen to the recording first without looking at the transcription: · Audience/Conditions · Gist of the retelling · Details of the retelling · Guess/relisten position · Next reaction · · Listener A · · · · · · Listener B or new device · · · · ·

Where the accent is obvious but still understood:
Where the meaning is really lost:
Understand areas that require extra effort but are not misunderstood:

A subjective evaluation is not a conclusion. Prioritize saving what the other party heard and what they need to do, rather than "does it sound like a standard accent?"

5. If the difference only shows that the reference variant, region or individual voice is different, and does not increase the cost of understanding, then record it without forcibly modifying it.

Five replaceable word chunks in this round:
1.
2.
3.
4.
5.

Theme variations:
Position variations:
Listener variant:
Stranger asked:
Unscripted answer position:

6. From word chunks to unfamiliar questioning: If you can only fluency in the memorized manuscript and cannot continue after changing conditions, reduce the number of complete sentence recitations and increase keyword reconstruction and questioning.

7. Record interactive repair: · Breakpoints · How do I find · Repair actions · The other party’s response · How to confirm and restore common understanding · · Didn’t hear clearly / Unclear scope / Need to think / Expression failure / Consensus is unstable · · · · ·

Sentences that I actively requested to repeat or confirm:
What I used instead:
My final conclusion:
If the repair fails, only what should be changed next time:
Repair is not a deduction item. Training is needed if the misunderstanding is not discovered, or if the task cannot be resumed after discovery.

Feedbacker/Tools/Model version and date:
Does it use the original audio or a transcription:

Issues it judges to be high impact:
Does it differentiate between accent differences, comprehension errors, comprehension effort, grammar, register and style:
How do I review using dictionary audio, a teacher, or a real audience:
What I accepted/rejected and why:

9. 3. Three stage thresholds: · Stage · Date · Questions that must be answered · Evidence to move to the next stage · · Calibration · Days 1–14 · What exactly am I practicing and what is the biggest bottleneck? · One baseline, three error categories, one stabilization period · · Stacking · Days 15–56 · Which action becomes stable under what conditions? · At least four comparable outputs and one external feedback · · Delivery · Day 57–90 · Will it still work for new audiences, topics, or real users? · Independent version, revised version and real delivery version · If there is no evidence for the threshold, do not automatically upgrade the difficulty; first narrow the task or fix the prerequisite knowledge.

4. Key judgments should go back to the work, recordings, reader/user feedback, and performance under new conditions; when a complete comparison of four time points is required, use the chain of evidence template.

1. Tasks and responsibilities: Change "learn AI" and "make an intelligent assistant" into observable actions, such as "users can import a file within 10 minutes and see a report that explains the source and errors."

2. Input, source and data boundaries: · Input/claim · Type · Source, version and location · Availability to model · Verifier · Failure conditions · · · Facts / Inference / Personal experience / User data / Third-party content · · Public / Masked / Organization approved / Prohibited · · ·

Final deliverables:

Output and evaluation sets: Build a small but realistic evaluation set, don’t just use the examples that the model does best: · Sample · Input conditions · Expected results · Unacceptable results · Measured results · Evidence locations · · Normal samples · · · · · · · Boundary samples · · · · · · · Missing/conflicting inputs · · · · · · · Real historical samples (desensitized) · · · · · · Acceptance must answer at least: whether the facts are traceable, whether the key actions are completed, whether the errors are visible, whether the permissions are correct, and whether the failure can be stopped. Being smooth, fast, or "human-like" is not an acceptance criterion.

AI can do: Questions / Classification / Candidate explanations / Counterexamples / Transcription / Draft / Test suggestions

Let the model rehearse goals, inputs, constraints, unknowns, and acceptance before starting generation. Tip word versioning; don't treat one chat window as the only project record.

5. Artificial gate: · Gate · Who must confirm · Passed evidence · When failed · · Source gate · · Original link, version, location · Mark not verified, not disseminated · · Fact gate · · Sampling verification, data caliber · Deletion or downgrade claim · · Privacy/permission gate · · Data scope, consent, access log · Stop processing and desensitization · · Quality gate · · Evaluation set, boundary sample, real feedback · Fix, reduce or reject delivery · · Cost gate · · Token, time, manual rework and budget · Downgrade model or stop · · Tool authorization gate · · Tool scope, call record, named authorization and withdrawal method · Prohibit calls or return to manual · · Responsibility gate · · Named approval and disclosure text · No release, no automatic execution · Critical decisions cannot be approved solely by generative models, automated scoring, or by individual developers themselves. 6. Cost, retention, and reversibility: If a cheap call results in a privacy incident, wrong decision, or a lot of rework, the true cost is not cheap. Document labor time, reviews, failures, reruns, and communication costs in addition to model fees.

7. Failure, pause and rollback: · Trigger condition · Immediate action · Notify · Restore/rollback location · · Source or version not found · Stop propagation, return to original material · · · · Hard door failure of evaluation set · Disable publication or automatic execution · · · · Input crosses permission boundary · Stop uploading, revoke access · · · Cost/delay exceeds upper limit · Degrade, limit or stop · · · · Real users report harm · Offline, retain evidence, escalate processing · · · If there is no clear stopper, notification path, and known working version, you are not ready to plug into the real process.

9. Check before starting: [ ] The real audience, action, deadline and person in charge have been written clearly; [ ] The input fields, sensitivity level, consent, copyright and retention boundaries have been confirmed; [ ] Key sources, versions and invalidation conditions can be traced; [ ] Normal, boundary, conflict and historical desensitization samples have been entered into the evaluation set; [ ] The scope of what AI can and cannot do has been clearly written; [ ] Long task checkpoints, retry/repeat safety rules, browser input boundaries and network exits are documented where applicable; [ ] Manual gates, fee caps, stop conditions and rollback locations are specified; [ ] Handover, disclosure and next review dates are determined.

Pilot Deliverables/Explicit Exclusions:

[Fill in after the experiment]

Basis for decision:

Copy blank cards: You don’t have to write a long text for each box. The evidence summary could be written as "User A shows de-identified examples of two tasks last week" instead of posting the full customer material into a public repository. Collection records retain only anonymized summaries required for verification, with private contact details and transaction credentials remaining in appropriate restricted locations.

Fill in the example: Product data collection pilot: This example only tests "whether small store operators are willing to pay for data collection within a limited range and can deliver it within limited working hours." It is not an AI product release plan. All characters, actions and figures are fictitious representations. · Fields · Sample filling · · Period and person in charge · Two weeks, recorded and decided by the person in charge of the pilot · · Users and tasks · Small store operators who maintain product information by themselves and have updated at least two batches of data in the past two weeks · · Role · The operator himself uses, decides and pays; only this case is included · · Current method · Use existing forms to copy item by item, and then manually check the specifications · · Main assumptions · Someone is willing to pay 200 yuan, ask someone to organize up to 20 confirmed product information into a draft to be released · · Counter example · The existing template is fast enough, and the additional communication time for purchasing services is more · · Recruitment and bias · Invite 10 people, target interview 6 people; including acquaintances, the results cannot directly represent unfamiliar customers · · Pilot scope · Maximum 2 form; a draft and items to be confirmed, including modifications within the scope of the round; no publication, no new product facts · · Materials and descriptions · Only use the information confirmed by the operator; manual arrangement and tool-assisted methods are not disclosed without permission · · Acceptance · The agreed fields within 20 items are complete, the items to be confirmed are identifiable, and the customer confirms receipt after checking · · Investment limit · Full round of 12 hours, cash disbursement 100 Yuan; these numbers are only selected for this example · · Continuing conditions · At least 3 people in the 6 interviews have recent repeated tasks; at least 2 people paid 200 yuan, completed acceptance, and each order was communicated to...

Example results and interpretation: Assume that 10 people were actually invited, 8 responded, 6 completed interviews, and 4 of them demonstrated recent recurring tasks. The same quotation was issued to 3 people, 2 paid and accepted, and the other 1 refused because the existing template was sufficient. A total of 400 yuan was received, with no refund and a cash disbursement of 40 yuan, including a total of 11 hours of recruitment and delivery work. The working hours of two of the service providers are 1.5 and 3.5 hours, and the other work is 6 hours. The total is still 11 hours. The format of the second order materials was inconsistent, resulting in additional verification; the user's own preparation and review time also exceeded the old process. Although the payment and acceptance quantities meet the agreement, the single working hours conditions are not met, so the decision in this round is an adjustment. In the next round, only data that conforms to the input template will be received, the price and quantity upper limit will remain unchanged, and the working hours will be checked again. This choice is still a hypothesis to be tested and cannot be written as a solved problem first. This round supports "these two users accepted the paid pilot under these conditions" and does not prove regular repurchases, customer acquisition costs through unfamiliar channels or sustainable profits. 400 - 40 = 360 yuan. It only deducts the balance of the listed cash expenditures, and does not include 11 hours of labor and other costs; it cannot be written as earning 360 yuan. If only 2 people are interviewed in this round, it should be recorded that "the amount of evidence has not reached the predetermined amount, judgment is suspended" and explain whether it is recruitment difficulties or insufficient investment. Don’t lower the threshold to 2 people after reading the results and then claim to have met the standard. If you really need to change the plan, keep the original version, change time and reason, and use the new conditions for the next round.

Finally, write a conclusion that can be reviewed: Within two weeks, 12 hours, and the expenditure limit of 100 yuan, we observed and accepted 2 payments, but 1 order exceeded the upper limit of delivery hours. We will narrow down the acceptable material formats and do another round; we are not expanding the order volume at this time. When reporting in English is required: Two customers paid for and accepted the pilot, but one delivery exceeded our time limit. We will test a stricter input format before taking more orders. Repeat demand and sustainable costs remain unproven.

Learners need to explain in English the AI ​​note-organizing tool they are developing in team communication. Plan to consider both work and family arrangements.

#Continuous Action Plan – Project Introduction in English

Update date: 2026-09-19
This cycle: 2026-09-21 to 2026-10-18
Review date or conditions: every Sunday; review in advance when work arrangements change

## Objectives and Evidence
- Why it’s worth doing now: The next round of team communication should explain the purpose and limitations of the project.
- Only one result for this round: independently complete a 90-second introduction and answer two follow-up questions.
- Current baseline and sample positions: approximately 50 seconds of initial recording; examples/baseline.m4a.
- Completion criteria: The audience can retell the purpose, users and one limitation; they can answer both follow-up questions in their own words, and the unknown item clearly states that they don’t know.
- Clarify content that is not within the scope of this round: accent imitation, complete product roadshow, new feature development.

## Realistic budget
- Existing work, care and life responsibilities: There are family matters in the evening on weekdays, and the time is unstable.
- The available window and total duration of this round: 20 minutes each at lunch twice a week and 20 minutes once on weekends; a total of 240 minutes in four weeks.
- How much time is required for preparation, execution and feedback: 10 / 35 / 15 minutes per week.
- Maneuvering Window: Maximum of one 10-minute window per week, may not be available and does not count towards the base budget.
- No diversion of time or resources: no occupied family time, no need to stay up late to make up for absences.
- Conditions that need to be negotiated or are still uncertain: weekend recording windows need to be negotiated in advance; feedback partners are available.

## Action portal
- When lunch is over on Tuesday and Thursday and the lunch break is still available:
- Open notes/project-intro.md in your workstation:
- First things first: write down a point you want to explain today.
- The biggest obstacle and the only thing that has been changed this round: the data is scattered; only this outline is used.
- Contacts or reminders that must be kept: work duty and home emergency contacts.
- Save the next step before ending: unanswered questions and examples for next time.

## Three versions
| Version | Conditions of use | Specific actions and end conditions | What to save |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Minimal version | Only 5 minutes | Write three explanations and highlight an uncertain expression | Three sentences and one question |
| Standard version | 20 minutes | Revise the outline at noon; record, listen back and revise one place on the weekend | Outline or record and revise the record |
| Extended version | The week's task is completed and the maneuver window is available | Answer a follow-up question in different ways, 10 minutes to end | A question and answer record |

- Minimum version cannot replace the training or verification: actual speaking, real-time questioning and real audience feedback.
- Maximum single investment: 20 minutes; additional 10 minutes for extended version.
- Shrinking condition: Temporary work occupies one window and only retains one point.
- Suspension conditions: There is no available window this week, save the status for review next week.

## Interrupt recovery
- Location of state files and recent works: notes/learning-state.md; recordings/.
- How to retest when first recovering: Talk for 30 seconds without looking at the outline, compare to baseline and record gaps.
- The first limited task of recovery: explain a purpose clearly and end after saving the recording.
- Date or condition for next re-evaluation: next Sunday, or after work schedule confirmation.
- How to adjust scope or negotiate when deadlines are affected: Use a short introduction first and confirm with the team in advance; do not promise that all training has been completed.

## Record of this round
| Date | Planned Action | Actual Product and Location | Obstacles/Costs | Next Steps |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-22 | Writing purpose and user points | Three sentences in notes/project-intro.md | Only 5 minutes left after the temporary message, use the smallest version | Check one expression next time |
| 2026-09-26 | Weekend recording | recordings/week-1.m4a, 60 seconds | Failed to explain the limitations of the tool clearly and within the budget | Write a specific limitation first |

## Periodic review
- What happened compared to baseline (with evidence): The first week of recording contains purpose and user and has not yet been verified to be understood by the listener.
- What still cannot be explained or completed independently: tool limitations; two impromptu questions have not yet been practiced.
- Whether the schedule goes over budget or crowds out existing responsibilities: the first week was under budget, but the Tuesday window was only 5 minutes.
- Conditions for continuing: The goal is still needed, the window is available, and the recording or feedback shows concrete improvements.
- Conditions for changing the method: after investing, you are still just memorizing the outline, and adding explanations and feedback without reading the manuscript.
- Conditions for pausing or stopping: if the window disappears, it will be paused; if the team communication needs are cancelled, then the purpose will be re-evaluated.
- Decision and basis for this round: Continue to the next week and make up for the limitations first; the existing records are not enough to judge the effect of the four weeks.
- Only one thing will be changed in the next round: ask the feedback partner to repeat the limitations heard in one sentence; if the other party is not available, record the lack of feedback.

The first week of recording in this example shows incomplete results: the task has not yet been achieved, but the next step is clear. The final review still requires four weeks of evidence, and the plan itself cannot be used as proof of effectiveness.

Below is my ongoing action plan and actual record of this round. Check that time budgets don't conflict with each other, completion criteria are observable, and minimal builds aren't mistaken for full training. Point out evidence gaps and do not fill in unfinished tasks or feedback. Based on existing responsibilities, only one adjustment for the next round is recommended. If key facts are missing, please clearly indicate what I need to verify.

[Paste plans and records]
Let AI help organize, not create progress for you: Before accepting a suggestion, check the actual schedule, work, and people involved. Changing plans based on reality is part of this template.

## Scope

## Record case by case (copy this area separately for each version)

Copyable record: If the final qualified quantity is zero, write "uncalculated" as the cost of each qualified result, and retain the total expenditure that has occurred without replacing it with zero.

Filling in example: Public information comparison table: The following is a hypothetical case, consistent with the chapter example: each of the ten cases is run once, 8 cases are qualified for the first time in the current version A, and 9 cases are qualified in the candidate B for the first time; 10 cases each are qualified in the two versions after manual revision. · Fields · Example filling · · Changes in this round · Only the extraction prompt is modified, the materials are the same as the tools · · Required conditions · Key figures have sources; missing prices cannot be inferred · · Failure record B-07 · The original text does not provide a price; B is written as "free"; manually change it back to "not provided" · · Cost of A · Total working hours 120 minutes, valued at 60 yuan/hour, tool 6 Yuan; a total of 126 Yuan · · Cost of B · Total working hours 100 minutes, same valuation, tools 8 Yuan; total 108 Yuan · · Decision · Keep the current scope; B repair first, do not expand use · · Next step · Add price shortage, price expiration, price conflict cases, and rerun previously qualified cases · · Evidence limitations · Small samples and one case per case; online error rates cannot be inferred; correct after revision does not mean independent reliability · Keep actual results in a reviewable file. When recording "completed," attach documentation, test output, or system status, not just a statement of completion for the model.

From documentation to action: Fix only one major bug pattern in a round, and check old cases for regression. items.title: Instructions on data, citation and verification
items.core: Explains how the "Advanced Life Guide" distinguishes research conclusions, personal experience and hypotheses to be tested, what cycle AI data is reviewed on, and how to cite this book in a standardized way.
body: Category three statements: Research conclusions come from published research, official guidelines, or normative documents. It describes results obtained using specific samples, materials, measurements and conditions and is not directly written as a guarantee to an individual. When citing in the book, the author, year, link and applicable boundaries will be retained; primary sources will be given where they can be verified, and marketing pages cannot be used instead. Personal experience only proves what the author has experienced. It can be part of the evidence, but not a rule: a failure cannot deduce that everyone should avoid the same path, and a recovery cannot deduce that the same approach will work for everyone. When reading a personal story, think of it as a scenario, not a prescription. The hypothesis to be tested is the author's or reader's inference about the future. It may be correct, or it may be disproven by the next experiment. The book will try its best to indicate the conditions of "if...then..."; for judgments that are not marked, you can treat them as assumptions first. When the three types of statements are mixed together, it is most likely to produce a paragraph that "sounds right but is ineffective when used". When reading, you can first ask: Which category does this sentence belong to?

Rules for review of AI materials: AI products, model capabilities, prices, packages, agreements, and supplier policies change quickly. This book is reviewed in stages according to the speed of change: 30 days: usage policy, safety notices, product features, regions and packages. The page will declare source_review_interval: 30. 60 days: Protocol specifications, implementation guidance, and rapidly changing workflows. 120 Days: Relatively stable concepts, research background, and historical facts. The rules are as follows: Give priority to quoting official documents, formal specifications or first-hand announcements, and do not use second-hand blogs instead; Record the verification date (sources_checked), which is separate from the text modification date (updated); The product entrance is only a "page that can be re-verified", not a current feature list, nor a guarantee of effectiveness; Pages that cannot be re-verified are marked as historical data and will not continue to be used as current evidence; Policies, prices and capabilities must be returned to the formal agreement, official page and actual acceptance. If you find that a product description is out of date, please report it by clicking on the next page.
How to cite this book: When citing, please indicate the title, author, edition, date and URL, and indicate that the text adopts CC BY-NC 4.0:
English version:

CITATION.cff in the root directory of the warehouse provides machine-readable citation information. This book has no DOI and no ISBN assigned; please do not add one yourself. When quoting a specific chapter, you can add the chapter title and page address to facilitate readers to return to the original text.

Report source error: If you find: The cited research conclusion is inconsistent with the original text; The link is invalid or points to another page; The product description is out of date; The Chinese version and the English version express the same fact inconsistently; Please submit through the question template and write down the page, original sentence, the source you think is correct, and the verification date. If personal information, unauthorized images or security issues are involved, do not post them publicly and report them through SECURITY.md’s private channels. The maintainer will first check the source before modifying the text; simply changing the date without checking the content does not count as completing the review.

Bibliography: See References for a list of sources organized by subject. It only includes materials actually cited in the book and is not exhaustive; papers and books are not distributed with the warehouse, and readers need to access them through DOI or official links.

items.title: English Proficiency Diagnosis|Find a starting point that can be retested
items.core: For self-learners who want to improve their English for work and daily life, first save an English baseline in five minutes, then complete a complete diagnosis of listening, speaking, reading and writing as needed, record obstacles and arrange a parallel task retest fourteen days later.
body: Who it’s suitable for: People who want to know where they are currently stuck in listening, speaking, reading, and writing. People who need English support for remote collaboration, interviews, technical documentation or customer communication. I have tried memorizing words or answering questions, but I cannot tell whether I have become a better learner in real work.

Leave a baseline for five minutes: This step only checks one ability, which is not equal to CEFR grading, nor is it equal to a complete diagnosis of listening, speaking, reading and writing. Choose a topic that you will actually use in the near future, set a five-minute timer, and complete one of the following: · Choice · Five-minute task · Saved evidence · · Listening · Listen to a 60–90 second piece of audio once · Write a main idea and a detail heard · · Reading · Read a paragraph of about 150–250 words of material · Write a claim and an evidence to support it · · Speaking · Write a 60-second explanation without reading the transcript · Save the original recording and mark a pause or unclear point · · Write · Write a real work or life message in five minutes · Save the original manuscript and circle an uncertain expression or fact · Don’t use AI to polish it yet. Write down specific stuck points, such as missing connections between words, finding no evidence, interruptions in expression, or the reader not knowing the next step. Save the sample privately, choose a stuck point to practice, and retest on a similar topic after fourteen days.

Complete diagnosis: When you need to determine where the listening, speaking, reading and writing are stuck, do a complete diagnosis. It's significantly longer than five minutes: the template suggests listening to 2–4 minutes of audio, reading 600–1000 words, recording 2 minutes of speaking, and 20 minutes to complete writing, before comparing conditions, errors, and transfer performance. Copy the English Proficiency Diagnostic Worksheet and do not use single item samples to infer overall grades.

Three steps to continue: first read the CEFR objectives and self-assessment, and choose a real topic that will be used in the near future. To continue with a complete diagnosis, save the four first-version samples with the English Proficiency Diagnosis and view the Listening Evidence Card, Speaking Evidence Card, Reading Evidence Card, or Writing Evidence Card as needed. Record a minimum obstacle, practice for fourteen days, and retest on different materials or different conversation partners; put visible changes into the evidence chain template.

Next step: Don’t turn diagnosis into an exam. Save a sample without AI, then use AI to explain errors, generate exercises or simulate conversations, and then you confirm meaning and transferability. After completing the first round of diagnosis, you can enter the recent updates or AI learning workflow portal.

items.title: AI learning workflow｜From prompt words to reliable delivery
items.core: For self-learners who want to use AI in real learning and work, use task briefings, source records, acceptance criteria and manual review to establish a repeatable workflow, and retain evidence of failure and rollback.
body: Specific problems you want to solve: AI answers smoothly, but the original source cannot be found or cannot be reproduced; After a long task is interrupted, you don’t know where to continue, and retry may result in repeated writing; Web pages, screenshots, and tool return values ​​carry operating instructions, which exceeds the original permissions; After changing models, data, or tools, it is impossible to explain whether the old "passed" result is still valid.

Who it’s suitable for: People who want to put AI into learning, writing, development, research, or customer delivery. People who are worried about illusions, privacy, cost and over-reliance, but still need to increase the speed of delivery. People who want to turn an effective conversation into a process that the team can reuse.

Three steps to get started: Use AI mission briefing to write down goals, inputs, constraints and final responsibilities; read again Use AI to learn everything and understand collaboration boundaries. Choose a small task and save original inputs, sources, model outputs, and manual modifications; design repeatable steps with AI workflows. By AI Measurement Records and AI Measurement and Reliability Acceptance Facts, Coverage, Risks, Costs, and Rollback Methods.

An example of a checkable result: After completing a public data comparison task, you should be able to hand over a draft with source locations, a manual verification record, and a recoverable status file. If a browser or external tool is used for the task, the network domain name, authorizer, checkpoint, final environment status, and unresolved issues must also be pointed out; the operation instructions on the page cannot automatically become authorization.
Worksheets that can be downloaded directly: AI task briefing (Markdown) AI evaluation record (Markdown) AI learning record (Markdown) AI trend experiment card (Markdown)

FAQ: With the prompt word template, can it be executed automatically? Can't. The template should first fix the tasks, sources, permissions, manual gates and rollback positions; whether to automatically execute it depends on the real case and the final status. What is the first thing to record in a long task? Document unique run numbers, checkpoints, timeouts and retry limits, duplicate security identifiers, network exits, and manual takeover points before discussing the model or framework. Can MCP complete a security clearance for me? cannot. It standardizes connectivity, but servers, proxies, credentials, networks, and write scopes still need to be reviewed on a case-by-case basis. Start with minimal experiments with AI workflows.

Next step: Let AI speed up the preparatory work before judgment, and let people retain the right to target, source, privacy and final signature. After completing a reviewable task, use the AI ​​Project Scorecard to determine whether it's worth moving to the next effort, and then return to Recent Updates.

items.title: Real projects, job hunting and entrepreneurship | Turn learning into evidence
items.core: Aimed at self-learners who are preparing for job hunting, remote collaboration or verifying entrepreneurial ideas, starting from specific positions, user problems and deliverables, use two weeks of experiments to determine the next step, rather than pile up courses and plans first.
body: Who it’s suitable for: People who want to turn their learning results into works, cases, interview evidence or the first users. People who need English to participate in multinational teams, communicate with customers or apply for jobs remotely. People who want to test entrepreneurial hypotheses at low cost and can accept rejection by users.

Three steps to get started: Start with Practice Roadmap: Start with a Problem Choose a real problem and use Briefing and Delivery Cards to define users, deliverables, and completion criteria. When applying for a job, refer to Job Search English and Remote Collaboration and Job Search English Evidence Card to convert the job description into demonstrable evidence. When starting a business, use From Questions to First Users for interviews, and then use Startup Experiment Cards to record assumptions, costs, feedback, and stopping conditions.

Next step: Don’t just ask “Did I learn it?” after two weeks. Check that the work is being used by real people, that interview responses are more specific, that users are willing to continue the conversation, and that the cost is affordable. Put the results into AI Development and Resource Layer Entrepreneurship or Recent Updates and continue to the next round.

items.title: Advanced Guide to Life｜Failure, recovery and re-learning of an ordinary person
items.core: "Advanced Guide to Life" bilingual open manuscript in Chinese and English: focusing on troughs and recovery, starting from English, AI and real projects, using repeatable actions to leave changes to time.
body: Who is this book suitable for: People who want to start over, but don’t know which page to start from; Self-learners who need to complete real tasks in English, rather than just want a test guide; People who are using AI to do real work, but don’t want to hand over their judgment, sources, and privacy; People who have experienced failure, interruption, or long-term slumps and want to catch themselves first; Parents and teachers who want to accompany their children to learn, but don’t want to impose adult rhythms on them. If you're looking for a quick formula, a complete English course, or clinical treatment advice, this book may not be the best place to start. Complete judgments and boundaries are written on who this book is suitable for and who it is not suitable for.

How to unfold the manuscript: The whole book unfolds according to a round-trip route: first catch yourself, then learn again, then borrow tools to amplify your abilities, and finally leave the changes to time. · Part · What is this part asking · Representing the entrance · · Prologue and how to read · Where do I enter, and why am I willing to start over? · Prologue · How to read this book · · Part 1: Put yourself back into life · Failure, body, relationship, career and choice, how to put yourself back into the same life? · Introduction to this part · My story · · Part 2: Re-learning, opening up input · How to use English as a specific training ground to re-establish learning ability? · Introduction to this part · CEFR self-assessment · · Part 3: Use tools to amplify capabilities · How to use AI without outsourcing attention and judgment? · Use AI to learn everything · Evidence · · Part 4: Practice and Recovery · How to bring learning back to the body, family and daily life? · Introduction to this part · First week of practice · · Part 5: Action and long-term change · How to bring a round of practice into a real project and let it still have echoes ninety days later? · Introduction to this part · Ninety Days of Action · · Part 6 and Postscript · How to understand, treat yourself well, improve yourself, and get along with yourself for a long time? · Make lifelong friends with yourself · Postscript · When the terminology is unclear, you can check the terminology and method index; if you want to go directly to a question, open the reading map; for the structure of the book and the three reading paths, see the road map of this book.

Bring a page of text back to today: Lifelong learning is not about opening ten courses at the same time, but making a page of text become a small reality today: Write down the problem at hand. In the learning state, note down what you already know, what is missing, and what is considered complete; if the question is about life capacity, relationships, or recovery, you can also use the Life Advancement Worksheet. Complete an action that can be seen. Let the AI ​​do the tearing for you, but check the sources yourself, make the choices, and leave notes, code, recordings, emails, feedback, or other real output, not just chat transcripts. Come back and see if it really takes away anything. Retest according to the training cycle of the chapter, and then use the weekly review or the ninety-day action list to judge whether the next step is worth continuing. If you find errors, translation differences or reproducible practical results, you are welcome to tell us through the Issue template; if this guide has helped you accomplish a real thing, you are also welcome to Star this repository so that more learners can find it.

Written to those who are still on the road: to young people You don’t have to be in your twenties to find a direction that is always right. Many directions do not appear after thinking clearly, but slowly emerge from the fog after doing several small projects, seeing several kinds of work, and bearing the results several times. More reliable than picking the perfect track is retaining the ability to learn, deliver and turn. If career anxiety keeps you collecting courses, certificates, and success stories, you might as well switch to a small project that can be completed in two weeks: solve a problem of someone around you, make a working tool, write an article with a source, or improve a process for real users. A project can fail, but it will tell you what you like, what's missing, whether it can be delivered, and whether others will want to use it again. For those who are going through rock bottom. Losing your job, failing a business, ending a relationship, damaging your health, and prolonged periods of confusion can all really sap your energy. Lows are not a test that must be won immediately. What you can do today may be to get a relatively complete night's sleep, eat a meal, go outdoors, or say "I need help now" to a trusted person. These things make sense on their own, without having to package them into a growth report first. Pausing is not giving up, asking for help is not weakness, and recalibrating is not backsliding. Wait until your strength comes back before deciding whether to increase the weight. The personal stories here are not medical or psychotherapeutic advice; if depression, insomnia, hopelessness, or dangerous thoughts persist, please contact trusted relatives and friends and seek local qualified medical or psychological professional support. Ensure safety first, then talk about growth.

Author and real practice: My name is Han Xiankai. The project started with the Outrageous English Learning Guide in 2017 and has since moved into learning, development, corporate services, entrepreneurial validation, and real life. The methods in the book will be put to the test in these scenarios, but the identity, business relationships, capabilities and income results are all written clearly, and only the evidence left by the work, users, cost and time will be accepted. Only when the method enters life can you know whether you can stand it. Relationships end and start over; jobs change, and learning takes on new meaning through encounters with real people. The participating products, company visits and real-life projects are unified into the author's projects and real-life practices. The page will indicate the author's association, purpose, update time and non-sponsored relationship. Third-party entries are concentrated in the resource directory, where it is stated that they are only optional resources and do not mean that the book or the author endorses their safety, quality, and compliance.

Read, download and co-revise: This project is an open content project, not open source software in the OSI sense: the text and author content adopt CC BY-NC 4.0, and the site configuration, inspection scripts and build code adopt MIT. See license description for details. The sources and authorization status of quotes, images, and third-party materials are recorded in Third-Party Materials and Citations; see the Appendix References for complete references. Please read the Contribution Guidelines, Chinese Contribution Guidelines and Code of Conduct before contributing. The verification dates of product and service entries are based on records on their respective pages and third-party materials and references; product capabilities, availability, and compliance scope are still based on official pages, formal agreements, and actual acceptance. Read online: GitHub Pages · GitHub Repository · English version: Still Here: A Field Guide to Beginning Again. If you only do one thing today, create a learning status and write down the problem you are facing, the clues you have at hand, and the next smallest task. Don't wait for the road to become wider before setting off; many roads only appear after your feet have set down.

items.title: Practice roadmap: Entrepreneurship, self-discipline and AI
items.core: Choose English, AI, entrepreneurship or self-discipline paths according to the current problem, and use four weeks of minimal practice to leave works, feedback and next decisions.
body: Choose a path based on your current problem: · Your current status · Where to read · What to leave this week · · Want to use AI to learn a new skill · Use AI to learn everything → AI workflow · An independently completed work and error record · · Have used AI, but don’t know whether the results are reliable · AI evaluation and reliability → Evaluation record · A small sample set and a well-founded version comparison · · Have a startup idea, but have not yet contacted customers · From problem to first users → Startup experiment card · Real interview records and evidence to support and oppose the hypothesis · · Someone is willing to use it, but is busy but not making money · Sustainable small business · A delivery account including communication, rework and support hours · · Difficulty in starting, or wanting to start again after interruption · Self-discipline and persistence in practice → Continuous action plan · A clear trigger condition, an action after narrowing the scope and verifiable output · · English hinders reading or communication · CEFR objectives and self-assessment → English diagnosis · A recording or a short article, mark the item that needs practice most · The output in the table is only a starting suggestion, not a unified assessment for everyone. When caregiving, shifts, or ad-hoc tasks take up time, reduce the number of tasks and maintain a clear standard for completion.

A four-week practice path: This is an adaptable arrangement with no commitment to four weeks of earning money or mastering a skill. Schedule two 25-minute tasks and one 10-minute review each week, or break the week into longer periods. Week 1: Establish a starting point. Fill in the learning status and write only one question. Save your current performance once: Don’t use the AI ​​to write an explanation, record how long an existing process took, or ask a user about their last difficulty. If you only get "someone should need it", the starting point is still an assumption. Week 2: Make a minimal version. Choose an output that can be demonstrated on the spot. Learning English can complete a real-purpose email; starting a business can manually deliver a small service; AI projects can compile a summary of information with sources. When AI collaboration is required, use the AI ​​mission briefing to fix the input, boundaries, and acceptance criteria; when verifying entrepreneurial ideas, use the entrepreneurial experiment card to first write down the assumptions and stopping conditions, and complete a closed loop first. Week 3: Let reality give feedback. Give the output to real users, or retest independently on new materials. Document what the other person did and where they got stuck, not just “fine.” AI projects include cases of missing information, conflict sources, tool failures, etc.; entrepreneurial experiments record non-responses, rejections, and no reasons for repurchase. Week 4: Decide What to Keep Use the Weekly Review to compare starting points with current evidence. Choose to continue, reduce, change approach, or stop, and write down your decision and reasons. Leave only the one most valuable thing for the next round. Being willing to stop a solution that is disproven is also progress.
All topics share a set of evidence: just create a local folder, there is no need to build a complex knowledge base first:

Save the minimum material that is useful to you; obtain permission first for information involving others and remove unnecessary identity details. When sharing your work publicly, do not disclose customer materials, chat history, or keys. To judge whether the record is useful, just ask two questions: Can you continue doing it tomorrow? Can you explain why you decided this way after a month?

Template toolbox: · Purpose · Template · · Determine the current baseline · Learning status, English diagnosis · · Collaboration with AI · Task briefing, learning records, evaluation records · · Verification of entrepreneurial ideas · Entrepreneurship experiment card, AI project score card · · Continuous action and review · Rhythm ledger, continuous action plan, weekly review, AI experience case review · The rhythm ledger arranges the volume and rhythm of the week; the continuous action plan details an action experiment. Templates can be deleted. If filling out a form takes longer than actually taking action, keep only the three items of "what to do, complete the evidence, and next step."

How to view the content in the guide: Methods chapters provide processes that can be tried and tested; author stories record experiences in specific situations; external research and product information should be continuously verified along with the source. The example numbers, two-week periods, and sample sizes in this article, unless explicitly stated, are design examples to help get started and do not represent scientific thresholds or operational guarantees. If you want to know the background, you can read Entrepreneurship and My Story. When action is needed, return to the chosen path and complete the first piece of work.
